kept.title: Photo fit ignores the stage chip and the zoom bar: the bar covers the photo's bottom and the chip covers its corner
kept.where: Editor canvas (stage), 1280x800 (also 1440 once the tip is dismissed)
kept.evidence: editor-visual/j-kitchen-1280.png: the frame is at y 88–637 and the Canvas toolbar at y 607–653, so the bar hides the bottom 30px of the photo, including the floor. The stage chip 'V1 · Scandinavian' (x16–142, y72–100) sits over the photo's top-left corner (the photo starts at x44, y88). At 1440 the bar only just touches the photo (a-1440.png: frame bottom 831, toolbar top 831). stage.tsx fits with a flat `pad = 32` on every side.
kept.repro: Open /visualizer/b46000d1-1638-4c7c-af20-bebbcc3b9744 at 1280x800, press Got it, open Kitchen, then V1.
kept.fix: In stage.tsx, fit into the box left after the overlays, with padTop = chip 28 + 16 + 12 and padBottom = toolbar 46 + 16 + 16 (≈78). Compute fw from (areaSize.h - padTop - padBottom) and offset the viewport by (padTop - padBottom)/2. Alternatively, anchor the chip to the frame's own top-left corner (inside the photo, 12px in) rather than the area's.

verdict.reason: Reproduced in both the code and the screenshot. stage.tsx fits the photo with a flat `pad = 32` on every side (lines 64–65): `fw = min(areaSize.w - 64, (areaSize.h - 64) * aspect)`. Two overlays are absolutely positioned inside the same `.area` and take no space from that fit. The `.chip` sits at top/left 16px (stage.module.css:13) and the Canvas `.toolbar` at bottom 16px, about 46px tall (stage.module.css:51). So whenever height decides the fit, the photo's bottom edge is at 32px and the bar reaches up to about 62px. The bar then covers roughly 30px of photo, and the chip, spanning y 16–44, overlaps the photo's top-left corner (photo top = 32). In j-kitchen-1280.png the zoom bar hides the floor strip (a floor marker at y≈581 sits just above it, so a marker placed lower would be hidden), and the "V1 · Scandinavian" pill overlaps the photo's top-left corner. The house precedent disagrees with the stage: the file viewer this bar is taken from keeps the zoom bar's band clear of the image (`.canvas` padding 100/120 on desktop and `spacing-20` bottom on tablet; the phone comment reads "the compact zoom bar's band (22 + 60 + 8) kept clear of the image"). The overlap is what a studio sees in a live demo at the common 1280 laptop size. It is also visible at 1440 once the tip is gone, where the bar just touches the photo.
verdict.fix:
In components/visualizer/editor/stage.tsx, replace the flat pad with padding that follows the overlays, as the file viewer does:
- `padX = 32`
- `padTop = chip ? 16 + 28 + 12 : 32` (chip top + chip height + gap = 56)
- `padBottom = toolbarShown ? 16 + 46 + 12 : 32` (≈74)

Compute `fw = max(0, min(areaSize.w - 2*padX, (areaSize.h - padTop - padBottom) * aspect))`. Centre the frame in the leftover box: either give `.viewport` `margin-top: padTop - padBottom` via style, or add the offset to the translate as `translate(pan.x, pan.y + (padTop - padBottom)/2)` so pan and zoom stay intact. The toolbar is hidden while the tray is open (`.editor[data-tray]` in editor.module.css:38). Either pass a `toolbar` or `tray` flag into Stage, or keep the bottom band regardless, which is simpler and avoids a jump when the tray opens. At ≤767 the bar sits at spacing-3, so use 12 + 46 + 8 there. This takes the photo's height from the free space and does not move the house chip or bar, so no new UI is invented. Do not re-anchor the chip inside the photo: it would then cover the render the studio is showing off. Verify at 1025, 1280 and 1440 (photo bottom must be at or above the toolbar top minus 8, and the chip's bottom above the photo's top) and at 390 with touch.

kept.title: The versions strip never scrolls the version on screen, a new render or the in-flight tiles into view
kept.where: Versions strip, every width (most visible at 1025 and with 10+ versions)
kept.evidence: editor-visual/i-many-versions-1440.png: after five Generates (15 versions), V13 is on the canvas but the strip still shows Original…V6. Measured: the row's scrollLeft is 2 and the [data-on] tile is at x=1924 while the row spans x104–557. editor-visual/i-inflight3.png: the three 'Rendering…' tiles land at the end, and the third is cut off. editor-visual/a-1025.png: Kevin's V3, which is on screen, is clipped at the strip's edge on first load.
kept.repro: On a design, set Versions to 3 via Change and Generate a style 4–5 times; or open Kevin Ng's design at 1025x768.
kept.fix: Add a ref on the row and a useEffect keyed on viewKey and inFlight. When inFlight > 0, scroll the row to its end; otherwise call `row.querySelector('[data-on]')?.scrollIntoView({ inline: 'nearest', block: 'nearest', behavior: 'smooth' })`, with reduced motion falling back to 'auto'.

verdict.reason: versions-strip.tsx (73 lines) has no ref, no effect and no scroll call of any kind, and nothing else under components/visualizer calls scrollIntoView or sets scrollLeft. The `.row` is `overflow-x: auto` with 128px tiles, so once the versions are wider than the row, the tile that is on screen (`data-on`), a newly landed V(n) and the in-flight 'Rendering…' placeholders (added at the end) all stay wherever the row was last scrolled. On first load that is scrollLeft ≈ 0. This matches the auditor's measurements (the on-screen tile at x=1924 in a row spanning 104–557, and V3 clipped at 1025). A studio showing a client V13 while the strip shows V1–V6, or pressing Generate and seeing nothing appear, will notice this. I rate it major because the strip is the only way to see a render has landed.
verdict.fix:
In components/visualizer/editor/versions-strip.tsx, add `const rowRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)` on `.row` and a `useEffect` keyed on `[viewKey, inFlight, live.length]`. The effect only touches the DOM, so the react-hooks rules are satisfied.
- When `inFlight > 0`, call `row.scrollTo({ left: row.scrollWidth, behavior })`.
- Otherwise find `row.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-on]')`. If the tile sits outside `[row.scrollLeft, row.scrollLeft + row.clientWidth]`, call `row.scrollTo({ left: tile.offsetLeft - row.offsetLeft - pad, behavior })`, or align the tile's right edge when it overflows on the right.
- Set `behavior` to 'smooth', or 'auto' when `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches`.
- Use `row.scrollTo` rather than `el.scrollIntoView`. `scrollIntoView` also scrolls the page or the editor's fixed frame vertically on short viewports and at 1025, even with block:'nearest'.
- Because the effect depends only on those keys, a manual sideways scroll isn't fought on re-render.
- No new UI and no register entry are needed beyond a bug-fix REG line.
- To verify, open Kevin Ng's design at 1025×768 (V3 is fully visible), then do 5 Generates at 1440 (the new tile is in view and the in-flight tiles are visible).

kept.title: Picks made while a render runs are silently wiped when it finishes
kept.where: Rail + Generate footer during a Generate, 1440
kept.evidence: editor-visual/n-during-run.png: while 'Relighting…' ran, the rail stayed live. Walls → Cool Grey was picked and 'warmer rug' typed, and the rail showed YOUR CHANGES · 3. Once the render ended, the change count was 0 and the note was '' (probe s14 log `{ during: 3, after: 0, note: '' }`). The render only used the pending captured at start, and then `patch((p) => afterRender(p))` in generate() cleared everything, including the picks it never rendered. The footer also reads 'Rendering…' while the card says 'Relighting…', because it shows the new intent's busy word.
kept.repro: Pick a light, press Generate, then within 1s open Surfaces › Walls, pick Cool Grey and type a note. Wait for the render to finish.
kept.fix: Either make the rail and room chips `inert` while `running` (a quiet 'Rendering — your picks are kept' line), or keep a snapshot `const used = pending` at the start and after the render clear only what was used (`patch(p => p === used ? afterRender(p) : subtractUsed(p, used))`). Also carry the run's busy label in `running`, and show `running.title` on the footer button.

verdict.reason: The code path matches the finding. `generate()` in visualizer-editor.tsx (lines 150–180) passes the `pending` captured when the run starts to `runPass`. After the save it calls `patch((p) => afterRender(p))` on whatever is pending by then. `afterRender` (lib/visualizer/model.ts:96) resets materials, furniture, style, lighting, note and tool to `emptyPending()`. So any pick or note made during the 1.6–2.6 s run (plus the save) is dropped even though it was never rendered, and nothing tells the user. The rail and footer are not locked while `running`: rail.tsx has no inert or disabled state tied to it, and only the Generate button is disabled through `busy`. The label mismatch is also real. The footer shows `busy ? intent.busy : intent.label` from the live intent (rail.tsx:78 and :98), while the stage card shows `running.title`, which is fixed at start. A pick made mid-run changes the intent, so the footer can read "Rendering…" while the card says "Relighting…". A studio would lose a pick without warning, which counts as major.
verdict.fix:
Keep what the run used, and clear only that; don't lock the rail. Picking the next change while a render runs is a good flow worth keeping.
1) In lib/visualizer/model.ts, add a pure `afterRenderOf(p: Pending, used: Pending): Pending`. When `p === used`, return `afterRender(p)`. Otherwise start from `p` and drop only what was used: each `materials[id]` equal to `used.materials[id]`, each furniture pick deep-equal to the used one, `style` when it equals `used.style`, `lighting` when it is JSON-equal to `used.lighting`, `note` when it equals `used.note`, and `tool` when it equals `used.tool`. Keep quality, variants, transfer and empty/furnish/asPhoto as `afterRender` does now.
2) In visualizer-editor.tsx, add `const used = pending` at the top of `generate()` and pass `used` to `runPass` and `saveRender`. Replace `patch((p) => afterRender(p))` with `patch((p) => afterRenderOf(p, used))`.
3) In rail.tsx, change `GenerateFooter` to take `busyLabel: string | null` in place of the boolean `busy`, or alongside it. In visualizer-editor.tsx pass `busyLabel={running?.title ?? null}`, so the button shows the run's own word and matches the stage card. If picks survived the run, the existing "V{n} is ready" snackbar can add ", your newer picks are kept", which is optional invented copy and should be logged as a REG.
Verify with a Playwright probe: pick a light, press Generate, then within 1 s pick Walls › Cool Grey and type a note. After the run, expect YOUR CHANGES · 2 (walls + note) and the footer label matching the card during the run.

kept.title: With many rooms, the active room's chip is off-screen, and at 1025 the room rail shrinks to one truncated chip
kept.evidence: editor-visual/g-many-rooms-1440.png: after adding the 8th room, the canvas shows its Kitchen photo but no chip in view is highlighted, and the active chip sits past the scroll arrow. editor-visual/h-rooms-1025.png: with 8 rooms the chip rail is about 150px wide and shows only 'Master bedro' between two arrows. On reload the editor always opens the first room, because the room is not kept in the URL.
kept.repro: Create a Blank design, add 8 sample rooms via Add room, and look at the top bar. Resize to 1025x768.
kept.fix: Scroll the selected chip into view when the value changes (ChipRail). When the rooms overflow (or below 1280), turn Add room into the icon button the narrow layout already uses, and replace the chip rail with a 'Room: <name> ▾' trigger opening a PortalMenu of rooms plus Add room. Keep `?room=` in the URL via router.replace so reload and Back return to the same room.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed two of the three claims in code and in the auditor's screenshots.

1. **Active chip goes off-screen (confirmed).** `ChipRail` (`components/om/chip-rail.tsx`) only scrolls a chip into view from `onClickCapture`, so only when that chip is clicked. When Add room selects the new room, nothing scrolls the rail. `g-many-rooms-1440.png` shows the canvas on the new room's photo while the chips in view (Living room … Kitchen sketch) are all unselected, and the active chip sits past the `>` pager.

2. **Rail shrinks to one chip at 1025 (confirmed).** The topbar's `.rooms` block (`flex: 1`) shares the bar with the title, the ⋯ button, the full "Add room" button, undo/redo and the full "Share with client" button. At 1025 that leaves about 150px, and `h-rooms-1025.png` shows only "Master bedro" between two pagers. This is still above the narrow breakpoint (`TABLET_DOWN`, which switches to `compact`).

3. **Room not kept in the URL (refuted).** `visualizer-editor.tsx` around lines 526–532 writes `?room=` with `history.replaceState` whenever `roomId` changes. `app/(editor)/visualizer/[designId]/page.tsx` reads `sp.room` into `initialRoom`, so reload and shared links return to the same room.

On severity: eight rooms in one design is an edge case, and the room still shows on the canvas and in its title. That makes this minor, not major.
verdict.fix:
1. **Scroll the selected chip into view (`components/om/chip-rail.tsx`).** Add an optional `active?: string | null` prop. In a `useEffect` on it, find the selected chip with `rail.current?.querySelector('[data-selected]')` (Chips already sets `data-selected`) and call `scrollIntoView({ inline: 'nearest', block: 'nearest', behavior: 'smooth' })`. This is a fix in the shared piece, so every ChipRail with a value set from code gains it.

2. **Pass the room in (`components/visualizer/editor/topbar.tsx`).** Use `<ChipRail active={roomId} …>`.

3. **Give the rail room at 1025–1280 (`topbar.tsx` + `topbar.module.css`).** Turn Add room into the icon-only IconButton `add_photo_alternate` with a Tooltip "Add room", and turn Share into the IconButton `send` form that `compact` already uses. Drive both from a `useMediaQuery('(max-width: 1280px)')`, which matches the existing 1280 rule that hides `.saved`. Both forms already exist in the file, so no new UI is invented.

4. **Leave these out.** Don't add the "Room: <name> ▾" PortalMenu replacement; it is new UI beyond the stated intent. Don't add URL work; `?room=` is already kept via `replaceState`.

kept.title: A version tile's ⋯ is hidden under the favourite badge
kept.where: Versions strip tile (V2 with star, notes, pins, sent), 1440
kept.evidence: editor-visual/c-v2-hover-zoom.png (2x): on hover the kebab (x388–412) sits under the badge group (x397.6–510). The star covers the ⋮, so the only way into Save to Files, Add to a quote and Share is barely visible. Four badges take 112 of the tile's 128px.
kept.repro: Hover V2 in Kevin Ng › Living room.
kept.fix: Move the kebab to the top-right corner (a white 28px disc) and the badges to bottom-left inside the image. Cap them at two plus '+n'. Make the kebab hit area at least 28–32px (the template editor's 36px target rule).

verdict.reason:
The overlap is real, and I reproduced it on :3017 at 1440 in Kevin Ng › Living room. On V2 the ⋯ sits at x388–412 and the badge group starts at x397.6 and runs 112px wide. The cause is in versions-strip.module.css: `.kebab` is pinned top-left (`top:2px; left:2px`) and `.badges` top-right, with nothing stopping them colliding when a tile has four badges. My hover screenshot (verify/tile-2.png) matches the auditor's: only the left edge of the three dots shows beside the red star.

Two parts of the finding are off:
1. The menu is not unreachable. `elementFromPoint` at the kebab's centre still returns the "More options for V2" button, so a click there opens the menu. The problem is that you can hardly see it, not that you can't use it. Minor is the right severity.
2. The proposed fix puts the badges bottom-left, but the "Before" tag (`.beforeTag`) already sits there during a compare, so that would just move the collision.

Also, `IconButton` only comes in sizes 36 and 24, so a "28px disc" isn't a house size.

Tiles with fewer badges (V1, V3) have no overlap.
verdict.fix:
In versions-strip.module.css:
- Move `.kebab` to `top:2px; right:2px`, and keep its hover/focus reveal and the `(hover:none)` always-on rule.
- Keep `IconButton size={24}` with its white background (radius 4, or `--om-radius-full` for a disc). Enlarge its hit area to 32px with a transparent `::before` at `inset:-4px`, rather than inventing a 28 size.
- Move `.badges` to `bottom:var(--om-spacing-1); right:var(--om-spacing-1)`. Bottom-right, not bottom-left, so they never meet the Before tag at bottom-left.

In versions-strip.tsx:
- Show at most two badges, in the order favourite, notes, pins, sent.
- Put the rest into one `.badge` reading "+n", wrapped in a `Tooltip` that lists what it hides, e.g. "2 pins · Shared with the client". This reuses the existing Tooltip and badge styles.
- At ≤1024, where tiles are 96px wide, allow at most one badge plus "+n".

Check at 1440 and 1025 with a mouse, and 768 touch: hover V2, confirm the ⋯ is fully visible and its bounding box doesn't intersect `.badges`, and confirm "Before" and the badges don't overlap when V2 is the compare pair.

kept.title: The change count disagrees between 'Your changes · n' and the Generate label
kept.evidence: editor-visual/e-many-changes.png: YOUR CHANGES · 6 next to 'Generate · 9 changes'. editor-visual/e-describe-long.png: 7 next to 10. intentFor (lib/visualizer/model.ts:154) counts materials per surface id (Cabinets ×3, Countertops ×2), while the chips group them by surface.
kept.repro: Kitchen: give each of the six surface groups a finish.
kept.fix: Count surfaces by group (surfaceGroupFor) in intentFor, or have the editor pass `changes.length` into the label so both read the same number.

verdict.reason:
The mismatch is real, both in the code and in the screenshot. In e-many-changes.png the rail reads "YOUR CHANGES · 6" and the button right under it reads "Generate · 9 changes".

- **Chips:** the list in visualizer-editor.tsx (around lines 272–293) groups finishes by `groupWord(label)|materialId` and furniture by `normFurnitureKey(label)|action`. In the screenshot's Kitchen, Cabinets (3 surfaces) → Cool Grey is one chip and Countertops (2 surfaces) → Warm White is one chip.
- **Button:** `intentFor` in lib/visualizer/model.ts (around lines 149–154) counts `Object.keys(p.materials)` per visible surface id and furniture per piece id, so it counts every Cabinet and Countertop surface separately.

The same room gives 6 on the chips and 9 on the button, and this happens whenever a group with more than one surface takes one finish, which is the default for a group pick. A designer reading the two numbers side by side in a live demo will think three changes are hidden. It is a small copy fault that is easy to see, so minor fits.
verdict.fix:
Keep one counting rule so the chips and `intentFor` can't drift apart again.

In lib/visualizer/model.ts, change the `intentFor` options:
- Pass `visibleSurfaces` as a `Map<id, label>` instead of a Set.
- Pass `visibleFurniture` as a `Map<id, label>` instead of a Set.

Then count distinct keys the way the chips do:
- **Materials:** `new Set(entries.filter(visible).map(([id, mid]) => `${groupWord(label)}|${mid}`)).size`
- **Pieces:** distinct `${normFurnitureKey(label)}|${action}`, with 'keep' left out.

`groupWord` is already in model.ts; import `normFurnitureKey` from ./surfaces.

In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx (line 121), build those Maps from `reading.surfaces` and `reading.furniture`.

Leave the remaining terms as they are (+1 each for style, refs, light and note). They already match the chips one for one. The tool chip never reaches the "Generate · n changes" branch, because the empty and furnish paths return earlier.

A lighter alternative: pass the editor's `changes.length` into `intentFor` as `changeCount` and use it for the label, but that means computing the list before line 121. The shared-key approach keeps `intentFor` honest in any other place that calls it.

kept.title: The changes list cuts a row in half with no sign that it scrolls
kept.evidence: editor-visual/e-many-changes.png: under 'Backsplash → Mushroom' a 4px sliver of a fifth chip shows at y≈928, right above Generate. `.changeList { max-height: 112px; overflow-y: auto }` does not match a whole number of 28px rows plus 8px gaps.
kept.repro: Give 5+ surfaces a finish.
kept.fix: Set max-height to 100px (three rows) and add a bottom fade mask (`mask-image: linear-gradient(#000 80%, transparent)`), or show the first four chips plus a '+n more' chip that expands the list.

verdict.reason: The finding is real, and it is visible in the screenshot. In components/visualizer/editor/rail.module.css line 28, `.changeList` has `max-height: 112px; overflow-y: auto` and the chips are 28px high with an 8px gap (`--om-spacing-2`). Three rows take 28·3 + 8·2 = 100px, so the fourth row starts at 108px and only 4px of it shows. In e-many-changes.png, under "Backsplash → Mushroom", a 4px strip of the next chip's border sits right above the Generate button. macOS overlay scrollbars hide the track, so nothing tells the user the list scrolls and the strip looks like a clipping bug. The count confirms it: the header says "YOUR CHANGES · 6" but only four chips can be seen. The auditor's fixes need adjusting. A permanent `mask-image` fade on the scroller would also fade the last chip once the user has scrolled to the end. A "+n more" chip is new UI the task doesn't need. Also, on touch at ≤1024 the chips grow to `min-height: 36px` (line 47), so a fixed 100px only fits the 28px chips.
verdict.fix:
1. In components/visualizer/editor/rail.module.css, size the list so the next row shows by about half when it overflows, instead of a 4px strip. On desktop, set `.changeList { max-height: calc(3 * 28px + 3 * var(--om-spacing-2) + 14px); }` (122px). In the touch/phone media query at line 47, override it with `.changeList { max-height: calc(3 * 36px + 3 * var(--om-spacing-2) + 18px); }`. A half-cut chip reads as "there is more below".
2. Optionally, add a bottom fade that shows only while there is more below. In rail.tsx, put a ref and an onScroll handler on the `viz-changes` div, plus a ResizeObserver or a check whenever `changes` changes. The handler sets `data-more` when `scrollTop + clientHeight < scrollHeight - 1`. In CSS: `.changeList[data-more] { mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, #000 calc(100% - 16px), transparent); }`. Set the attribute from an event or observer, not during render and not by calling setState in an effect body, to stay within the house ESLint rules.
3. Keep the chips and the Clear all link as they are. No new "+n more" control is needed.

kept.title: The Maison AI FAB floats mid-canvas when there is no rail (blank or deleted design)
kept.evidence: editor-visual/f-empty-1440.png: the FAB sits at x1000, y940 in open canvas, 372px from the right edge, with no rail beside it. editor-visual/f-empty-1025.png: the FAB (x585–633, y684–732) overlaps the bottom edge of the 'Add the first room' card. editor.module.css `.fab { right: calc(var(--viz-rail) + 20px) }` applies whether or not the rail renders.
kept.repro: On /visualizer choose New ▾ › Blank design.
kept.fix: Set `data-rail` on .editor only when the aside renders, and scope the offset to `.editor[data-rail] .fab`. Otherwise keep the house FAB position (bottom-right).

verdict.reason:
This is real, and I found it in the code as well as the screenshot. In `components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx` (around line 655), the desktop `<aside className={styles.rail}>` only renders when `room && !readOnly`. A blank design has no room, and a deleted design is read-only. But `editor.module.css` line 29 applies `.fab { right: calc(var(--viz-rail) + 20px); bottom: 36px; }` every time, with `--viz-rail: 372px`. So without the rail, the FAB still sits 392px in from the right, in empty canvas.

In `f-empty-1025.png` the FAB overlaps the bottom edge of the centred "Add the first room" card. That is exactly where a new user is looking, and it reads as broken. At 1440 it floats alone in the middle of the canvas, away from every other page's position.

The narrow layout (`data-narrow`) already has its own override and is unaffected. The house default in `components/shell/maison-fab.module.css` is `.wrap { right: 24px; bottom: 24px }`. Severity is minor: nothing breaks, but it is visible on the very first screen of a new design.
verdict.fix:
1. In `visualizer-editor.tsx`, work out `const hasRail = !narrow && !!room && !readOnly`. Set `data-rail={hasRail || undefined}` on the `.editor` root (line 619), next to `data-narrow` and `data-tray`.
2. In `editor.module.css`, change line 29 to `.editor[data-rail] .fab { right: calc(var(--viz-rail) + 20px); bottom: 36px; }`. The FAB then falls back to the house `MaisonFab` position (right 24, bottom 24) when there is no rail. Keep the `[data-narrow]` and `[data-tray]` rules as they are; `hasRail` is false whenever `narrow` is true, so they don't conflict.
3. Check with Playwright at 1440 and 1025: a blank design (New ▾ › Blank design), a deleted design, and a design with a room. In the last case the FAB must still clear the rail, byte-identical to before. No REG entry is needed beyond a bug-fix line.

kept.title: The photo opens at the fallback 3:2 frame, with grey bars and offset markers until the next switch
kept.evidence: editor-visual/d-frame-edge.png (2x) shows a 3px grey band on the photo's left edge. Probe s4 log: on load the frame is 1004×669 (the 1.5 default) while the image's natural size is 900×603 (1.4925). After any version switch the frame becomes 1004×672.7, so the canvas jumps. The motion.img onLoad never fires for an image that finished loading before hydration, so `natural` stays null.
kept.repro: Load /visualizer/b46000d1-1638-4c7c-af20-bebbcc3b9744 fresh and inspect the photo's left edge, then click V1.
kept.fix: Add a ref callback on the photo, `el => { if (el?.complete && el.naturalWidth) setNatural({ w: el.naturalWidth, h: el.naturalHeight }) }`, or check `complete` in an effect keyed on image.

verdict.reason: The bug is real, but it's smaller than a minor. On :3011 at 1440 I did two fresh loads of /visualizer/b46000d1-…. Both times the frame measured 1004×669.3, the 1.5 fallback, while the image's natural size was 900×603 (ratio 1.4925), so `natural` never got set on the first load. The cause is in stage.tsx. `natural` starts null (line 53), `aspect` falls back to 1.5 (line 63), and the only thing that sets it is the motion.img's onLoad (line 117). That event has already fired before hydration for an image that came with the server HTML and was cached, so it never reaches React. The photo uses `object-fit: contain` (stage.module.css:9), so it draws at about 998.8px wide inside the 1004px frame. That leaves roughly 2.6px of surface-variant on each side, split into two bands, not one 3px band on the left. The markers are positioned in % of the frame, so they sit about 0.25% off the photo, which is invisible at marker size. There is also a second trigger the auditor missed: every image change calls `setNatural(null)` during render (line 57). So each version switch goes back to 1.5 until the new image loads, and the frame jumps twice. On a cached switch the load is quick, but it still reflows. A studio would at most notice a hairline and a small jump, so this is polish, not minor.
verdict.fix:
In components/visualizer/editor/stage.tsx, make `natural` pick up images that are already decoded, and stop resetting the frame to 1.5 on every switch:
1) Put one callback on the motion.img, `const readNatural = (el: HTMLImageElement | null) => { if (el?.complete && el.naturalWidth) setNatural((n) => n && n.w === el.naturalWidth && n.h === el.naturalHeight ? n : { w: el.naturalWidth, h: el.naturalHeight }) }`. Use it as both `ref={readNatural}` and `onLoad={(e) => readNatural(e.currentTarget)}`. The equality guard stops extra renders, and a ref callback is allowed under the react-hooks lint rules because it isn't a ref read during render.
2) Delete `setNatural(null)` from the render-phase adjust at line 57 so the previous version's aspect stays until the new image reports its own. Every version of the same room has the same size, so the frame then stays still across switches. Keep the `img` state only if something else uses it; otherwise drop it.
To verify, load fresh at 1440: the frame should be 1004×672.7 straight away, with no grey on the photo's edges, and switching to V1 shouldn't change the frame's size.

kept.title: Markers and pins grow with zoom, and panning has no bounds
kept.evidence: editor-visual/k-zoom-pan.png: at 200% the wall marker is 32px (16px nominal) and covers the window frame; the 36px hit area doubles too. After a 400px drag the photo's edge sits at x=0. setPan has no clamp, so the photo can be dragged off the canvas.
kept.repro: Zoom in four times, then drag the photo.
kept.fix: Set `--z: zoom` on .viewport and give `.dot, .pin` `scale: calc(1 / var(--z))`. Clamp pan to ±fw*(zoom-1)/2 horizontally and ±fh*(zoom-1)/2 vertically.

verdict.reason: Both halves are real, and I found them in the code. In stage.tsx the markers (`.dot`) and pins (`.pin`) are children of `.frame`, which sits inside `.viewport`. The viewport is transformed with `translate(pan) scale(zoom)`, so at 200% a 16px marker draws at 32px, and its 10px `::before` hit ring doubles with it. The auditor's k-zoom-pan.png shows exactly this: the oversized wall marker covers the window frame. For panning, `onFrameMove` does `setPan({ x: d.px + dx, y: d.py + dy })` with no clamp at all, so the photo can be dragged as far as the pointer goes, leaving empty canvas. There is a second gap: `zoomTo` resets pan only when zoom goes back to 1. Zooming out from 300% to 125% keeps a pan that is now too large, so the photo jumps partly off-stage. Severity stays minor: this is polish while zoomed, and nothing breaks.
verdict.fix: 1) stage.tsx: put `['--z' as string]: zoom` in the `.viewport` inline style next to the transform. 2) stage.module.css: add `scale: calc(1 / var(--z, 1));` to `.dot` and `.pin`. The individual `scale` property composes with the existing `translate: -50% -50%` around the element's centre, so the anchor stays put, and the `::before` hit ring plus the hover / selected growth stay at their nominal size. 3) stage.tsx: add a helper `clampPan(p, z) => ({ x: clamp(p.x, ±fw*(z-1)/2), y: clamp(p.y, ±fh*(z-1)/2) })`. This works because the translate is written before the scale, so it is in screen px, and `transform-origin` is the centre. Use it in `onFrameMove` (`setPan(clampPan({...}, zoom))`) and in `zoomTo`, where it re-clamps the current pan for the new zoom instead of resetting only at 1. The Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel zoom goes through `zoomTo`, so it is covered too. No new UI and no register entry beyond a bug-fix line. Verify at 1440: zoom to 200% and 300% and check the marker is still 16px in getBoundingClientRect. Then drag 1000px each way and check the photo's edge never passes the stage's edge. Then zoom from 300% down to 125% and check the photo is still inside.

kept.title: Markers take a light finish's colour and vanish on light photos

So a Pure White, Ivory Cream or Off-White finish turns the square almost entirely white. I zoomed the evidence shot at 3x. On the wood floor and cabinets (514,636 and 333,744) the markers stand out clearly. On the pale ceiling (484,185) and cream wall (854,448) the square still shows, but only through the faint grey ring and drop shadow. That is low contrast rather than gone. So "vanish" and "barely see" overstate it. It is still a real legibility dip on exactly the light photos studios use, and the same weak edge affects any pale finish. There is no functional impact: the markers are still findable and clickable, and the panel list mirrors every surface.

Add a rule `.dot[data-kind='surface'] { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--om-color-overlay-40p), var(--om-elevation-level-2); }`. The existing `[data-selected]` rule comes later in the file with the same specificity, so its purple halo still applies unchanged. Keep the white border: it is what separates the swatch from dark photos. No stage.tsx change is needed because a `data-filled` flag isn't required when every square gets the ring. kept.title: Marker tooltips and the furniture list keep the original photo's labels after edits
kept.where: Stage markers + Furniture panel on an edited version, 1440
kept.evidence: editor-visual/m-marker-tip.png: on V3 (sage walls) the wall marker's tooltip reads 'White Painted Back Wall'. The focus order lists 'White Ceiling' and 'Light Oak Floor' while the floor is walnut. editor-visual/b-mode-furniture.png: V3 shows an emerald sofa, but the list reads 'Grey Fabric Sofa · Keep · Seating'.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this in the code and on screen. In visualizer-editor.tsx (lines 186–191), each marker's `label` comes straight from the photo's detection (`s.label` / `f.label`), and stage.tsx line 127 uses that as the tooltip. A surface marker's `fill` follows only `pending.materials`, never the version's `finishes.surfaces`. The version's own record never reaches the tooltip.

FurniturePanel is not passed `finishes` at all (line 555). A row with no pending change always prints `Keep · {category}` (furniture-panel.tsx, the caption span). That happens even when `finishes.customized[id]` holds the pass's description. The engine writes that in engine/run.ts lines 169, 180 and 187, and the demo's V2 customizes the grey fabric sofa to Emerald Velvet (demo.ts line 15). editor-visual/b-mode-furniture.png shows exactly this: V3 has an emerald sofa while the list reads "Grey Fabric Sofa · Keep · Seating".

The Surfaces panel is partly handled already: its caption shows the version's finish name (`finishes[id].name`). So on the surface side the mismatch is the marker tooltip alone, plus the name line inside the panel.

A studio would notice this in a demo, because the list contradicts the picture right beside it. It is copy only, so the severity stays minor.

The auditor's fix is slightly off. Renaming the marker label to `groupWord + finish` would break `onDot`, which groups by `surfaceGroupFor(m.label)` and keys on `m.label.toLowerCase()`. It would also break the furniture grouping by `normFurnitureKey(label)`. The label should stay the identity and the current finish should be added next to it.
verdict.fix:
Leave the detection labels alone, because they are keys for grouping and selection. Add the version's finish as extra copy instead.

1) visualizer-editor.tsx `markers`:
- Give `Marker` an optional `now?: string | null` field.
- For surfaces, set `now: finishes.surfaces[s.id]?.name ?? null`. Also set `fill: mid ? resolve(mid)?.hex : finishes.surfaces[s.id]?.hex ?? null`, so a finished surface's square shows its current colour.
- For furniture, set `now: finishes.customized[f.id] ?? null`.

2) stage.tsx line 127:
- Make the tooltip `titleCaseLabel(m.label) + (m.now ? ` · now ${m.now}` : '')`.
- Keep aria-label in step with it.

3) furniture-panel.tsx:
- Take a new prop `customized: Finishes['customized']`, passed as `finishes.customized` at line 555.
- When `p.action === 'keep'` and `customized[ids[0]]` is set, the caption reads `Now ${customized[id]} · ${f.category}`.
- Keep `data-new` off in that case, because the change is already on the version and not pending.

Pieces already removed on the version are filtered out by `readingFor`, so they need no copy.

Optionally, the Surfaces panel's row name could stay the photo label, since its caption already shows the finish.

No new components are needed. This reuses the existing Tooltip and caption styles.

Verify on Kevin Ng › Living room › V3 at 1440:
- Hover the back-wall marker. The tooltip should read "White Painted Back Wall · now Sage Green" (or the version's actual finish name).
- Open Furniture. The sofa row should read "Now Emerald Velvet · Seating".

kept.title: The rail keeps 372px between 1025 and 1279, starving the photo and the panels

verdict.reason:
The observation is real. `.editor` sets `--viz-rail: 372px` in components/visualizer/editor/editor.module.css:3. The only breakpoint below that is the ≤767 layout, so between 1025 and 1279 the rail stays at 372px, which is 36% of a 1025px viewport. The screenshots bear this out: a-1025.png shows a photo of about 589×393, and i-many-versions-1025.png shows the panel body between the tabs and the "Describe a change" footer at about 390px tall, with only one row of style cards fully visible.

kept.title: The draft pin card crams its helper line, and both pin boxes show a native resize grip
kept.evidence: editor-visual/k-pin-draft.png: 'The client sees it on the shared link' wraps to three lines squeezed between Cancel and Pin it. The note box and the Reply box (k-pin-thread.png) both show the browser's resize grip, which no house field has.

kept.fix: Put the helper on its own line above the actions (the actions right-aligned), and give the textareas `resize: none; field-sizing: content` (DescribeBox's rule).

verdict.reason:
I confirmed both halves in the auditor's k-pin-draft.png at 1440 and in the code.

1. **The helper line is cramped.** `DraftPin` puts the `.count` span, Cancel and Pin it in a single `.foot[data-row]` row, which is a flex row inside a 280px card. The two buttons take about 170px, so "The client sees it on the shared link" is squeezed to about 90px and wraps to three lines.

2. **The resize grip is real, but it comes from the design system.** The DS `TextArea` (`vendor/openmaison-react/dist/styles.css`, `._textarea_knmj9_26{…resize:vertical}`) shows a native vertical grip. So "no house field has" one is wrong: the DS default has it, and task-panel's Description keeps it on purpose because the mock draws the glyph. Still, the house's own boxes turn it off: move-stage `fields.module.css`, task-panel `.areaControl`, and the visualizer's own `DescribeBox` (`resize: none; field-sizing: content`). The pin card doesn't override it. A grip on a small card floating over the photo lets the box be dragged past the card's `max-height`, and it sits right at the pin. Both the draft note and the Reply box use the DS `TextArea` with no override.

Severity stays polish.
verdict.fix:
These are CSS changes in `pin-card.module.css`, plus one markup change in `DraftPin`.

1. **Helper line (`pin-card.tsx`, `DraftPin`).** Take the `.count` span out of the button row. The simplest way is to drop `data-row` from the draft's `.foot`, so it keeps the default column layout. Render the count/hint first as its own line (`.count { flex: none }` or a separate `.hint` class, body-s, secondary). Then put the Cancel and Pin it buttons in a `<span className={styles.actions}>` (already `display: flex; justify-content: flex-end`) and add `gap: var(--om-spacing-2)`. `.foot[data-row]` is then unused and can go.

2. **Grip.** Add `.card :global(textarea) { resize: none; field-sizing: content; max-height: 160px; }`, and fold it into the existing `.foot :global(textarea) { min-height: 56px; }` rule so it covers the body's draft box too. That matches `DescribeBox`'s rule. Keep the min-heights so the empty box doesn't collapse. The `max-height` stops a long note from pushing the card past its own `max-height`; the textarea scrolls instead.

Leave the DS vendor files alone.

To verify, check 1440 and 390: the hint should sit on one line (two at most) above right-aligned buttons, with no grip on either box.

kept.title: The save stamp is blank at rest (the template editor shows 'Saved <date>')

verdict.reason:

kept.title: Surface edges bounded by an outline come out stair-stepped
kept.where: Engine render and region highlight, every sample surface with a hull; 1440
kept.evidence: S/z-v2-stair.png: the wall/ceiling line in V2 is a staircase of about 25 px steps instead of the photo's straight diagonal. The same staircase shows on the ceiling line in S/06-frame-result.png and S/03-walls-picker.png, and on the floor under the curtain in S/z6-floor-left.png. Cause: segment.ts growRegion rasterises the hull at the small copy's resolution (480/640 px, blocked[] per small pixel), and upscaleMask's narrow smoothstep (0.3–0.7) keeps the 1-small-pixel steps.
kept.repro: Living room Original › Walls › any paint › Generate; zoom 200% on the wall/ceiling line.
kept.fix: lib/visualizer/engine/segment.ts: after upscaleMask, multiply the mask by a full-resolution antialiased hull mask (polygonMask(W,H,poly), already in the file, unioned over hull polys, minus cutout polys) so outline edges are exact at full size. Only the colour-decided edges stay at the small copy's resolution.

verdict.reason:
The observation holds. In lib/visualizer/engine/segment.ts, growRegion sets blocked[] from the hull and cutout polygons one pixel at a time on the small copy (480 or 640 px long side). It then zeroes those pixels in the small mask (lines 64 and 82), and upscaleMask does a bilinear upscale followed by a narrow 0.3–0.7 smoothstep. Because the sample photos are 900×603, each small pixel covers about 1.9 photo pixels. A shallow outline, such as the wall/ceiling line in the living room, therefore renders as a staircase: jogs about 2 px tall and about 20–25 px long. z-v2-stair.png shows this clearly when zoomed. In 06-frame-result.png the jaggies can just be seen at 1:1 along the ceiling line on the right. It is real, but at normal view it is a subtle edge artefact, not a broken render. In that same shot, the floor's boxy rug exclude and the wall bleeding into the ceiling at the far left are far more visible, so "major" overstates it. It becomes clearly visible at 200% zoom, which studios do use in demos.

The proposed fix, as written, would not remove the stairs. Multiplying the upscaled mask by a full-resolution hull mask only clips it. The upscaled mask already falls off about half a small pixel inside the hull, in the same staircase, and the product keeps the lower of the two values, so the stairs stay. The fix has to stop the small mask ending at the hull so the full-resolution polygon alone decides that edge.
verdict.fix:
In lib/visualizer/engine/segment.ts, growRegion:
1. Keep blocked[] exactly as it is for growing and keying.
2. After the close step (and in the key branch), stop zeroing hull and cutout pixels in the small mask. Instead, dilate the region by 2 small pixels into those pixels only: a pixel is set if it is blocked by the hull or a cutout and next to the region. Keep zeroing for `within` and `exclude` boxes.
3. Upscale the result with upscaleMask.
4. Multiply the upscaled mask by a full-resolution edge mask built from the existing polygonMask: the maximum over the hull polygons of polygonMask(W, H, poly), times (1 − the maximum over the cutout polygons). If `def.cut` is passed as the hull, it is covered the same way.
With this, the outline edges are exact and antialiased at full size, and only colour-decided edges keep the small copy's resolution. polygonMask on 900×603 is cheap, but the result can be memoised per def and size in run.ts if needed. Check it with a zoomed crop of the living room wall/ceiling line and the floor under the curtain, before and after, and confirm maskCoverage barely changes.

kept.fix: surfaces-panel.tsx: pass a mixed flag (picks.length > 1) to MaterialPicker, don't tick As in the photo when mixed, and write the sub line as "Now: As in the photo · → Mixed (1 of 2 changing)". Optionally show a small tick-count badge on each swatch picked for part of the scope.

verdict.reason:
The code and the auditor's screenshot both show it. In surfaces-panel.tsx (lines 52–53), `picks` is the set of different pending picks across the scope, and `pick = picks.length === 1 ? picks[0] : null`. If one wall is set to Sage Green and the other is untouched, `picks` holds two values ([sage, null]), so `pick` becomes null. Three things follow:
- The sub line (line 68) shows only "Now: As in the photo", with no "→ …".
- MaterialPicker (material-picker.tsx line 76/79) sets `data-on` and draws the check_circle on "As in the photo" whenever `pick === null`.

In 04-all-walls-mixed.png the "As in the photo" card is filled and ticked, and the sub line reads "2 surfaces · Now: As in the photo". Meanwhile the canvas marker for the window wall is sage and the footer reads "Walls → Sage Green". The panel says the opposite of the pending state. A studio user could press the ticked card thinking nothing changes, and that clears the pick on every wall.

Asymmetry: `nowName` already handles the mixed case ("Mixed") for current finishes. Pending picks don't. I'm keeping the severity at major: this is a misleading state on the main editing surface, not a cosmetic issue.
verdict.fix: Two files need changes. components/visualizer/editor/panels/surfaces-panel.tsx: - Add `const mixed = picks.length > 1` and `const changing = scope.filter((s) => pending[s.id]).length`. - Sub line: when `mixed`, append ` · → Mixed (${changing} of ${scope.length} changing)`. This follows the "Mixed" wording `nowName` already uses. Otherwise keep the current `→ {name}`. - Pass `mixed` to MaterialPicker, plus `partial` = the set of material ids picked for some of the scope: `picks.filter(Boolean)`. components/visualizer/editor/panels/material-picker.tsx: - Accept `mixed?: boolean` and `partial?: string[]`. - The keep card's `data-on` and check_circle become `pick === null && !mixed`, so it only ticks when nothing in the scope is changing. Pressing it still clears all of them, which is correct. - Swatch: tick when `pick === m.id`. When `partial` includes `m.id` and it isn't the whole scope, reuse the existing `nowTag` badge styling to show a small "Some" tag. No new component is needed. The footer chip ("Walls → Sage Green" when only one wall changed) is a related wording issue in the changes list. It could say "White Wall Above The Window → Sage Green", but that is a separate change. kept.title: Remove on the sofa leaves a ghost of its arm, and a Replace after a Remove paints the pasted floor
kept.evidence: S/22-result.png + S/z22-arm.png: after Grey Fabric Sofa → Remove, a semi-transparent grey sofa arm/throw is left at the rug's left edge, the floor there is smeared, and the coffee table's front-left edge is cut. In the same pass, Upholstered Armchair → Replace (photo) paints a brown rectangle on the floor under the chair, because the armchair region was grown on the image after the plate paste had replaced the chair's lower half with floor. (The armchair being cut short is already known.)
kept.repro: Living room Original › Furniture › Grey Fabric Sofa › Remove; Upholstered Armchair › Replace › Add a photo of it (public/visualizer/demo/swatch-walnut.jpg) › Generate.
kept.fix: lib/visualizer/samples.ts: extend the sofa's plate polygon to take the throw and the right arm (cut currently stops short). lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts editPass: compute the regions of recoloured pieces on the base image before any paste, then subtract the removed pieces' plate masks from them so a recolour never lands on the pasted floor.

verdict.reason:
Both artefacts are real and show on the settled V8 (22-after.png), not only mid-transition. After Grey Fabric Sofa › Remove, a pale, sofa-shaped patch stays where the throw and right arm were, and the coffee table's front-left edge is gone. Upholstered Armchair › Replace (photo) then paints a brown slab on the floor under the chair.

The fix for the first half is wrong, though. I drew the sofa's `plate` polygon (samples.ts:47) over original.jpg (verify/poly.png) and it already covers the whole throw and arm; the ghost sits inside the polygon. So it comes from `paste()` (recolor.ts:52-80), not from the polygon being too small. `paste()` sets its light-gain map from ring pixels just outside the mask, and the only test is hue within 0.07 and a brightness ratio of 0.5 to 1.9. The beige jute rug and the oak table pass that test against the plate's floor, so the gain near the rug brightens and greys the pasted floor. You get a pale patch bounded by the polygon's own top-right corner at (0.645, 0.697). Making the polygon bigger would move the patch, not remove it.

The table cut does come from the polygon. Its top edge (0.46,0.689)→(0.58,0.705) runs across the table's front apron at y≈0.693-0.713, and the empty plate has floor there.

The second half is confirmed as described. `editPass` (run.ts:139-189) pastes the plate first, and the sofa plate covers the chair's lower half. Replace/Customize then call `regionOf(img, i.base.url, …)`, which grows from seeds like (0.36,0.64) on the pasted image. Those seeds now land on floor, so the region fills the chair's box and you get the brown rectangle. The auditor missed one thing. `regionOf` caches by the base URL (run.ts:59), so this wrong mask is also stored under the base's key and reused by later edits on the same version. Whether the bug shows depends on cache order, which makes it non-deterministic.

It stays major: removing the sofa on the living-room sample is a headline demo move.
verdict.fix:
1) lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts `editPass`: resolve every recolour region (surfaces in `p.materials`, Replace/Customize picks, note paints) with `regionOf(base, i.base.url, def, size)` on the untouched `base`, before any paste. Keep those masks in a map, and clamp each by `1 − removedMask`, where removedMask is the union of the masks the removes pasted. A recolour then never lands on pasted floor, and the cache only ever holds masks grown on the image its key names.

2) lib/visualizer/engine/recolor.ts `paste(dst, src, mask, keep?)`: add an optional `keep` mask and skip ring pixels where `keep > 0.02` when sampling the gain. In `editPass`, pass the union of the cut polygons (`polygonMask(def.cut)`) of the pieces that stay. For the living room that is the rug, coffee table, armchair and console, so their colours stop feeding the floor's gain. This removes the ghost. As a fallback, tighten the hue gate for ring pixels that fall inside another piece's box.

3) lib/visualizer/samples.ts, the sofa's `plate` top edge: drop it below the coffee table's front apron between x 0.44 and 0.60 (about y 0.715 instead of 0.689-0.705), so Remove no longer shaves the table. Leave the right edge alone; it already takes the throw.

Re-check with the auditor's s22 flow and a zoom on the rug's left edge and the chair's base, on a scratch DB.

kept.title: Curtains and bedspread get ceramic / brass / marble finishes, and Terracotta appears twice
kept.where: Editor › Furniture › Customize, living room Sheer Curtains ×2 and bedroom Grey Knit Bedspread
kept.evidence: S/15-before.png: Sheer Curtains › Customize lists MATERIAL Ceramic · Terracotta · Brass · Marble · Glass · Woven. The bedspread gets the same list, and Playwright found two radios named "Terracotta" (finish and colour) in the open row. Cause: lib/visualizer/furniture.ts FINISH_TYPES uses \b(curtain|drape|drapery|blind)\b, which misses the plural "curtains", and there's no bedding entry, so both fall to FINISH_BY_CATEGORY.Decor.
kept.repro: Living room › Furniture › Sheer Curtains ×2 › Customize. Bedroom › Grey Knit Bedspread › Customize.
kept.fix: lib/visualizer/furniture.ts: allow plurals in FINISH_TYPES (e.g. (curtain|drape|drapery|blind)s?, and likewise rugs, lamps, stools, cushions) and add a bedding row (bedspread|duvet|throw|quilt|blanket|cushion|pillow → Fabric: Linen, Cotton, Knit, Velvet, Bouclé, Wool). Rename or drop the Decor finish "Terracotta" so it doesn't collide with the colour chip.

verdict.reason:
The core bug is real and I reproduced it in code. `customizeFinishes()` in lib/visualizer/furniture.ts lowercases the label and tests the FINISH_TYPES regexes. Those use `\b(curtain|drape|drapery|blind)\b`, and in node that returns false for "sheer curtains". No row matches "grey knit bedspread" either: `\bbed\b` fails on "bedspread", and there is no bedding row. Both labels are sample-room labels in lib/visualizer and inferCategoryFromLabel puts them in Decor, so both fall to FINISH_BY_CATEGORY.Decor: Ceramic · Terracotta · Brass · Marble · Glass · Woven.

The same missing-plural gap hits every FINISH_TYPES row: lamps, stools, chairs, cushions, plants, cabinets and so on. The code's own `containsAny()` already allows plurals (s|es|ies), so FINISH_TYPES is the odd one out.

Two things are off in the finding:
- **The Terracotta collision is not a defect.** The two groups are separate Chips groups ("Material" and "Colour"), and material vs colour is a legitimate pair; vases and planters keep it by design. Renaming it is unnecessary.
- **Severity is overstated.** This is wrong option copy inside the Customize sub-panel, not a broken flow. Call it minor, though it is visible in a demo on the sample living room and bedroom.
verdict.fix:
Change lib/visualizer/furniture.ts only.

1. **Accept plurals everywhere.** Build FINISH_TYPES matchers with the same plural-tolerant pattern as `containsAny`, e.g. a helper `words(['curtain','drape','drapery','blind'])` → `new RegExp('\\b(?:' + … + ')(?:s|es|ies)?\\b')`, rather than hand-editing each regex. `customizeFinishes` then checks `t.match.test(l)` as now.
2. **Add a bedding row.** Words: bedspread, duvet, quilt, coverlet, blanket, throw, cushion, pillow. Heading 'Fabric', options e.g. ['Linen', 'Cotton', 'Knit', 'Velvet', 'Bouclé', 'Wool']. Place it before the `bed|headboard` row so "duvet on bed" does not become Headboard. Add hex swatches for any new option names that the finish swatch map lacks (Knit, Wool).
3. **Leave the Decor 'Terracotta' finish as it is.** Once curtains and bedding route correctly it only shows on vases and objects, where material vs colour is legitimate.

Check the living room's Sheer Curtains and the bedroom's Grey Knit Bedspread › Customize with Playwright on :3011, and log a REG line as a bug fix.

kept.title: After Redraw its outline, the photo keeps showing the old region

kept.evidence: S/10-redrawn.png: after tracing the window frame, the square moves to the new centroid but the purple highlight still covers the whole photo, the flooded region from before. After a reload the same surface shows the traced polygon (S/11-window-after-reload.png). Cause: visualizer-editor.tsx hlKey = imageUrl + scope ids, so a changed region doesn't change the key and the overlay effect never reruns. The engine's maskCache key does include the region, so the render itself uses the new one.
kept.repro: Add a surface by tap (it floods) › Expand its group › open the leaf › Redraw its outline (pen icon) › trace a small shape › look at the highlight.

verdict.reason: The code confirms it. In visualizer-editor.tsx:202, hlKey is `${imageUrl.slice(-80)}|${scope.map(s => s.id).join(',')}`, so it depends only on the ids. Redraw (startDraw → line 311) patches the same surface in place with `{ ...s, region: poly, x: cx, y: cy }`, which keeps the id. So hlKey doesn't change, the [hlKey] effect never reruns, and `highlight` keeps the old flooded overlay. regionOverlay → regionOf (lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts:59) keys maskCache on the region/seeds, so the render and a fresh overlay both use the new polygon. That is why a reload, which rebuilds hl from scratch, shows the traced shape. The user traces an outline and the photo still lights the old region, so it reads as if the redraw failed. It is real, and major is fair for the step's main feedback.
verdict.fix: In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx, build hlKey from each scoped def's geometry as well as its id, mirroring the maskCache key in run.ts: `${imageUrl.slice(-80)}|${scope.map((s) => `${s.id}:${JSON.stringify(s.region ?? s.seeds ?? [s.x, s.y])}`).join(',')}`. The existing `hl.key === hlKey` guard already hides the stale overlay until the new one lands, and scopeRef already carries the updated defs. No other files are needed.

kept.title: Take off the list can't be undone with ⌘Z, and the snackbar's Undo can revert an unrelated pick
kept.where: Editor › Surfaces / Furniture leaf row × (Take off the list) + Undo; header undo
kept.evidence: s12 run: after × on "Tiny" the list shows 6 surfaces; ⌘Z still shows 6. The snackbar Undo then brings it back to 7. Code: forget() stores hidden ids in detection, which is outside the undo history (use-editor-state setDetection doesn't push past). Its Undo calls patchDetection(hiddenWas) and ed.undo(roomId), which pops whatever the latest pending step is. After a ⌘Z, or a pick made before the snackbar closes, that is the wrong step. Adding, drawing and redrawing a surface can't be undone with ⌘Z either.
kept.repro: Surfaces › expand a group › hover a leaf › × › press ⌘Z (nothing comes back) › press the snackbar's Undo (restored, but an earlier pick is gone too if you had one).
kept.fix: components/visualizer/editor/use-editor-state.ts: keep detection in the history entries (past/future hold {pending, detection}) so forget / add / draw / redraw are single ⌘Z steps. The snackbar Undo then calls the same undo. Or have it restore a snapshot taken at forget time (pending + detection) rather than ed.undo().

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this by reading the code; I didn't run it on :3018. In use-editor-state.ts the history holds only Pending (`past: Pending[]`, `future: Pending[]`). setDetection changes detection and bumps rev but never touches past or future.

forget() (visualizer-editor.tsx:265-271) makes two separate writes:
1. patchDetection adds the ids to `hidden`. This is outside the history.
2. patch() runs `omit` on the materials and furniture picks. `omit` (line 72) always returns a new object, so this always pushes one pending step, even when the ids had no picks.

What that means:
- **⌘Z after ×:** it pops only the pending half. The picks come back but the row stays hidden, which matches the s12 run: 6 surfaces before and after ⌘Z.
- **Snackbar Undo:** it restores `hidden` from the closure (`hiddenWas`) and then calls `ed.undo(roomId)` blindly. If the user pressed ⌘Z first, that pops the step before the forget, an unrelated pick. If the user made a pick after the forget and before the snackbar closed, it pops that pick. Either way a real pick is silently lost.
- **Adding surfaces and pieces:** addSurfaceAt, addSurfaceDrawn (draw and redraw) and addPieceAt only call patchDetection, so ⌘Z can't undo them at all. The header Undo button is disabled for them too, since canUndo reads past.length.

Undo that drops a pick without saying so is a correctness bug a studio would feel, so major stands.
verdict.fix:
Put detection into the history in components/visualizer/editor/use-editor-state.ts. One ⌘Z would then undo a forget, add, draw or redraw as a single step, and the snackbar Undo would be a plain undo.

**use-editor-state.ts**
1. Make each history entry a snapshot: `type Snap = { pending: Pending; detection: Detection }`, and `Room = { pending; detection; past: Snap[]; future: Snap[]; rev }`.
2. `setPending` pushes `{ pending: cur.pending, detection: cur.detection }`. Keep the existing coalesce and `history: false` handling.
3. `undo` and `redo` swap both fields, from and into the snapshot.
4. Give `setDetection` the same `opts: { history?: boolean }` and push a snapshot by default.
5. Add `edit(roomId, { pending?: fn, detection?: fn })`. It applies both in one setSt and pushes one snapshot, so a forget is one step, not two.
6. The re-read path at visualizer-editor.tsx:370 (setDetection + setPending with history: false) should also reset past and future for the room, or pass `history: false` to both.

**visualizer-editor.tsx**
1. forget: make one `ed.edit(roomId, { detection: d => ({...d, hidden: [...]}), pending: p => ({...p, materials: omit(...), furniture: omit(...)}) })`.
2. Snackbar action: `ed.undo(roomId)`, the same call the header button and ⌘Z make. Drop the `hiddenWas` closure.
3. Stop it popping the wrong step: capture the room's rev (or past.length) right after the edit. The snackbar action undoes only while the top of past is still that step; otherwise it does nothing, or restores the saved snapshot. Apply the same guard to clearAll's Undo (line 263), which has the same blind `ed.undo`.
4. addSurfaceAt, addSurfaceDrawn and addPieceAt keep calling patchDetection. With the default history they become ⌘Z steps automatically.

Autosave needs no change, since it still saves `{ pending, detection }` on rev.

kept.title: Replace or Customize with nothing chosen still lets you Generate, then fails after a fake progress run
kept.where: Editor › Furniture › Replace / Customize with no pick; the rail's Generate
kept.evidence: S/14-after-replace-nothing.png: Oak Coffee Table › Replace with no quick pick, description or photo. Generate stays enabled ("Oak Coffee Table · Replace" chip), runs about 1.6 s of the progress card, then shows the red "Pick or describe what replaces the oak coffee table first.". Customize with no colour or finish does the same (run.ts editPass checks this only inside the pass).
kept.repro: Furniture › Oak Coffee Table › Replace › Generate.
kept.fix: lib/visualizer/model.ts intentFor: count a replace pick only when replacementDesc or refImage is set, and a customize pick only when a colour, a finish with a hex, or words are set. Otherwise return reason "Pick or describe what replaces the {piece} first." so the button waits with the hint. Also in the row caption: "Replace · choose what" in the warning tone.

verdict.reason: The code confirms it. In lib/visualizer/model.ts, intentFor counts every furniture pick whose action isn't 'keep' as a change (`pieces`). So Replace or Customize with nothing chosen returns kind 'edit' with reason null, and Generate stays enabled. The completeness checks only happen inside the pass, in lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts editPass lines 132–133: the customize check is colour, or a finish with a FINISH_HEX, or readNote words that yield paints; the replace check is replacementDesc or refImage. By then visualizer-editor.tsx runVersion (line ~155) has already started the progress card, so the studio sits through a pretend render and then gets the red error. The furniture-panel caption also shows plain "Replace" / "Customize", which hints at nothing. The whole edit pass fails on one incomplete pick, so a valid wall-finish change waiting beside it is blocked the same way. I'd put severity at minor rather than major: the error message is clear, no credit or data is lost, and the fix is a one-step correction. It is still a real waste of time a studio would feel.
verdict.fix:
1. Make the completeness rule one pure helper, e.g. `pickReady(f: FurniturePick): boolean` in lib/visualizer/furniture.ts. Replace is ready when replacementDesc is trimmed non-empty or refImage is set. Customize is ready when customizeColor is set, or customizeMaterial has a FINISH_HEX, or readNote(`${replacementDesc} sofa`) yields paints. This is the same test run.ts uses today.
2. Use the helper in run.ts editPass's two guards, so the engine keeps the check as a backstop.
3. In model.ts intentFor, after the hasImage / sketch / tool checks and before the `materials || pieces` branch, look for a visible pick that is not ready. If one exists, return `off('Generate', ...)` with "Pick or describe what replaces the {piece} first." or "Pick a colour or a finish for the {piece} first.". This means passing the pieces' labels in the options (a `furnitureLabels` Map beside visibleFurniture) or a generic "the piece" wording. It must return off rather than just leave the pick out of the count, or Generate would quietly skip the piece while another change goes through.
4. In components/visualizer/editor/rail.tsx line 76, the compact text shows "n changes waiting" ahead of intent.reason. When intent.kind is null, show the reason first.
5. In components/visualizer/editor/panels/furniture-panel.tsx line 59, give an unready Replace / Customize the caption "Replace · choose what" / "Customize · choose a colour or finish" in the existing hint/warning caption style. Use no new components.
Afterwards, verify at 1440 on :3011 that Generate is disabled with the hint and becomes enabled after a quick pick.

kept.title: Drawn surfaces paint over whatever stands in front of them
kept.where: Editor › Surfaces › Draw a surface / Redraw outline
kept.evidence: S/10-feature-drawn.png: the traced Feature Panel outline takes in the fiddle-leaf fig's leaves, and a drawn region is used as it is (run.ts regionOf: def.region → polygonMask, no growing), so the leaves get the wallpaper. S/11-window-after-reload.png: a traced "window frame" covers the glass and the trees, so any finish paints the view outside.
kept.repro: Surfaces › Draw a surface › name "Feature panel" › Trace its outline around the wall behind the plant › pick a wallpaper › Generate.
kept.fix: lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts regionOf: treat a drawn region as a hull, not a final mask. Run growRegion with hull:[def.region], key:true and seeds sampled inside the polygon (its centroid plus a few interior points), so things in front of the surface, with a different colour, stay out. Fall back to the plain polygon only when the grown mask covers less than 40% of it.

verdict.reason:
The code path is real. In lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts, regionOf returns polygonMask(def.region) whenever a region exists and skips growRegion completely. A drawn outline is therefore painted as a flat polygon, and 10-feature-drawn.png shows the Feature Panel overlay covering the fiddle-leaf fig's leaves. It is worse than the finding says. "Redraw outline" on a curated sample surface also puts `region` on it (visualizer-editor.tsx:311, model.ts:44). That surface then loses its curated cutout, exclude, hull and seeds, so a redrawn back wall would paint the TV, the art and the plant pot.

The window-frame example is weak evidence. There the user traced the whole window, glass included, so the polygon does what was drawn. The proposed fix would also make it worse: growing from the centroid would seed on the trees and grow over the view.

The proposed fix is not reliable. Growing from interior seeds breaks on patterned or high-contrast surfaces, and the 40% fallback sends the worst cases straight back to the plain polygon. The engine already holds furniture masks and curated cutouts, and those are the dependable way to keep pieces in front of a surface unpainted.
verdict.fix:
In lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts regionOf / the surface branch, keep the drawn polygon as the area the user meant, then take out what stands in front of it:
(1) Pass the room's reading into regionOf for surfaces, or do this where surfaces are recoloured in run.ts. Build the polygon mask, then zero every pixel covered by regionOf(img, url, piece) for each detected furniture piece whose box overlaps the polygon. The fig, the TV and the sofa are all furniture defs on the samples with seeds, box and cut, and the masks are cached. This fixes both the Feature Panel case and redraws on the samples.
(2) When a curated surface is redrawn (it still has seeds or cutout), keep growing it: growRegion with hull: [def.region] plus its own seeds, exclude and cutout, with key as before. That way Redraw outline narrows the wall without dropping its cutouts. Use the plain polygon only when there are no seeds (a manual surface).
(3) Optionally, grow a manual surface from a few interior seeds inside hull [region], with key true, and keep that result only when it covers at least 60% of the polygon; otherwise use the polygon minus the furniture masks. Do not grow when the label reads as glass or window.
No UI change. Add a probe step: draw the Feature Panel around the plant, apply Geometric Grey, Generate, and check that the leaf pixels near (0.88, 0.5) are unchanged against the original.

kept.title: The outline being traced is invisible: stroke width is 0.004 px

kept.evidence: S/11-trace-mid.png: mid-trace only a faint 12% purple fill shows, with no outline. The colour does resolve: `.frame` sets `color: var(--om-color-primary-default)`, so only the width is wrong. S/11-trace-mid.png matches this. Mid-trace, the only thing on the photo is a pale 12% purple patch, with no line, and it is hard to see what you are tracing. That hurts the main moment of Draw a surface / Redraw. I kept the severity at minor because the outline you finish still saves correctly. The point about hiding the region highlight is less certain. Stage renders `highlight` whenever it is set and not in compare, and it uses a breathing multiply blend, so a region selected before entering draw mode can compete with the trace. That part is plausible but secondary.
verdict.fix: In components/visualizer/editor/stage.tsx, draw the trace as two `<polygon>` elements so the shape closes back to the first point. First, a halo: `fill="none" stroke="var(--om-color-surface-default)" strokeWidth={4}`. On top of it, the line: `fill="rgba(85,0,255,0.12)" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth={2}`, which stays --om-color-primary-default. Both keep `vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke"` and `strokeLinejoin="round"`, so the widths are real screen pixels. Also hide the stored highlight while tracing: at line 123, add `&& !path` to the `highlight && !compare` condition. It is best to do that inside Stage rather than in visualizer-editor, so the shape already on the photo does not compete with the new one. Nothing else changes: no new UI, and the colours are DS tokens.

The rail footer (components/visualizer/editor/rail.tsx:86-87) shows "Your changes · {changes.length}" from the `changes` array built in visualizer-editor.tsx:272-293. That array groups surfaces by `groupWord(label)|materialId` and furniture by `normFurnitureKey(label)|action`, so two wall surfaces with the same finish make one chip ("Walls → X") but count as 2 in the button. Two curtain pieces work the same way: one chip, 2 in the button. So the header and the primary button give different numbers on the same screen, for example 3 against "Generate · 4 changes". The two counts also differ on the tool: the chips count it and `intentFor` doesn't. The compact footer (≤ tablet) already says "{changes.length} changes waiting", so the phone and the desktop also disagree for the same pending state. `intent.changes` is only read for the label, so fixing it won't break anything else. It's minor: nothing breaks, but a studio owner reading the rail sees two different numbers for "how many changes".
verdict.fix:
Make the grouped chips the one source of the count.
- **lib/visualizer/model.ts:** give `intentFor`'s options an optional `count?: number`. Use `const changes = o.count ?? (materials + pieces + …)`, and keep the per-id `materials` / `pieces` values only for choosing the kind (the `if (materials || pieces)` branch). The label stays `changes > 1 ? `Generate · ${changes} changes` : 'Generate'`.
- **components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:** move the `intentFor` call (line 121) below the `changes` array (lines 272-293), or build the array first, then pass `count: changes.length`.
- **Tool edge case:** when `pending.tool` is set, the tool branches return their own label ("Empty the room" / "Furnish the room"), so counting the tool chip never reaches the Generate label. No special case is needed.

No new UI or copy. Add a check to the visualizer probe: pick Walls (2 surfaces) + Floor + Ceiling, then assert that the number in "Your changes · N" equals the N in "Generate · N changes".

kept.title: Picks made just before leaving are lost: autosave waits 900 ms and has no flush
kept.evidence: s7b run: picked Floor → Walnut vinyl and closed about 300 ms later. On reload the floor square was unfilled and the pick was gone. use-editor-state.ts saves in a 900 ms timeout that the effect cleanup clears on unmount, and there's no pagehide or unmount flush.

verdict.reason: The code confirms it. In components/visualizer/editor/use-editor-state.ts (lines 51–68) the autosave effect finds the dirty room ids and schedules saveRoomState in a setTimeout(…, 900). Its cleanup `return () => clearTimeout(t)` runs both on every rev change and on unmount. So when the editor unmounts within 900 ms of the last change, the pending save is cancelled and nothing else sends it. Nothing in components/visualizer listens for pagehide, beforeunload or visibilitychange, and the hook exposes no flush. The top bar's Back (visualizer-editor.tsx:620) is a plain `router.push(back)`, which unmounts the editor and drops the timer. The reported repro follows directly from this: pick a finish, leave within a second, and the pick is lost. I didn't re-run it live because the code path is clear. Severity stays minor: it needs a quick exit, and the in-editor Saving/Saved label does warn the user. Still, a studio demoing picks and backing out would notice it.
verdict.fix:
In components/visualizer/editor/use-editor-state.ts:
1. Pull the save loop out into a `flush = useCallback(async () => …)` that reads stRef, picks the ids whose rev is greater than saved.current[id], calls saveRoomState for each and updates saved and setSave the way the loop does now. The timer effect then calls flush() after 900 ms and still clears its timer on rev changes.
2. Add a mount-only effect that registers `pagehide` and `visibilitychange` (when document.visibilityState is 'hidden') listeners calling `void flush()`. Its cleanup removes them and also calls `void flush()` on unmount. That call is fire-and-forget: a server action started during a client navigation still completes. Keep a ref-held in-flight promise so an unmount flush doesn't double-send while a timer save is running.
3. Return `flush` from the hook.

In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:620, change onBack to `async () => { await flush(); router.push(back) }`. Do the same for any other in-editor navigation that leaves the page, such as the rail/menu links to Files or the lead. No new UI and no copy changes. Verify with a probe: pick Floor, then Walnut vinyl, press Back after 300 ms, reopen, and assert the floor swatch is filled. Leave local.db as found.

I confirmed this by reading the code. I didn't check it on :3020, because the code path leaves no doubt. In `surfaces-panel.tsx` (line 97), every group row calls `onSelect({ kind: 'group', group: g })`, even when the group holds one surface. A tap on the photo behaves differently. `onDot` in `visualizer-editor.tsx` (line 194) switches to `{ kind: 'label' }` when the group has one member. The chevron (line 102) is also drawn for every group. For one surface it offers "Set each of the trim & moulding on its own" and expands into a single sub-row that repeats the parent. That sub-row is currently the only place a one-surface group's + (add another) and × (take off the list) live, so dropping the chevron means moving those buttons onto the group row.

Render the existing `rowTools` span on the group row instead, with the same `IconButton` add / close and their Tooltips, calling `onAddLike(members[0]!.label)` and `onForget([members[0]!.id])`. This keeps + and ×, which today live only in the expanded sub-row.

kept.title: Replace quick picks suggest the wrong kind of piece
kept.evidence: S/14-after-replace-nothing.png: Oak Coffee Table offers "Modern dining table" and "Modern console table". S/22-long-desc.png: Upholstered Armchair offers "Modern dining chair". suggestReplacements keeps any preset sharing a non-generic word such as "table" or "chair".
kept.repro: Furniture › Oak Coffee Table › Replace.
kept.fix: lib/visualizer/furniture.ts suggestReplacements: score the head noun phrase ("coffee table", "armchair") higher than a shared generic noun, and drop presets whose type noun differs (dining vs coffee).

verdict.reason:
I reproduced this by calling suggestReplacements directly in lib/visualizer/furniture.ts with style "Modern":
- "Oak Coffee Table" gives Modern coffee table, Modern dining table, Modern side table, Modern console table.
- "Upholstered Armchair" puts "Modern dining chair" first, ahead of every armchair.
- "Side table" is worse: "Modern dining table" comes first and the side table itself is only third.

The cause is in the scoring. Every shared non-generic word adds +8, and "table" and "chair" are not in GENERIC_WORDS. So every Tables preset matches equally on "table", and style affinity then decides the order. The "{Style} {type}" alternatives the function already builds (e.g. "Scandinavian coffee table") are the right kind of piece, but they only fill slots after the presets that matched a word. With limit 4 they get pushed out.

Nothing breaks, but a designer offered a dining table when replacing a coffee table will find it plainly wrong in a live demo. Severity: minor.
verdict.fix:
Change only suggestReplacements in lib/visualizer/furniture.ts (no UI change).

1. Work out the label's type phrase. Take the cleaned label minus GENERIC_WORDS; its last word is the head noun, and a two-word phrase is used when it is a known compound (coffee/side/dining/console/end table, dining/accent/bar/lounge chair, bar stool). The function already computes this as `type`, so reuse it.
2. When scoring a preset against its label, give the type phrase a large bonus (+20 when the label contains the whole phrase). Drop a preset whose label names a different compound with the same head: the label ends in "table"/"chair"/"stool" but carries a different qualifier (dining vs coffee). Keep generic-head matches only when the item's label has no qualifier (e.g. plain "table").
3. Put the generated "{Style} {type}" alternatives right after the exact-type presets, ahead of weaker word-only matches. Oak Coffee Table then gives Modern coffee table · Scandinavian coffee table · Mid-century coffee table…, and Upholstered Armchair gives armchairs only.
