verdict.reason:
The problem is real, but the proposed fix is in the wrong file. The screenshot shows it: a manual "Window Frame" gets six glass swatches under Suggested · Modern (Frosted White, Clear Float, Laminated Safety, Tinted Green, Reeded Clear, Fluted Clear), so a studio has to search to paint or powder-coat a frame.

The picker does not get these categories from surfaces.ts. `surfaces-panel.tsx:51` and `suggestMaterials` (`catalogue.ts:90`) both call `resolveSurfaceCategories` in `lib/visualizer/catalogue.ts` first. That function's `has('window','glazing')` check (line 56) sends "window frame" to `SURFACE_CATEGORY_MAP.Window = ['Glass','Fabrics']`. `surfaceCategoriesFor` in surfaces.ts is only the fallback when that returns undefined, so changing only surfaces.ts would change nothing on screen.

The code also contradicts itself. `surfaceGroupFor` already files window, mullion, sill and trim under 'Trim & Moulding', and selecting that whole group suggests Paints and Laminates (it reuses the Ceiling mapping). Selecting the same frame on its own suggests glass.

Severity stays minor: this is the Suggested row's ranking, not broken behaviour.
verdict.fix:
1. In `lib/visualizer/catalogue.ts`, add a `Trim` entry to `SURFACE_CATEGORY_MAP`: `['Paints', 'Metals', 'Laminates']`.
2. In `resolveSurfaceCategories`, add a check before the door and window lines: `has('frame', 'trim', 'sill', 'mullion', 'skirting', 'baseboard', 'cornice', 'architrave', 'moulding', 'molding')` returns `SURFACE_CATEGORY_MAP.Trim`. That way "window frame" and "door frame" reach Trim, while a bare "window" or "glazing" keeps Glass and Fabrics.
3. Mirror the same check in `lib/visualizer/surfaces.ts`:
   - In `surfaceCategoriesFor`, test `/frame|trim|sill|mullion|skirting|cornice|architrave|mould|mold/` → `'Trim'` before the `/window/` and `/\bdoor\b/` branches.
   - In `groupMaterialCategories`, point `'Trim & Moulding'` at `'Trim'` instead of `'Ceiling'`, so selecting the group and selecting one of its surfaces suggest the same materials.

This needs no new UI or copy. To verify, check that Surfaces › + › "Window frame" shows paints and metals under Suggested, and that a label of just "Window" still shows glass.

kept.title: On a phone the Surfaces list scrolls inside a short tray under the Describe box
kept.evidence: S/20-phone-surfaces.png: with the tray open, the Describe a change field sits above the panel and the list card shows only Walls and Panelling, with Floor cut off inside its own scroll box. verdict.reason:
The observation is real, but the cause is a layout bug, not the Describe box, and it's worse than "minor". The list isn't scrolling inside its own box: it's clipped, and nothing can scroll to the hidden rows. On the live :3013 build at 390×844 (touch), with the Surfaces tray open, `[data-testid=viz-surface-list]` measures clientHeight 126 against scrollHeight 318, with overflow-y hidden, 6 rows. Its scroller, `.panelBody` (rail.module.css:22, a flex column with overflow-y auto), has scrollHeight equal to clientHeight (196 = 196). So `.panelBody` never scrolls, and Floor plus the remaining rows can't be reached. Setting `scrollTop` to 9999 changes nothing (verify/tray-scrolled.png is the same as the auditor's shot). The cause is `.list` in panels.module.css:10: it's a flex item with `overflow: hidden`, which sets its automatic min-height to 0, so it shrinks to fit `.panelBody` and hides the rows it cuts off. It isn't phone-only:
- **1440×700 laptop:** surfaces list 218/318, furniture list 282/497.
- **768×1024 touch tablet:** surfaces 238/318, furniture 270/477.
- **1440×1024:** fits (318/318, 497/497), which is why the desktop baseline never showed it.

The Describe box takes tray height and makes the clipping start sooner, but it isn't the cause. Collapsing it would still leave the rows unreachable on laptops and tablets. It would also invent a new control, and the house rules say not to invent UI. The picker shot (swatches below the scope chips) is only a short tray whose `.panelBody` does scroll, so that part is minor.
verdict.fix:
In components/visualizer/editor/panels/panels.module.css, add `flex-shrink: 0` to `.list`, so the bordered card keeps its full height and `.panelBody` becomes the only scroller. Do the same to any other `overflow: hidden` block that sits directly in a panel's flex column; the ones to check are `.section`, the swatch grid and the board / reference cards. Keep `overflow: hidden`, because the card's rounded corners need it. With that, the "no max-height on .list" part of the auditor's fix already holds.

Leave Describe as it is; collapsing it into a button is not needed. If the tray still feels cramped after the fix, one small follow-up is to raise `.tray`'s `max-height: 44dvh` (editor.module.css:35) for ≤767 only, about 55dvh, which would give the list more room without new UI.

To verify, load the Surfaces and Furniture panels at 390×844 (touch), 768×1024 (touch) and 1440×700, and check that every list's clientHeight equals its scrollHeight and that the last row can be scrolled into view. 1440×1024 should stay byte-identical.

kept.title: Patterns and tiles are laid flat, with no perspective or tile texture
kept.where: Engine render › Wallpapers on a ceiling; Tiles on a floor
kept.evidence: S/z6-ceiling.png: the Japanese Wave ceiling is a flat, uniform, screen-space tile that doesn't shrink toward the back wall, so it reads as a sticker. S/17-kit-result.png: Herringbone White renders as flat white with no herringbone, losing the tile texture the photo had.
kept.repro: Living room › Ceiling › Wallpapers › Japanese Wave › Generate. Kitchen › Floor › Tiles › Herringbone White › Generate.
kept.fix: lib/visualizer/engine/recolor.ts: for floor and ceiling groups, map the texture through a simple homography from the surface's hull quad (samples.ts already has the four corners). Give the tile catalogue entries a pattern (herringbone, subway, hex) in lib/visualizer/patterns.ts, and keep a fraction of the photo's high-frequency detail so grout lines survive.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed both halves in the code and in the auditor's screenshots.

1. **Patterns are laid flat.** `recolor()` in lib/visualizer/engine/recolor.ts picks each pixel's tile colour by screen position, `tex[(y % texture.height) * texture.width + (x % texture.width)]`. Nothing depends on which surface is being painted or on depth. `run.ts` passes one square tile, about a twentieth of the photo wide, for every surface (`textureFor`, and `refinish` line 101). z6-ceiling.png shows the result: the Japanese Wave arcs stay the same size and point the same way across the whole ceiling, so it reads as a sticker, not a plane that recedes.

2. **Tiles have no pattern.** `WALLPAPER_PATTERNS` in lib/visualizer/patterns.ts only covers wp-001…wp-012. So `patternOf('tile-009')` returns null, and Herringbone White is painted as the flat colour #F5F5F5. The same goes for every other patterned tile or floor: Subway, Hexagonal, Fish Scale, Penny Round, Basketweave, Oak Herringbone (floor-002) and Chevron Oak (floor-013).

   The shading term is the photo's lightness against the region's average, so the old floor's large tile joints still show through. That is visible in 17-kit-result.png: the old big-format joints, no herringbone.

Two points in the proposed fix need correcting:
- The shading already carries the photo's high-frequency detail. For a new tile, the photo's old grout should be damped, not kept.
- `catalogue.gen.ts` is generated, so it should not be edited by hand.

Severity is polish: the renders work, but a patterned ceiling or floor looks fake.
verdict.fix:
1. **lib/visualizer/patterns.ts.** Extend `PatternKind` with 'herringbone', 'chevron', 'subway', 'hex', 'fishscale', 'penny' and 'basketweave'. Add `TILE_PATTERNS` keyed by catalogue id: tile-001/006/012 subway, tile-003 hex, tile-004 fishscale, tile-005 penny, tile-009 herringbone, tile-013 basketweave, floor-002 herringbone, floor-013 chevron. Grout goes in `accent`, a light or dark grey chosen against the swatch. Draw each one in `patternTile` and `patternCss`, the way the wallpapers are drawn. Have `patternOf` read both maps. Leave catalogue.gen.ts alone.

2. **lib/visualizer/engine/recolor.ts.** Add an optional `plane` argument: `{ kind: 'floor' | 'ceiling', horizon: number }`. When it is set, look the tile up in ground-plane coordinates, not by `x % w`:
   - `depth = k / |y - horizonY|`
   - `u = (x - W/2) * depth`, `v = depth`
   - clamp near the horizon, then sample the tile bilinearly.

   This makes the motif shrink toward the back wall and converge toward it. Only walls keep the screen-space tiling. When a texture is present, also pull `shade` toward its local blur (keep about 0.6 of the low-frequency light), so the photo's old joints fade under the new grout.

3. **lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts** (`textureFor` and `refinish`). Pass the plane for surfaces whose kind is floor or ceiling. Take the horizon from the sample's back-wall hull when there is one, since samples.ts has its top and bottom edges; otherwise use 0.45·H. Use the same tile size.

4. **Checks.** Re-check the Living room ceiling with Japanese Wave, the Kitchen floor with Herringbone White, and a wall with Subway on :3011 at 1440×1024. Bank the shots under design-source/verify/ai-visualizer/. Log a REG line for the tile motifs: user-directed, carrying on from REG-680.

verdict.reason:
Reproduced from the audit shot 15-before.png at 1440×1024. The code matches: `.changeList` in rail.module.css:28 has `max-height: 112px; overflow-y: auto`, with 28px chips and an 8px gap. kept.title: Picks shown under 'Your changes' are silently dropped by Restyle, Relight, Style transfer, Render from sketch, Empty and Furnish, then wiped from the room
kept.where: Editor rail, Generate footer + engine, all widths (verified 1440x1024)
kept.evidence: Living room V3: Style Modern + Lighting Golden Hour + note 'white ceiling'. The footer read 'YOUR CHANGES · 3 · Style · Modern · Lighting · Golden Hour · Your note', but the button said 'Restyle as Modern'. The result was V4 · Modern with no golden light and no note, and afterward the footer read 'Generate · Pick a finish, a style or a light first.' because all three picks were cleared (04-style+light+note-footer.png, 06-result.png). Same on the showroom sketch: Industrial + Golden Hour + 'navy lower cabinets' produced 'V2 · From sketch · Industrial' only (25-sketch-render-industrial.png). Kitchen: Industrial + Overcast + note + Furnish showed four chips for one pass (58-1366x768-furnish.png). Cause: intentFor() in lib/visualizer/model.ts picks a single pass kind. restylePass, relightPass, transferPass, sketchPass, emptyPass and furnishPass in lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts read only their own inputs. Then afterRender() resets style, lighting, note and tool.
kept.repro: /visualizer/b46000d1-… Living room. Style > Modern. Lighting > Golden Hour. Type 'white ceiling' in Describe a change. The footer shows 3 changes. Generate. V4 shows only the restyle, and the light and the note are gone from the rail.
kept.fix: lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts: after restylePass, transferPass and sketchPass, apply the lighting knobs with grade() and the note's paints/preset, as editPass already does through its `extra` arg. Let relightPass also read pending.note through readNote. For empty and furnish, apply the lighting grade to the plate. Where a pick truly cannot ride along, stop hiding it: in visualizer-editor.tsx, mark those chips (e.g. a `skipped` flag on Change rendered as a struck-through chip with the meta 'Not used by Empty the room'), and make afterRender (lib/visualizer/model.ts) keep the picks that pass did not consume instead of clearing them.

verdict.reason:
The code confirms the finding exactly, so no live run was needed. intentFor() in lib/visualizer/model.ts adds materials, pieces, light, note, style and refs together into `changes`, and the rail shows all of them under "Your changes · n" (rail.tsx:87). But it returns only one pass kind: sketch > empty > furnish > edit > transfer > restyle > relight > note. Only the default edit branch of runPass (lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts) carries the other picks, through editPass's `extra` for the note and through its own style grade plus p.lighting. The other passes read only their own inputs:
- restylePass never reads p.lighting or p.note. On a sample it returns the stored look URL untouched for V1.
- relightPass reads lighting.instruction but not p.note or p.style.
- transferPass, sketchPass, emptyPass and furnishPass ignore lighting and the note.
After that, visualizer-editor.tsx:175 calls afterRender(). afterRender resets style, lighting, note, materials and furniture to emptyPending() and keeps only quality, variants, the transfer settings, the empty and furnish settings, and asPhoto. So Style + Golden Hour + note produces a restyle only, and the unused light and note are wiped with no message. A studio would notice this: the footer promised 3 changes and the button's label ("Restyle as Modern") is the only hint. The severity of major stands.
verdict.fix:
1) lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts: add one helper, `rideAlong(img, pending, applied, finishes)`. It applies the lighting grade: preset knobs, or p.lighting.knobs when lightingSet(), then instruction warmth via readNote. It sets applied.lighting and finishes.lighting with lightLabel(p). It also reads the note once with readNote(p.note): paints go onto matching surfaces the way editPass's paints loop does (move that loop into a shared function), and applied.note is set.
- restylePass: call rideAlong on each variant. When it changes anything, V1 on a sample must go through toDataUrl(cloneImg(look)) and not reuse the raw look URL.
- transferPass and sketchPass: call rideAlong. For sketch, load the look or original into an Img first.
- relightPass: also take the note's paints/warmer and the style's grade (styleLight at 0.5, as editPass does).
- emptyPass and furnishPass: apply only the lighting grade. A note that paints surfaces does not belong on an emptied plate.
2) lib/visualizer/model.ts: change afterRender(p) to afterRender(p, applied: Applied). Clear only what the pass consumed: materials and furniture when applied.surfaces/furniture came from the picks, style when applied.style is set, lighting when applied.lighting is set, and the note when applied.note is set. Always clear tool after empty/furnish. Anything not consumed stays on the rail. Update the call at visualizer-editor.tsx:175 to pass out.variants[0].applied.
3) Where a pick still cannot ride along (for example the note on Empty the room), mark it and do not drop it silently. Have intentFor also return `skipped: string[]` (change ids the chosen kind won't use). In rail.tsx, render those Change chips with the existing chip style plus data-disabled/muted, plus a one-line meta under the list: "Not used by Empty the room — kept for your next Generate". No new component; reuse the chips.module.css chip and the rail's existing meta type.
4) Add a check to the visualizer probe: Style + Golden Hour + note, then Generate. Expect the descriptor to carry the style and applied.lighting and applied.note to be set. With Empty + note, the note chip must survive the render.

kept.title: Restyle in any of the 20 styles without a finished render (the lead's own pick included) leaves hard rectangles of old floor and a blown-out white wall
kept.where: Canvas result of Restyle / Style transfer, Living room

The walls are clipped to pure white, and the grey floor keeps rectangular patches of the old orange wood around the rug box and the plant pot (06-result.png; zoom 07-v4-zoom.png). Style transfer shows the same blocks (36-v10-floor-zoom.png: a wood rectangle beside the throw and around the rug on a dark-grey floor). kept.fix: In restylePass/transferPass (run.ts), feather the recolour mask where exclusion boxes cut it: run spreadMask/blur on the mask edges, or replace the living-room floor excludes with `cutout` polygons that follow the rug and pot. Cap wall lightness in recolor() so near-white palette entries keep the photo's shading (blend luminance instead of replacing it). verdict.reason:
I reproduced both defects from the auditor's shots and traced each one in the code. The hard floor blocks come from `samples.ts:44`, where the living-room floor seed has `exclude: [[0.66,0.72,0.868,0.995],[0.46,0.65,0.705,0.74],[0.515,0.59,0.785,0.69]]`. `segment.ts:39` blocks every pixel inside those boxes. So when `restylePass` or `transferPass` (`run.ts:201` and `run.ts:251`) run `recolor()` on the floor region, whole rectangles of the old oak stay untouched: the strip right of and below the rug, and the square around the pot. The zooms show exactly this on V4 (Modern) and V10 (Style transfer), with straight wood-coloured edges on a grey floor.

The blown-out wall comes from `recolor.ts`. The new lightness is the material's lightness times `shade`, and `shade` is clamped to 0.2–1.6. For a near-white paint (L≈95), any pixel brighter than the region's average goes past 100 and is clipped, so the wall turns flat white and the photo's shading is gone. That is visible in `06-result.png`.

Only five styles have finished looks (Scandinavian, Industrial, Japandi, Bohemian, Dubai Luxury; `samples.ts:34`). The other 15, Modern (Kevin's pick) included, all fall back to this recolour path. That is where the finding's "any of the 20 styles" really applies, and a studio would see it in a live demo. Severity major is right.
verdict.fix:
1. **Hard floor blocks** (`lib/visualizer/samples.ts:44`). Take the three box `exclude`s off the living-room floor seed. Add `cutout` polygons in their place that follow the rug's quadrilateral, the pot's base and the console's feet, the same way the seed already carries a sofa cutout. The mask then follows the objects instead of boxes. As a backstop in `lib/visualizer/engine/segment.ts`, give `exclude` boxes a soft edge of a few pixels using the existing `featherMask`/`spreadMask`, so no future box can print a hard rectangle. Check the bedroom floor seed (line 67) and the kitchen floor seed (line 90) for the same pattern.

2. **White-out on light paints** (`lib/visualizer/engine/recolor.ts`). Replace the linear `L = Lt*shade`, capped at 100, with a soft knee on the highlights. For example, when `shade > 1`, use `L = Lt + (100 - Lt) * (1 - 1/(1 + (shade - 1)*k))`. Also lower the upper clamp as `Lt` rises, so a near-white paint keeps the photo's gradient rather than flattening to 255.

3. **Leave the style cards alone.** Don't add card copy or reorder the cards; that would be invented UI. With fixes 1 and 2 the recoloured styles become acceptable on their own. If a note is still wanted, propose it and log it as `invented copy` in `REGISTER.md` first.

4. **Verify.** Run Restyle as Modern on Living room V3 and a Style transfer, check both on :3011, and bank the before and after shots in `design-source/verify/ai-visualizer/`.

verdict.reason: I reproduced it from the code and the auditor's live screenshots. On an uploaded photo the room gets `fallbackDetection()` (lib/visualizer/model.ts:50). Its Walls surface uses `global: 18` with a hard box `within: [0, 0.04, 1, 0.8]`. `growRegion` (lib/visualizer/engine/segment.ts:27-77) flood-fills through neighbours within `local` and then checks distance from the seed colour. Lightness only counts half there (LW = 0.5), so a cream bedspread, white curtains and a pale window frame all pass as "wall". That is what 45-upload-restyle-japandi.png shows (bed, curtains and floor bleached cream) and 48-upload-note-navy.png shows (bedspread, window and nightstand painted navy). Both have the same straight edge at y≈0.8, which is where the `within` box ends. Nothing in the UI warns that the surfaces on a fallback room are rough: `source: 'fallback'` is set but no component reads it. Separately, style-panel.tsx:18/50 falls back to `ANY_LOOK`, so an uploaded bedroom's Style cards show another room's finished living-room pictures. In a live demo on a client's own photo, the Generate result is visibly broken, so major is right. I disagree with one part of the auditor's fix: a new confirm-the-region step before Generate would be invented UI. The house rule prefers using the region highlight the editor already has, with a line of copy logged in the register.
verdict.fix:
1) lib/visualizer/engine/segment.ts: add a `lightWeight` option to `GrowOpts`. Keep 0.5 for curated samples and use 1.0 for fallback surfaces, so a white bed stops being mistaken for a white wall. Also add an edge stop: skip a neighbour whose own step is small but whose local gradient is above a threshold, taken from a single Sobel pass on the downscaled L channel. Next, feather the `within` limit. Instead of blocking outright, stop admitting pixels in the last ~6% of the box, or fade the mask alpha across that band when upscaling, so there is no straight seam. Finally, run erode→dilate (open) on the fallback mask to drop thin tendrils that crawl into furniture.
2) lib/visualizer/model.ts `fallbackDetection`: pass `lightWeight: 1` and lower Walls `global` to about 12 (floor about 16, ceiling about 10). Bring the Walls `within` bottom up to about 0.7. The floor seed then owns the lower band, and the feather hides the join.
3) Tell the studio the regions are rough, using existing pieces. When `detection.source === 'fallback'`, show the Surfaces panel's region highlight for the hovered or selected surface as the existing overlay already does. Put a caption line under the panel header ("Marked roughly on your photo — check the highlight, or Draw a surface to trace it") that links to the existing Draw a surface tool. Log the copy in REGISTER.md as invented copy.
4) components/visualizer/editor/panels/style-panel.tsx: use `ANY_LOOK` only when the room has a sampleKey. For a fallback room, show the palette + materials card with no photo, as the Classic card already renders.
5) Bank a probe under design-source/verify/ai-visualizer/ that uploads bedroom/original.jpg as a new room, runs Japandi and the navy note, and checks that the bed's pixel box keeps its original colour.

kept.title: ⌘Z does nothing after dragging a lighting slider (focus stays on the range input)
kept.evidence: Master bedroom: dragged Intensity. The drag coalesces correctly into one undo step (the toolbar Undo went moderate→bright→moderate). But document.activeElement stayed 'viz-intensity', and ⌘Z left it at 'bright'. With focus on the range input, the key handler treats INPUT as typing and returns (`typing` check in visualizer-editor.tsx keyRef). Arrow-key edits on Colour temperature were likewise not undoable by ⌘Z.
kept.repro: Master bedroom > Lighting > Fine-tune it by hand > drag Intensity > press ⌘Z without clicking elsewhere.
kept.fix: In visualizer-editor.tsx's key handler, exclude range/checkbox/radio inputs from `typing`: `const typing = t && (t.isContentEditable || t.tagName==='TEXTAREA' || t.tagName==='SELECT' || (t.tagName==='INPUT' && !/^(range|checkbox|radio|button)$/.test((t as HTMLInputElement).type)))`.

verdict.reason:
The bug is real, but I'd rate it minor, not major, and the proposed fix has a regression. I confirmed it from the code and did not run it on :3013. In visualizer-editor.tsx (line 503), `typing` is true for every INPUT, and the sliders in lighting-panel.tsx (line 27) are `<input type="range">`. So once a slider has focus after a drag or an arrow-key change, the ⌘Z branch on line 505 is skipped. Native undo does nothing on a range input, so the press does nothing at all. The toolbar Undo still works, and one click elsewhere brings ⌘Z back. That makes it a keyboard inconvenience rather than a broken feature.

The auditor's fix changes `typing` itself, which would also let the rest of the handler run while a range input has focus. Escape would then clear the selection or close the tray. ArrowLeft/Right would do two things at once: move the slider natively and switch the rendered version. The arrow guard only looks for elements with an explicit `role="slider"` attribute (`closest('[role="slider"]')`), which a bare `<input type="range">` does not have.
verdict.fix: Leave `typing` as it is and change only the undo check in components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx's keyRef handler. Add `const textEntry = typing && !(t instanceof HTMLInputElement && /^(range|checkbox|radio|button)$/.test(t.type))`. Then write the ⌘Z line as `if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === 'z' && !textEntry) { ... }`. Keep the following `if (typing) return` so Escape and arrow keys still go to the slider. Because `ed.undo` coalesces the drag into one step, ⌘Z then undoes the slider change as the toolbar does. Check it with Playwright on Master bedroom > Lighting > Fine-tune it by hand: drag Intensity, press Meta+Z, and expect the value back at its previous setting. Also check that ArrowRight on the focused slider does not change the rendered version. No new UI, so it needs a REGISTER entry as a bug fix only.

verdict.reason: I reproduced it from the code and the auditor's screenshot. In rail.module.css the `.foot` block has `flex-shrink: 0` and no height cap. kept.title: Relighting a version that is already relit stacks the grades (Blue Hour on a Golden Hour version stays golden)
kept.evidence: Master bedroom V1 (Relit · Golden Hour) > Blue Hour: the live preview is a darker golden-hour photo with orange sun patches, not blue dusk (41-bedroom-v1-bluehour-preview.png). Golden Hour on the Living room V3 (already golden) doubled into an orange, blown-out window (03-style+light-preview.png). relightPass and previewLight grade the version on screen, not its un-lit parent.
kept.repro: Master bedroom > V1 > Lighting > Blue Hour.
kept.fix: In visualizer-editor.tsx (preview) and in the relight PassInput base, when view.finishes.lighting is set and view.kind==='relight', use the parent version's image (view.parentKey) as the source so a new light replaces the old one. Or, on the sample's original, use sample.relit when it exists.

verdict.reason: The code confirms it. In visualizer-editor.tsx, imageUrl is always the picture of the version on screen (line 113). The lighting preview effect (around line 219) calls previewLight(imgRef.current, knobs), and previewLight in lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts (line 334) just runs grade() on that picture. generate() (line 160) passes the same picture as runPass's base, and relightPass (run.ts line 235) loads i.base.url and grades it again. So a relight on a version that is already 'Relit · Golden Hour' puts a second grade on top of the first: Blue Hour over Golden Hour comes out as a darker gold, and Golden Hour over Golden Hour doubles. The exact sample.relit shortcut never helps here, because it only fires when viewKey === ORIGINAL. A studio would notice this. Relighting is naturally a 'try another light' action, and the result contradicts its own label: the version says 'Relit · Blue Hour' but still looks golden. Minor severity is right. It is a quality problem, not lost data. One case stays open: a version edited after a relight (a non-relight kind with finishes.lighting set) still carries the old grade, and this fix does not address that.
verdict.fix:
In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx, work out the light source once, next to imageUrl:

    let lightSrc = view
    while (lightSrc && lightSrc.kind === 'relight') lightSrc = lightSrc.parentKey === ORIGINAL ? null : all.find((v) => v.key === lightSrc!.parentKey) ?? null
    const lightKey = view?.kind === 'relight' ? (lightSrc?.key ?? ORIGINAL) : viewKey
    const lightUrl = view?.kind === 'relight' ? (lightSrc ? urlOf(lightSrc) : room?.imageUrl ?? null) : imageUrl

The loop walks back through consecutive relights to the last picture that has no light on it.

Then use it in three places:
(1) The preview. Build pvKey from lightUrl, and have the effect read lightUrl (through a ref, as imgRef does today) in place of imgRef.current.
(2) The `relit` shortcut. Test lightKey === ORIGINAL in place of viewKey === ORIGINAL, so that Blue Hour on a relit-from-original version still shows the curated sample.relit picture.
(3) generate(). When kind === 'relight', pass base: { key: lightKey, url: lightUrl, finishes }. Keep the view's own finishes, since relightPass overwrites finishes.lighting anyway, and keep parentKey: viewKey on saveRender so the version history still reads 'from V1'.

relightPass in lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts needs no change. Its existing i.base.key === ORIGINAL check then matches the curated relit picture on its own. No new UI and no new copy.

kept.title: Empty the room ignores 'Strip to shell' vs 'Keep built-ins' and 'Anything else to take out'

verdict.reason:
The observation is real. In `emptyPass` (lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts:298-306), both scopes paste the same `sample.empty` plate (`public/visualizer/samples/living-room/defurnished.jpg`). The scope only reaches the version label ("Emptied · Strip to shell"), and `extra` only lands in `applied.note`. The auditor's screenshot 18-empty-shell-from-original.png shows V8 labelled "Strip to shell" with both sheer curtains still hanging. That picture matches the plate exactly.

The proposed fix would not work. The defurnished plate has the curtains in it (both panels either side of the window), so pasting the plate over the curtain `cut` polygons changes nothing. The curated engine has no curtain-free source to paste from.

There is also a second, related inconsistency. `finishes.removed` lists every sample furniture piece as removed, including f8 and f9 (the two sheer curtains), while the picture still shows them. The version's record says the curtains are gone when they are not.

On scope: the living-room sample has no panelling or fitted cabinetry, so "Keep built-ins" and "Strip to shell" should give the same picture on it. That part is correct behaviour, but the UI never says so. Severity stays minor: this only happens when someone asks for something the stand-in engine cannot do. The problem is that it answers with a label claiming it did.
verdict.fix:
Don't fake a removal the engine can't do. Make the result and the panel say what really happened.

1. **lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts, `emptyPass`:**
   - Build `removed` only from sample pieces that are really absent from the plate. Add a small `inPlate` / `staysEmpty` flag on the sample's furniture entries in lib/visualizer/samples.ts: true for the curtains in the living room, and for the bedroom's linen curtains if its plate keeps them. Filter those out, so `finishes.removed` no longer lists the curtains.

The same line should reach the Generate snackbar through the existing `note` path, instead of echoing the request as if it had been done.

2. **components/visualizer/editor/panels/tools-panel.tsx:** under the "How far" chips, when the room's sample has no built-ins (a `builtIns: false` flag on the sample in samples.ts), add one hint line: "This photo has no panelling or fitted cabinetry, so both give the same room."

3. For a real image model later, `scope` and `extra` belong in the prompt. Leave a comment in `emptyPass` saying so.

The full names are only reachable through a native `title` on each chip and an `aria-label` on a plain span. Screen readers don't reliably announce an `aria-label` on a span with no role, and the card is a radio button anyway.

The problem is real but cosmetic, so it stays polish. It does matter to the feature, though: the handoff sold these cards as "the room in that style plus the materials it picks", and today the materials can't be read.
verdict.fix:
Keep the words and let them wrap rather than dropping them, since naming the materials is what the board is for.

**In `panels.module.css`:**
- Make `.board` `flex-wrap: wrap`.
- Give `.boardWords` `flex-basis: 100%` and `margin-left: 0`, so it sits on its own line under the chips.
- Replace the nowrap/ellipsis on `.boardWords` with `white-space: normal; display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden`, keeping `--om-type-body-s` and `on-surface-secondary`.

**In `style-panel.tsx`:**
- Drop the chips' native `title={m.name}`, because the words now name them.
- Mark the chips `aria-hidden`.
- Remove the span's `aria-label`, so the visible words are what a screen reader reads as part of the radio's name.

**Check:** 1440 and 390 (phone sheet), making sure the cards in a row stay the same height.

**If the words should go instead:** remove `.boardWords` and put each chip's name in the house tooltip (`components/om` tooltip) rather than a native `title`.

kept.title: Cancel leaves the old run's step timer going; a quick re-Generate advances at double speed
kept.evidence: Code path: cancelRun() bumps runRef and clears `running`, but the `tick` setInterval created in generate() is only cleared once that run's runPass + wait(min) resolves. A Generate started in that window receives step increments from both intervals. Observed: Cancel itself works ('Stopped — nothing was kept', no V added; 15-cancelled.png).
kept.repro: Lighting > Daylight > Generate > Cancel at about 0.5 s > Generate again at once: the progress steps jump.
kept.fix: Keep the interval id in a ref (tickRef) and clearInterval it in cancelRun and at the start of generate().

verdict.reason: Confirmed in code (components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx lines 150–181). `cancelRun` bumps `runRef` and clears `running`, but it cannot reach the `tick` interval, which is a local in `generate()`. That interval is cleared only after the cancelled run's `Promise.all([runPass, wait(min)])` resolves, at line 161, which takes 1.6–2.6 s or more. `cancelRun` sets `running` to null, so the guard at line 151 lets a new Generate start straight away. The old interval's updater is `setRunning((r) => r && r.step < len-2 ? {...r, step+1} : r)`. It doesn't check the token, so it also advances the new run's step. The step labels therefore run up to about twice as fast, and the new run reaches its second-to-last label early and sits there. The effect is cosmetic only. The step cap (`steps.length - 2`) holds, the final step and save are token-guarded, and nothing wrong is kept or shown. So the bug is real, but it only shows if you Cancel and re-Generate within about 2 s, and the only symptom is progress labels moving faster. That is polish, not minor. I did not run it live, because the code path is unambiguous.
verdict.fix: In visualizer-editor.tsx, add `const tickRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null>(null)` next to `runRef`. In `generate()`, call `if (tickRef.current) clearInterval(tickRef.current)` before creating the interval, then store it in `tickRef.current = setInterval(...)`. Make `stop`, the two token-mismatch early returns and `cancelRun` use `clearInterval(tickRef.current!)` guarded by a check that the stored id is this run's tick, so a late-resolving old run cannot clear the new run's interval. A simpler option is to keep the local `tick` and have `cancelRun` clear `tickRef.current`, which `generate` sets. As a belt-and-braces measure, also check the token inside the tick callback: `() => { if (token !== runRef.current) return clearInterval(tick); setRunning(...) }`. That self-cancelling check is on its own enough to fix the bug, and it is a one-line change.

kept.title: Small copy slips around Generate and the sketch
kept.evidence: A 3-version restyle's last step reads 'Keeping the version' (s3 step log). The sketch's tile says 'Original · the photo' (23-sketchorig-tools.png). On the sketch, where no squares are shown, the hint banner still says 'Click a square on the photo to pick its finish'. 'Draw a surface' is disabled on a sketch without saying why.

Swap the hint for a sketch ('Render it into a photo first — pick a style, then Render from sketch'). Give the disabled Draw button a meta/tooltip reason.

verdict.reason: All four slips are real in the code. (1) In visualizer-editor.tsx:59-67, the last entry in every STEPS list is the fixed string 'Keeping the version'. generate() (line 153) runs up to pending.variants renders for edit, restyle and transfer, but the step text never changes, so a 3-version run still ends on "Keeping the version". (2) versions-strip.tsx:61 always gives the Original tile the subtitle 'the photo'. For a sketch room that tile shows the sketch. (3) The hint banner at visualizer-editor.tsx:627-630 checks only hintSeen, rooms and the tray. It has no sketch branch, so on a sketch it still says to click a square on the photo, but a sketch shows no squares. (4) tools-panel.tsx:68 disables Draw a surface with isDisabled={sketch && !pending.asPhoto}, and the hint under it doesn't give the reason. Also, the Surfaces panel's draw and add icon buttons (surfaces-panel.tsx:78) are disabled on a sketch, but their tooltips still say "Draw a surface on the photo" and don't give a reason either. Each one is a small copy slip, so polish is the right severity. The banner can be dismissed once, which limits slip 3 but doesn't fix it.
verdict.fix:
- **visualizer-editor.tsx:** In generate(), compute count first, then build the steps: `steps = count > 1 ? [...STEPS[kind].slice(0, -1), 'Keeping the versions'] : STEPS[kind]`.
- **Hint banner:** When the current room's detection is a sketch, and no photo version is being viewed yet, show the sketch copy: 'This is a sketch — pick a style, then Render from sketch to turn it into a photo.' Keep the rest of the banner as it is. Log that line in REGISTER.md as invented copy.
- **versions-strip.tsx:** Add a prop that tells the strip it holds a sketch (for example `originalSub`, passed from the editor as detection.sketch ? 'the sketch' : 'the photo'), and use it on the Original tile.

- **surfaces-panel.tsx:** Change the disabled icon buttons' Tooltip label on a sketch to the same reason.

Reuse the existing styles.hint, Tooltip and note pieces. No new UI.

kept.title: The Compare slider can't be dragged, clicked or tapped in the editor; only the keyboard moves it
kept.where: Editor canvas › Compare, 1440 desktop and 390/768 touch
kept.evidence: s2.cjs: dragging from 70%→30% on [data-testid=viz-compare], a plain click at 80% and dragging the handle itself all leave aria-valuenow at 50. The computed pointer-events on the compare box is 'none'. s21.cjs: a touch tap at 20% at 390 and 768 also leaves it at 50. Screenshot versions-menus/06-compare-drag.png shows the divider still at the middle after the drag. The same slider works inside Present (14-present-compare-drag.png moved it to 25).
kept.repro: Open /visualizer/b46000d1-…?room=4088c474-… on V3, press Compare, then drag the white divider or click anywhere on the photo. Nothing moves.

Give the slider its own class (e.g. `.compare { position:absolute; inset:0; }` with no pointer-events rule) and keep `.fill` for the passive overlays (preview, highlight).

verdict.reason: The code backs the finding. In components/visualizer/editor/stage.tsx line 112, the editor passes `className={styles.fill}` to `<CompareSlider>`. In components/visualizer/editor/stage.module.css line 10, `.fill { pointer-events: none; }` is set. `pointer-events` is inherited, so the slider box and its role="slider" divider (including the handle) both stop receiving pointer events. The box's onPointerDown/Move/Up never fire, and a drag, click or touch tap falls through to the stage underneath. Only the divider's onKeyDown still works, which is why the arrow keys move it. The Present dialog passes `styles.presentCompare` and the share page's `.fill` has no pointer-events rule, so both of those work. That matches the auditor's working Present screenshot. In components/visualizer/editor/stage.tsx line 112, pass `className={styles.compare}` instead of `styles.fill`. Leave `.fill` (pointer-events: none) on the passive overlays: the preview img, the highlight img and the pins svg. No change is needed to the shared components/om/compare-slider.tsx. kept.title: Leaving the editor within about 1 s of a pick silently loses that pick (autosave timer dropped on unmount)
kept.evidence: s9.cjs, Kitchen room: I picked Cabinets → Rose Gold and pressed Back 100 ms later. After reopening, the room showed 'Cabinets → Midnight Blue', the previous saved pick. Picks that got the full 900 ms survived a reload, and so did picks followed by a room switch. The top bar keeps showing the old 'Saved' tick during that window, so nothing tells the designer the pick isn't saved yet.
kept.repro: In a room, pick any finish, then press Back (or close the tab or reload) within about 900 ms. Reopen the design: the pick is gone.
kept.fix: use-editor-state.ts: the autosave effect's cleanup `clearTimeout(t)` also runs on unmount. Keep a `flush()` that saves every room whose rev is ahead of saved.current. Call it from the unmount cleanup and from `pagehide` / `visibilitychange`, and await it in the editor's onBack before router.push(back) (visualizer-editor.tsx). Also show 'Saving…' (or an unsaved dot) as soon as rev is ahead of saved, not only while the request is in flight.

verdict.reason: The code confirms it without a live run. In use-editor-state.ts (lines 54–68), autosave is a single effect keyed on `revs` that schedules `setTimeout(…, 900)`. Its cleanup, `return () => clearTimeout(t)`, runs on every rev change and also on unmount. No flush runs on unmount, `pagehide` or `visibilitychange`. The editor's Back (visualizer-editor.tsx:620 `onBack={() => router.push(back)}`, and line 472) navigates straight away. So a pick made less than 900 ms before Back, a reload or a tab close is never sent to `saveRoomState`. Switching rooms keeps the hook mounted, so the timer survives, which matches the auditor's control case. The top bar (topbar.tsx:48) shows "Saving…" only while `save.saving` is true, and that only flips inside the timer callback. During the 900 ms debounce it keeps the old "Saved" tick, so nothing warns the designer. The pick is silently lost, and a designer who picks and leaves at once will hit this often. Major is fair.
verdict.fix:
1. use-editor-state.ts: pull the save loop out of the timer into a `flush = useCallback(async () => …)`. It computes the dirty ids from stRef/saved (rev > saved), saves each with saveRoomState, and records `saved.current[id] = r.rev`. Guard it with an in-flight promise ref so two flushes never overlap. The debounce effect then calls `flush()` after 900 ms.
2. Add one effect with empty deps. It registers `pagehide` and `visibilitychange` (when hidden) listeners that call `void flush()`, and its unmount cleanup also calls `void flush()`. A server action can still complete after a client-side route change. Return `flush` from the hook.
3. Show the pending state. Add `dirty` = any room with rev > saved (computed in render from `st` plus a saved-revs state mirror, not by reading the ref in render), and pass `saving={save.saving || dirty}` so the top bar shows the existing "Saving…" line as soon as a pick lands. No new UI is needed.
4. visualizer-editor.tsx: make Back async, `onBack={async () => { await flush(); router.push(back) }}` (and the same at line 472). If the save fails, use the house rule and snack "Couldn't save your changes" instead of leaving silently.
5. Optionally add a `beforeunload` prompt only while dirty, as a fallback for tab close.
6. Verify with the auditor's s9 probe: pick, Back after 100 ms, reopen, and the pick is kept. Also check that the top bar shows Saving… right after a pick.

kept.title: The version tile's ⋯ and Present's ‹ › arrows have no background, so they are near-invisible on photos (display:contents bug)
kept.where: Versions strip tile kebab (hover) and Present dialog prev/next, desktop and phone
kept.evidence: s16.cjs: `.kebab > *` lands on the Tooltip anchor span, which has display:contents. It gets background rgb(255,255,255) but paints nothing, and the real <button> stays transparent. 100-hover-mb.png: hovering Master bedroom V1 shows no ⋯ at all (dark dots on a dark render). 101-hover-v3.png: the dots are faint grey on the photo. The same happens with `.nav > *` in Present: s23.cjs shows the anchor with display:contents and the button with a transparent background, and 150-present-next-arrow.png shows only a thin outline over the bonsai. 133-touch-present-390.png: the arrows are barely visible on a phone. verdict.reason: Reproduced from the code and the screenshot. The Tooltip anchor is `.anchor { display: contents; }` (components/om/tooltip.module.css:2), so it has no box. That means `.kebab > *` (versions-strip.module.css:21) and `.nav > *` (dialogs.module.css:50) put their background, radius and shadow on an element that paints nothing. The IconButton underneath keeps `.btn { background: transparent }` from icon-button.module.css. The kebab uses variant="bare", so it has no border either: dark dots sit straight on the render. The Present arrows use the default secondary variant, so all that shows is a 1px border with a grey chevron. 150-present-next-arrow.png confirms it: a thin outlined square over the bonsai with the chevron almost invisible. The same trap is already documented in segmented.module.css:11 ("Each segment sits inside a display:contents tooltip wrapper"), so this is a known pattern that was missed here. The 24px target is real but secondary. The tile is only 96–128px wide, so a full 36px button on every breakpoint would cover a lot of the thumbnail. Enlarge it on touch only.

Keep the bare variant's own hover wash through `.kebab button:hover { background: color-mix(...) }`, or simply let the surface stay. Add `@media (hover: none) { .kebab button { width: 36px; height: 36px; } }` so the phone/tablet target meets the house's 36px while the desktop hover chip stays 24px over the small thumbnail. Leave versions-strip.tsx as is, or pass size={36} only if the owner prefers one size everywhere. 2) components/visualizer/editor/dialogs/dialogs.module.css:50: change `.nav > *` to `.nav button { background: var(--om-color-surface-default); box-shadow: var(--om-elevation-level-3); }`, drop the `!important`, and add `.nav button:hover { background: var(--om-color-surface-variant); }` so the secondary hover wash is still visible over the solid surface. Verify on :3011 with Master bedroom V1 hovered (desktop), Present with Before and after on at 1440 and at 390 touch, and check that the 1440 tile layout is otherwise byte-identical.

verdict.reason: I reproduced this in both the code and the auditor's screenshot. In moodboard-dialog.tsx (lines 60–74), the moodboard looks up surface and piece labels only in `version.applied`. That list holds only the current pass's changes, so a relight (V3) or a wallpaper edit on top of V3 (V4) has no labels for the finishes it inherits from V2. When no label is found, line 65 prints `c?.category` and then appends ` · ${c.category}` again, giving "Paints · Paints · Matte" and "Flooring · Flooring · Satin". Pieces fall back to "A piece". 20-mood-V3.png shows exactly "Paints · Paints · Matte", "Flooring · Flooring · Satin" and "A piece — Emerald Velvet". This page is printed and shared with the client, so losing where each finish goes and which piece was restyled is a visible defect. Major is fair.
verdict.fix:
1. In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx (line 717), pass the room's current detection (`detection`, already in scope at line 115) to `MoodboardDialog` as a new prop, e.g. `labels={{ surfaces: detection?.surfaces ?? [], furniture: detection?.furniture ?? [] }}`.
2. In components/visualizer/editor/dialogs/moodboard-dialog.tsx, resolve a surface label by looking in `version.applied.surfaces` first, then in the detection's surfaces by id, then `groupWord`. Build `where` from that.
3. When nothing resolves, print only `c.category` once: `[where || c?.category, FINISH[...]]`. Drop the duplicated ` · ${c.category}` whenever the category already stands in for `where`. That gives "Walls · Paints · Matte", or "Paints · Matte" when nothing resolves.
4. Resolve pieces the same way: `applied.furniture`, then the detection's furniture by id, with `titleCaseLabel` and the brackets stripped.
5. Keep "A piece" only as a last resort, for example when a manual mark was deleted since.
6. Optional hardening: when a pass is saved, also store `label` in `FinishedSurface` (lib/visualizer/model.ts, `finishes.surfaces[id]`). Stored versions then carry their own labels even if detection changes later. This is additive and optional; `label?: string`, read first.

After the change, check V2, V3 and a new V4 wallpaper moodboard at 1440×1024, including the print view.

kept.title: A Designer who can't delete the design can still delete any whole room (and every version in it)
kept.where: Top bar › Room options › Delete room; app/visualizer/actions.ts deleteRoom
kept.evidence: s12.cjs, viewing as Michelle (Designer on Kevin's lead): the design menu shows 'Delete design — Only whoever made it, an Owner or an Admin can rename or delete this [disabled]', but the room menu offers 'Delete room' enabled. deleteRoom() calls roomFor() only and checks no rule. lib/visualizer/policy.ts says 'a design, a room's delete and a studio material are changed by whoever made them, an Owner or an Admin'.
kept.repro: Use Demo Studio › View as › Michelle, open Kevin Ng's design, then ⋯ (Room options) › Delete room. The room and its renders go.
kept.fix: In deleteRoom, return { error: DESIGN_RULE-style message } unless designChangeBlock(viewer, room.createdBy ?? design.createdBy) is null. Add `mayDeleteRoom` per room to VisualizerEditorData and disable the menu item with the rule as meta text, the same way 'Delete design' does. Consider the same rule for Delete on a version that has been shared.

verdict.reason: The code confirms it. deleteRoom (app/visualizer/actions.ts:158-162) calls only roomFor(), which runs designFor(). That checks the lead's visibility (canOpenLead) and that the design isn't deleted, but it never checks who made the design or the room, so there is no designChangeBlock. The editor's menu item (visualizer-editor.tsx:690) is disabled only on `readOnly`, which means the design is in the trash. It ignores data.design.mayChange, while Rename and Delete design next to it (lines 694 and 698) respect it. lib/visualizer/policy.ts states the intended rule in its header: "a design, a room's delete and a studio material are changed by whoever made them, an Owner or an Admin". So this is a gap against a rule the build already declared, not a new rule. project_rooms already has created_by (schema.ts:1193; addRoom stamps it), so the fix needs no migration. The delete is soft, but restoreRoom's only caller is the snackbar's Undo; once that is dismissed, no screen can bring the room back. A Designer who only sees Kevin's lead can therefore permanently remove another member's room and all its renders. That is major, the same class as the Quote X-Ray delete rule (REG-641). I did not run it live, because the code path is unambiguous and the auditor's run as Michelle matches it.
verdict.fix: 1) lib/visualizer/policy.ts: add `export const ROOM_RULE = 'Only whoever made it or the design, an Owner or an Admin can delete this room'` and `roomDeleteBlock(v, roomCreatedBy, designCreatedBy)`. It returns null when the viewer is an Owner or Admin, or when v.id equals the room's maker or the design's maker; otherwise it returns ROOM_RULE. The design maker is included because the design rule already lets them delete the whole design. 2) app/visualizer/actions.ts deleteRoom: after roomFor, add `const block = roomDeleteBlock(got.viewer, got.r.createdBy, got.d.createdBy); if (block) return { error: block }`. Apply the same guard to restoreRoom, which currently skips roomFor entirely; route it through a lookup that allows deleted rows but still checks the viewer. 3) lib/visualizer/queries.ts: give each room in VisualizerEditorData a `mayDelete: string | null` computed with roomDeleteBlock. 4) components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:690: `disabled={!!room?.mayDelete || readOnly}`, with the rule shown in the menu row's meta line, in the same `styles.menuRow` / `styles.menuMeta` pattern as Delete design. The existing snackbar already shows a server refusal. Put the rule in the Settings › Studio *Who may do what* list (lib/settings/permissions.ts) and add a REG entry. Leave version deletes as they are: they are per-render and have their own Undo, and gating them is a separate call.

kept.title: Deleting a shared version (the client's favourite) has no warning and no way back once the snackbar closes; the client's pins and notes vanish from the studio's view
kept.evidence: s6.cjs: deleting V2 (★ favourite, 1 note, 2 pins, shared) removes it immediately. The snackbar Undo is the only way back, and 30-deleted-v2.png shows the snackbar covering the strip. After it closed there was no Deleted-versions place anywhere, so V2 stayed gone in my scratch DB. The client link /renders/17fe84ab2eca47 still shows V2 with its favourite and pin controls (31-client-while-deleted.png), and the client's pin 'Is the velvet easy to keep clean?' is now invisible in the editor. The hint band still says 'Every version stays in the strip; nothing is lost.'
kept.repro: Living room › V2 ⋯ › Delete, then wait for the snackbar to close.
kept.fix: Before deleting a version that is on an active link, or has client responses or pins, show the house ConfirmDialog naming what goes ('V2 is on Kevin's link — his favourite, 1 note and 2 pins'). Add a 'Deleted versions' entry (the strip head's count or the room menu) listing soft-deleted variants with Restore (restoreVersion already exists), like the Deleted sheets elsewhere. Reword the hint once Delete exists.

verdict.reason:
The code does what the auditor describes. `removeVersion` in visualizer-editor.tsx (lines 441-448) marks the version deleted straight away, with no ConfirmDialog. The only way back is the snackbar Undo, which calls `restoreVersion`. The editor then drops that version everywhere. The strip and the viewer use `filter(v => !v.deleted)` in versions-strip.tsx:56 and visualizer-editor.tsx:107. Pins are shown only for the version on screen (`vPins`, line 238), so a deleted version's client pins can't be reached. No surface lists deleted versions: `VersionView.deleted` is read only to hide them, and there is no Deleted-versions sheet, unlike Deleted designs and Deleted materials.

The client link keeps working. `fetchShare` in lib/visualizer/queries.ts reads the frozen `snapshot` and never checks `deletedAt`, so the client still sees V2 and can favourite it and pin it while the studio can't see those replies. The hint at line 629 still says "Every version stays in the strip; nothing is lost.", which is now untrue.

The data needed for a warning is already in the editor: the `badges` map (lines 243-252) holds favourite, notes, pins and shared for each version key. Deleting a design already has a ConfirmDialog (line 723), so a confirm for a version that carries client input matches the house pattern.

Severity stays major rather than blocker. Nothing is hard-deleted (the row keeps `deletedAt`), but in the UI the client's feedback is lost for good once the snackbar closes.
verdict.fix:
1) Confirm in visualizer-editor.tsx before deleting a version that carries client input. The ⋯ › Delete item should read `badges[v.key]`. If `shared || favourite || notes || pins` is true, open the house `ConfirmDialog` (already imported) and name what goes, for example: title "Delete V2?", message "V2 is on Kevin's link, with his favourite, 1 note and 2 pins. It moves to Deleted versions, where you can restore it." Otherwise keep the one-press delete with the snackbar Undo. `removeVersion` itself doesn't change.

2) Add a way back for deleted versions. A "Deleted versions (n)" entry should appear in the room ⋯ menu only when n > 0, reusing the Deleted-sheet pattern (`LibraryDeletedSheet` or the visualizer's own Deleted designs sheet). It lists `(versions[roomId] ?? []).filter(v => v.deleted)` with a thumb, the label and a Restore button that calls the existing `restoreVersion` and then `router.refresh()`. Don't add a new server action, and don't add Delete forever unless the owner asks for it.

3) Change the hint at line 629 so it no longer claims "nothing is lost". For example: "Deleted versions can be restored from the room menu." Log this as invented copy.

4) Optional, for consistency: have `fetchShare` in lib/visualizer/queries.ts check each snapshot key against the job's `deletedAt`, and mark deleted versions "No longer available" on the client page, or hide them. That stops the client leaving feedback the studio can't see. If this is skipped, the confirm must say the link keeps showing the version.

Log the new UI in REGISTER.md as user-directed / invented copy, add a Deleted-versions step to the UAT story, and add a probe (delete a shared V2 → the confirm names the favourite, notes and pins → Restore from Deleted versions → the badges come back).

kept.title: Present's version thumbs overflow the 280 px side column; the one on screen is often hidden and there is no scroll cue
kept.evidence: 11-present.png: presenting V3 shows thumbs Original, V1 and a clipped V2. V3, the selected one, is off-screen to the right with no scrollbar or fade. 12-present-original.png and 15-present-orig-compare.png show the same clipping.
kept.repro: Open Present on the latest version of a room with 3 or more versions.
kept.fix: dialogs.module.css `.thumbs`: lay the thumbs out as a wrapping grid (`display:grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr)`) in the side column, or at least scrollIntoView({ inline: 'nearest', block: 'nearest' }) the data-on thumb whenever `key` changes.
