verdict.reason: Reproduced in both the code and the screenshot. `.present` gives the side column a fixed 280px (`grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) 280px`), and `.thumbs` is a single flex row (`overflow-x: auto`) of 104px thumbs with fixed-width images. Only about 2.5 thumbs fit. present-dialog.tsx starts on `start` (the latest version) and never scrolls the `data-on` thumb into view. So with Original + V1…V3, the selected V3 is off-screen and V2 is cut off at the edge. 11-present.png shows exactly this: Original, V1 and a clipped V2, with no highlighted thumb visible. macOS overlay scrollbars hide the fact that the row scrolls, and nothing fades or hints at more thumbs. The side column has plenty of empty height below the row, so the one-row layout wastes space it already has. The active thumb only has `data-on` and no aria-current / aria-pressed. Severity stays minor: ← → and the arrows still move between versions, and the title names the current one.
verdict.fix:
1. components/visualizer/editor/dialogs/dialogs.module.css, desktop: make `.thumbs` a wrapping grid in the side column. Use `display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: var(--om-spacing-2); padding-top: var(--om-spacing-3);` and drop `overflow-x`; `.side` already scrolls vertically. Change `.thumb` to `min-width: 0` (drop `flex: 0 0 104px`) and `.thumb img` to `width: 100%; height: auto; aspect-ratio: 104 / 66`. Keep the existing box-shadow rings. Every version is then visible on open, whatever the count.
2. In the existing ≤1024 media query, where `.side` is capped at 180px: keep the thumbs as one horizontal row (`display: flex; overflow-x: auto`, `.thumb { flex: 0 0 104px }`).
3. components/visualizer/editor/dialogs/present-dialog.tsx: keep a ref on the thumbs container. In an effect keyed on `key`, find `[data-on]` and call `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline: 'nearest' })`. This covers the phone/tablet row and a long desktop list. The effect only touches the DOM and never calls setState, so it follows the house ESLint rule.
4. Add `aria-current={x.key === key ? 'true' : undefined}` on each thumb button. Also give it a real `aria-label` (e.g. 'Original' / `V${x.n} · ${descriptor}`), because the img has alt="".
No new UI. Verify at 1440 on the Kevin Ng living room (4 entries) and at 768 touch.

kept.title: Esc does nothing inside a pin's note or reply box (react-aria TextArea stops the key)
kept.where: Pin draft card and pin thread card
kept.evidence: s7.cjs: with the draft's textarea focused, Escape leaves [data-testid=viz-pin-draft] count at 1. s19.cjs: typing in a thread's Reply box and pressing Escape leaves the thread open. The card-level onKeyDown never sees the key, because the DS TextArea (react-aria) stops keyboard propagation, and the window handler bails out while typing.
kept.repro: Pin mode › click the photo › press Esc with the caret in the note box.
kept.fix: pin-card.tsx: handle Escape in the TextArea's own onKeyDown (call onCancel / onClose there) rather than on the wrapping div.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this by reading the code. I didn't check it on :3011, but the code leaves no room for doubt. In pin-card.tsx, both DraftPin (line 78) and PinThread (line 45) handle Escape in the wrapping div's onKeyDown. Each also passes its own onKeyDown to the DS TextArea (react-aria-components TextField), which wraps it with react-aria's createEventHandler. That wrapper calls e.stopPropagation() after the handler runs, unless the handler calls continuePropagation() (see node_modules/react-aria/dist/private/interactions/createEventHandler.js). So a key pressed inside the textarea never reaches the card's onKeyDown. The window handler in visualizer-editor.tsx (lines 502-506) returns early on `typing`, so it can't catch the key either. Pressing Esc with the caret in the note or reply box does nothing. The draft opens with autoFocus on its TextArea, so the caret is almost always there, which makes the draft card's Esc effectively dead. The same components are used on the client's share page (render-share-page.tsx:130-132), so clients hit it too. The severity is minor: the Cancel and Close buttons still work.
verdict.fix:
Fix it in components/visualizer/editor/pin-card.tsx, where one change covers both the editor and the share page. In each TextArea's onKeyDown, handle Escape next to the existing ⌘/Ctrl+Enter check:
- DraftPin: `if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.preventDefault(); onCancel(); return }`
- PinThread: `if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.preventDefault(); onClose(); return }`

Keep the wrapping div's Escape handler, because it still catches Esc while focus is on the card's buttons. react-aria already stops the key from propagating, so the textarea handler doesn't need its own stopPropagation, and the window handler's Esc chain in visualizer-editor.tsx won't also fire. Optionally, after the pin closes, return focus to the pin-mode toggle or the pin marker so keyboard users aren't left with focus on the body. No new UI or copy is needed.

To verify, press Esc in the draft's note and in a thread's Reply box, in both the editor and /share, and check that [data-testid=viz-pin-draft] or viz-pin-thread goes to 0. Then press Esc again and check that pin mode turns off, as the window chain does today.

kept.title: Pin mode gives no instruction, the surface markers stay live under it, and pinning works while Compare is on
kept.evidence: s7.cjs: after toggling Pin, the stage shows no banner (the place/draw modes have one). 40-pin-mode.png shows only the button state. s19.cjs: clicking a marker in pin mode selects the surface instead of dropping a pin (draft count 0). 46-pin-in-compare.png: with Compare on, a click on the V2 (before) half opens a draft that saves onto V3, and the existing pins are hidden.
kept.repro: Press Pin, then click a purple square; or turn on Compare and press Pin, then click the left half.
kept.fix: visualizer-editor.tsx: while `pinning`, empty `markers` and pass a banner to Stage ('Tap the photo where your note goes' + Cancel, the Stage banner pattern). Turn Compare off when pin mode starts, or disable Pin while comparing with a tooltip.

verdict.reason: The code confirms all three parts. (1) In stage.tsx the `banner` is built only for the place, draw and remove modes (lines ~90-92). A `pin` mode gets no banner, so the only sign pin mode is on is the pressed state of the push_pin button. (2) In visualizer-editor.tsx, `markers` (line ~186) is emptied for markersHidden, placing, sketch and readOnly, but not for `pinning`. Stage keeps rendering the dots, and a dot's onClick calls stopPropagation and then `onDot(m)` (outside remove mode). onFrameDown also returns early on `button`. So a tap on a marker in pin mode selects the surface or furniture and switches the tool mode instead of dropping a pin. (3) Pin mode and Compare don't exclude each other: `stageMode` becomes `pin` whenever `pinning && view`, and `compare.on` leaves it alone. Stage hides pins while comparing (`pins && !compare`) yet still sends the frame's pointerdown to `mode.onAdd`, so a tap on the before half makes a draft pin keyed to `view` (the after version) while the existing pins are hidden. The auditor's s7, s19 and s46 probes match this. Severity minor is fair: nothing breaks and nothing is lost, but a studio pinning a note to a client's render would be confused (no instruction, a tap that does something else, a note landing on the other version).
verdict.fix:
1. stage.tsx: give the pin mode a cancel callback, `{ kind: 'pin'; onAdd; onCancel }`. Add a branch to `banner`: `mode.kind === 'pin' ? { text: 'Tap the photo where your note goes', cancel: mode.onCancel }`. It reuses the existing motion banner and Cancel button, so no new UI. Also, as a safety net, don't render markers while `mode.kind === 'pin'`.
2. visualizer-editor.tsx: add `pinning` to the conditions that empty `markers` (`... || placing || sketch || pinning || readOnly ? []`). Pass `onCancel: () => { setPinning(false); setDraftPin(null) }` in the pin `stageMode`.
3. Make Pin and Compare exclude each other. The Pin toggle's onClick also calls `setCompare({ on: false, key: null })` when it turns pin mode on, and the Compare toggle (both the narrow IconButton and the desktop compareBtn) calls `setPinning(false); setDraftPin(null); setActivePin(null)` when it turns Compare on. Turning the other one off is better than disabling the button: it keeps both buttons live and matches how Escape already unwinds pinning, then compare.
4. Log a REG entry (bug fix + invented copy for the banner line). Extend the visualizer probe to check that the banner shows in pin mode, that no markers show in pin mode, and that Pin turns Compare off. Verify on :3011 at 1440 and 390.

kept.title: ← → change the version behind an open ⋯ / room / design menu
kept.evidence: s20.cjs: with V1's ⋯ menu open (focus on its first menuitem), ArrowLeft moved the canvas from 'V4 · Walls' to 'V3 · Relit · Golden Hour' while the menu stayed open (121-arrow-in-menu.png).
kept.repro: Open any version's ⋯ and press ← or →.
kept.fix: In keyRef's handler, return early when a menu is open (`if (menu) return`), or add `[role="menu"]` to the closest() exclusion list.

verdict.reason: The code confirms it. The window keydown handler (keyRef, visualizer-editor.tsx:501-522) only skips ← → when focus sits inside [role="slider"], [role="tablist"], [role="radiogroup"] or [role="listbox"]. It never checks the `menu` state (line 424), and it never excludes [role="menu"]. The ⋯ version menu, the room menu and the design menu are all PortalMenus with role="menu" (lines 669, 686, 692). None of them is aria-modal, so the early return for dialogs does not catch them. PortalMenu does not handle ArrowLeft or ArrowRight itself. So with any of these menus open, ← → calls setView behind it. The version menu then also changes meaning: its "Compare with the one on screen" and "Before and after" row depends on `mv.key !== viewKey`. This matches the auditor's screenshot. It is a small keyboard slip, not a data risk, so it stays minor.
verdict.fix: In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx, inside keyRef.current's ← → branch, add `!menu` to the condition. Also add `[role="menu"]` to the closest() exclusion list: `if ((e.key === 'ArrowLeft' || e.key === 'ArrowRight') && !menu && !e.metaKey && !e.ctrlKey && !e.altKey && !(t?.closest?.('[role="slider"], [role="tablist"], [role="radiogroup"], [role="listbox"], [role="menu"]')))`. Put the guard on the arrow branch only, not as a blanket early return, so Esc and ⌘Z keep their current behaviour. PortalMenu already closes itself on Escape. After the change, re-run the auditor's s20 check: open V1's ⋯, press ←, and the canvas should stay on the same version.

kept.title: Compare against a deleted parent shows the deleted version, while Present falls back to the Original
kept.where: Canvas Compare vs Present, after deleting a version's parent
kept.evidence: s6.cjs: after deleting V2, the canvas Compare on V3 still shows 'V2' as Before (32-compare-parent-deleted.png), a version no longer in the strip. Present's button for the same V3 reads 'Before and after · Original'.
kept.repro: Delete V2, show V3, then press Compare; open Present and read the footer button.
kept.fix: Resolve the before-key in one helper: walk parentKey up to the nearest live version, else Original. Use it in visualizer-editor.tsx (compareKey / parentLabel) and present-dialog.tsx.

verdict.reason: Confirmed from the code. In visualizer-editor.tsx, lines 106–107 define `all` as every version including soft-deleted ones and `live` as the non-deleted ones. The canvas Compare (line 232: `compareKey = compare.key ?? view.parentKey`, line 233: `beforeV = all.find(...)`) and the toolbar tooltip (line 576: `parentLabel` from `all.find`) both look in `all`. So with V2 deleted, V3's Before is still V2's image and the label reads "V2", a version the strip no longer shows. Present gets `versions={live...}` (line 718). In present-dialog.tsx, line 27 (`list.find(parentKey) ?? list[0]`) misses the deleted V2 and falls back to list[0], the Original, so its button reads "Before and after · Original". The same V3 compares against two different befores depending on the surface. Neither surface climbs to the nearest live ancestor. Present jumps straight to the Original even when V1, the grandparent, is still live. And if there is no Original, `list[0]` is simply the first version. I didn't need a live run because the code paths are unambiguous and match the auditor's screenshot description. It is a minor consistency issue: nothing breaks, but a studio presenting to a client sees a different "before" than it saw on the canvas.
verdict.fix:
1. Add a pure helper to lib/visualizer/model.ts: `beforeKeyOf(v: VersionView, all: VersionView[]): string`. It walks `parentKey` through `all`, skipping deleted versions, until it reaches a live version or ORIGINAL, and guards against cycles with a seen-set.
2. In visualizer-editor.tsx:
   - line 232: use `compare.key ?? beforeKeyOf(view, all)`.
   - line 233: keep the lookup in `all` but resolve to a live version (or use `live`).
   - line 576: derive `parentLabel` from the same resolved key.
3. In present-dialog.tsx:
   - Either pass the full list (or a `beforeKey` resolver) from the editor, or apply the same walk over `versions` plus the original.
   - Replace the `?? list[0]` fallback with an explicit ORIGINAL entry, so the button and the CompareSlider labels agree with the canvas.
No new UI and no copy change.

kept.title: Room rename accepts a name another room already has, and cuts long names at 60 characters without saying so
kept.evidence: s10.cjs: renaming Kitchen to 'Living room' leaves two 'Living room' chips. A 74-character name became '…counter that go', cut mid-word (62-renamed-long.png). addRoom de-duplicates names; renameRoom (cleanName(name, 60)) doesn't.
kept.repro: Rename Kitchen to 'Living room'; rename it to a very long name.
kept.fix: renameRoom: refuse a name another live room in the design uses ({ error: 'There’s already a room called Living room' }). Give the rename TextField maxLength 60 with the house counter.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed both halves by reading the code, without running anything on the live server. In app/visualizer/actions.ts, `renameRoom` (line 151) only calls `cleanName(name, 60)` and writes the result. It never checks the other live rooms in the design, although `addRoom` (lines 140–143) de-duplicates names against them. So renaming Kitchen to "Living room" leaves two "Living room" chips.

The rename dialog in visualizer-editor.tsx (line 721) passes no `maxLength` to `TextField`. `saveRename` (line 459) puts the full untrimmed name into the chip straight away. The server then keeps only the first 60 characters, and `router.refresh()` swaps the chip to the cut name with no message. That is the mid-word "…counter that go" the auditor saw.

The design rename has the same silent cut at 80 characters (`renameDesign` uses `cleanName`'s default of 80), so the fix should cover it too. The finding's "house counter" doesn't exist: `TextField` has `maxLength` but no character counter, so the fix should use only `maxLength` and not add a new counter.
verdict.fix:
1. In `renameRoom` (app/visualizer/actions.ts), load the design's live rooms with the same query `addRoom` uses (`designId` matches and `deletedAt` is null, excluding this room). Compare names ignoring case after `cleanName`. If another room has the name, return `{ error: 'There’s already a room called ${n}.' }`. If the name hasn't changed, return `ok` without a write.
2. In visualizer-editor.tsx, give the rename `TextField` `maxLength={rename?.kind === 'room' ? 60 : 80}`, matching the server caps, so a long name can't be typed and is never cut silently.
3. Check for a duplicate name in the browser too, against `ed.rooms`. Show the message through the field's own error state (TextField's error, as the house forms do) and keep the dialog open. Don't use only a snackbar or make the optimistic write.
4. Keep the existing rule of putting the old name back if the server refuses.
5. Keep the dialog's current rule: it closes only once the save lands.

kept.title: Back loses the gallery folder, and 'Open the lead' doesn't carry ?from= (REG-465)
kept.where: Top bar Back; design menu › Open the lead
kept.evidence: s18.cjs: opening 'Showroom — kitchen concept' from /visualizer?folder=lf-visualizer-showroom gives ?from=%2Fvisualizer, and Back lands on /visualizer (the root, not the folder). s11.cjs: Open the lead goes to /leads/1f12… with no from, so the lead's Back says 'Leads' instead of returning to the design.
kept.repro: Gallery › Showroom ideas › open the design › Back. Separately, Kevin Ng's design › ⋮ › Open the lead.
kept.fix: visualizer-home.tsx `open`: use withFrom(`/visualizer/${id}`, current pathname + search). visualizer-editor.tsx: router.push(withFrom(`/leads/${id}`, here())).

verdict.reason: I confirmed this from the code and did not run it on the live server. In visualizer-home.tsx:47 and :59, `open` and `forLead` always pass `withFrom(..., '/visualizer')`. LibraryGallery keeps the open folder in `?folder=` (library-gallery.tsx:160, REG-664), so the folder is dropped from `from` and the editor's Back (visualizer-editor.tsx:96, `back = from ?? '/visualizer'`) lands on the gallery root. 'Open the lead' pushes a bare `/leads/${id}` with no `from` in two places: the editor's design menu (visualizer-editor.tsx:693) and the home card kebab (visualizer-home.tsx:122). The lead page reads `readFrom(sp.from)` and `fromLabel` already maps `/visualizer` to 'AI Visualizer', so the missing `from` is the only reason the lead's Back says Leads. The editor already has `here()` and uses it for the Files and quote snackbars, so this is an oversight against REG-465. It is minor because nothing breaks, but a studio would notice it after filing designs into folders.
verdict.fix: In components/visualizer/home/visualizer-home.tsx, read the gallery's own URL (`usePathname()` + `useSearchParams()`, or `window.location.pathname + search` at press time as the editor's `here()` does). Pass it as `from` in `open`, `forLead` and the sample flow, so `?folder=` rides along. Also give the card kebab's 'Open the lead' `withFrom(`/leads/${t.d.leadId}`, here)`. In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:693, change it to `router.push(withFrom(`/leads/${data.lead!.id}`, here()))`. The lead's L2 Back then reads 'AI Visualizer' through the existing `fromLabel`. No new UI is needed.

kept.title: Delete design lands on the gallery with no Undo snackbar
kept.evidence: s11.cjs: after confirming, the page lands on /visualizer and the snackbar host is empty ([class*=snack] text ''). Restore is only possible by reopening the design (73-deleted-design.png) or through Deleted designs. Room, version and pin deletes all offer Undo.
kept.repro: Personal design › ⋮ › Delete design › Delete.
kept.fix: After router.push(back), raise the house snackbar '{name} deleted' with Undo → restoreDesigns([id]) (the snackbar host lives in the shell and survives the navigation).

verdict.reason:
The gap is real, but the suggested fix wouldn't work. In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:469-473, removeDesign calls deleteDesigns and then router.push(back). It raises no snackbar. Deleting a room, a version or a pin in the same file (lines 447, 454, 495) each offers Undo, so the missing Undo is a real inconsistency.

The suggested fix assumes the snackbar host survives the navigation, and it doesn't. The editor lives under app/(editor)/visualizer/[designId], and app/(editor)/layout.tsx wraps it in its own SnackbarProvider. The gallery /visualizer sits in AppShell's separate SnackbarProvider. A snack raised before router.push would unmount with the (editor) layout and never show on the gallery.

The house already has a pattern for this (REG-634). The contract template editor pushes `/company/templates/contracts?deleted=<id>`. contract-templates-gallery.tsx:37-46 reads `deleted` once, strips it with router.replace, and raises '{title} deleted' with Undo → restore. The visualizer should follow the same pattern. Severity minor stands: a studio can still restore from Deleted designs or the in-editor banner.

kept.title: Present focus drops to <body> at the first or last version, and 'Show it alone' stays pressed but disabled on the Original
kept.evidence: s3.cjs: after pressing Next to reach V3, the Next button unmounts and document.activeElement is BODY. With Before and after on, stepping to the Original leaves the footer button reading 'Show it alone' while disabled (15-present-orig-compare.png).
kept.repro: Present › press the › button until the end; separately turn on Before and after and click the Original thumb.
kept.fix: present-dialog.tsx: keep both nav buttons mounted and set them disabled at the ends. Reset `compare` to false when the current item has no parent.

verdict.reason:
Both issues are real, and you can see them straight from the code. In present-dialog.tsx (lines 47–48) the Previous and Next buttons are only rendered when `i > 0` or `i < list.length - 1`. Pressing Next onto the last version removes the button that has focus, so focus falls to <body>. The same happens with Previous on the Original. After that, Tab starts again from the top of the dialog. Separately, `compare` is never reset. On an item with no parent (the Original), the stage falls back to the plain image because it renders `compare && parent`. But the footer label uses `compare` alone, so it reads "Show it alone" on a disabled button, even though no comparison is showing. That label is wrong. A studio doing a live demo with the keyboard would notice both. It is a minor a11y and polish issue, not a blocker. I did not re-run it live because the code path is unambiguous.

The auditor's fix needs two changes. (1) A plain native `disabled` on a focused button still drops focus to body in Chromium, so keeping the buttons mounted is only half the fix. (2) Forcing `compare` to false loses the user's chosen mode as they walk through the versions. Anyone going Original → V1 → V2 in Before and after would have to switch it back on each time. Deriving the label keeps the mode on and makes the label honest.
verdict.fix:
Changes are in components/visualizer/editor/dialogs/present-dialog.tsx only.
(1) Keep both nav spans mounted at every index. At an end, pass `aria-disabled={true}` and `tabIndex={-1}` only if the button is not focused, or simply keep it focusable. Make its onClick a no-op there (`if (i === 0) return`). Dim it with a `[aria-disabled]` rule in the dialog's module CSS: opacity at the DS disabled level, `cursor: default`, and no hover wash. Don't use native `disabled`, because it blurs the focused element. The ← / → handler already clamps, so it doesn't change. If you'd rather not show an inert chevron, the alternative is to leave the conditional rendering and, in the onClick that reaches an end, move focus to the opposite nav button with a ref after the key changes.
(2) Don't reset `compare`. Compute `const showing = compare && !!parent` and use it for both the stage (already effectively the case) and the label: `showing ? 'Show it alone' : \`Before and after${parent ? ' · …' : ''}\``. The Original then reads "Before and after" (disabled), and the comparison comes back when the user steps on to a version that has a parent.

kept.title: Moodboard wallpaper swatch shows a different motif, and a different scale in print, from the one on the wall
kept.evidence: 93-mood-wallpaper.png: the render's walls carry scattered leaves, but the swatch shows interlocking circles. In the PDF (93-mood-wallpaper-pdf.png) the swatch is a 2×2 blow-up of large petals, because patternCss uses px tiles that scale differently in print.
kept.repro: Generate Walls → Tropical Botanical, then ⋯ › Moodboard, then print or save as PDF.
kept.fix: Draw the moodboard chip from the same tile the engine paints (lib/visualizer/patterns.ts: render the tile to a canvas and use it as a data-URL background) so motif and scale match on screen and in print.

verdict.reason:
This is real, and the cause is in the code. lib/visualizer/patterns.ts draws each wallpaper twice, in two unrelated ways. patternCss() makes the chip picture: for 'botanical' it lays two crossed radial-gradient ellipses (5×11 and 11×5) on a 22px grid, which reads as interlocking circles or crosses. patternTile() makes what the engine paints on the wall: four rotated leaf ellipses with a midrib per tile, which reads as scattered leaves. The moodboard chip goes through chipCss() → patternCss() (moodboard-dialog.tsx:63), so it cannot match the wall.

The screenshots show both problems:
- On screen (93-mood-wallpaper.png), the wall has diagonal leaves and the swatch has a green interlocking-circle lattice.
- In the PDF (93-mood-wallpaper-pdf.png), the swatch becomes a 2×2 blow-up of large petals. Chrome's print rasteriser handles the multi-layer px-sized gradient differently, so motif and scale both drift.

The same patternCss mismatch also reaches the picker chips (surfaces-panel.tsx:47 and everything else that uses chipCss), so it is not limited to the moodboard. Other motifs differ too: 'deco' is gold rings on black on the wall but base-coloured rings in the chip, and 'floral' is five petals on the wall but dot pairs in the chip.

This is a minor, visual issue, but a studio would notice it: the moodboard is the printout handed to the client, and its swatch should show the wallpaper that is on the wall.
verdict.fix:
Make patternTile the single source for the swatch picture.

1. In lib/visualizer/patterns.ts, add a browser-only `patternUrl(p, base, t = 48)`:
   - It calls patternTile(), puts the Img into an offscreen canvas (putImageData) and returns canvas.toDataURL('image/png').
   - It memoises the result in a Map keyed by kind|accent|base.
   - When `document` is undefined (server render), it returns null.
2. In lib/visualizer/materials.ts, have chipCss (and the surfaces-panel.tsx:47 call, via chipCss) use `url("<data>") 0 0 / <cssPx>px <cssPx>px repeat, <base>` when patternUrl returns a URL, and fall back to the existing patternCss otherwise.
   - Pick cssPx so the chip shows roughly the same number of repeats as a wall tile does at the render's scale, about 2–3 tiles across a 150px chip.
   - A bitmap tile scales the same in print as on screen, so the PDF keeps the motif and the scale.
3. In the moodboard stylesheet, add `print-color-adjust: exact` to the chip if it is not already there.

Keep patternCss only as the server/SSR fallback, or retire it once every chip is client-rendered. No new UI.

Verify at 1440 on Walls → Tropical Botanical → Moodboard, both on screen and with page.pdf(). Also check Deco and Floral chips in the material picker.

kept.title: Printed moodboard puts the render in a grey box with big empty bands
kept.evidence: 21-mood-pdf.png (A4 landscape via page.pdf with body[data-print-board]): the picture sits mid-way in a tall surface-variant grey panel, with about a third of the page grey above and below. It prints on one page.
kept.repro: Moodboard › Print or save as PDF.
kept.fix: moodboard.module.css @media print: `.picture { background: none; align-self: start; }` and let the image take its natural height.

verdict.reason: This is real, and it's polish. In `moodboard.module.css`, the print rule makes `.board` `position: fixed; inset: 0` as a grid on the whole page. The default grid stretch makes `.picture` as tall as the page. `.picture` keeps its screen styling, a `--om-color-surface-bg` fill with the image centred and `object-fit: contain`. So a landscape render ends up letterboxed inside a full-height grey panel. The auditor's `21-mood-pdf.png` shows this: about a third of the page is grey above the render and the same below. The side column sits at the top, so the two columns don't line up. On screen the grey stage is fine, because it frames the dialog. It only looks wrong on paper.

kept.title: Snackbars sit on top of the versions strip's labels
kept.evidence: 30-deleted-v2.png and 141-changed-photo.png: 'V2 deleted · Undo' and 'Photo changed…' cover the Original/V1 tiles' captions.
kept.repro: Delete a version or change a room's photo.
kept.fix: Lift the snackbar above the strip in the editor frame (an offset variable the snack host reads, as the template editor does for its bottom bar).

verdict.reason: I reproduced it from the code and from 30-deleted-v2.png. The house snackbar host (components/om/snackbar.module.css) is fixed at `left: calc(var(--rail-w, 52px) + 32px); bottom: calc(24px + var(--bottom-dock, 0px))`. The visualizer editor is a `position: fixed; inset: 0` frame and never sets `--bottom-dock`. So the 344×48 bar sits at x 84–428, 24px from the bottom, right on the versions strip. In the screenshot "V2 deleted · Undo" covers the "Original · the photo" and "V1 · Japandi" captions and the bottom of both thumbnails, which are the tiles the user may want next. The Undo still works, so this is polish. One part of the finding is wrong: the template editor has no snackbar offset to copy (grep finds no `--bottom-dock` or offset in components/templates). The house mechanism is the review banner's (components/leads/review-banner.tsx, REG-302): a ResizeObserver writes `--bottom-dock` on the document root, and the snackbar and bulk bars already read it. The finding's fix also has a catch. Lifting the bar only by the strip's height (about 113px) puts it at y ≈ 839–887, which overlaps the centred canvas toolbar (x ≈ 318–748, y ≈ 830–876) where they share x 318–428. The lift has to clear that toolbar too.
verdict.fix: Reuse the house offset instead of adding a new variable. In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx, add an effect like review-banner.tsx's: a ResizeObserver on the editor's `.main` column (and on the window's resize) writes `--bottom-dock` on `document.documentElement`, and the cleanup removes the property. The value is `innerHeight - top` of the canvas toolbar (`[role=toolbar][aria-label=Canvas]`, the top of the versions strip when that toolbar is hidden) `- 24 + 8`, so the snackbar rests 8px above the toolbar and clear of the strip. At ≤1024 (`data-narrow`), measure the top of the strip / go bar / tray instead, so the bar also clears the dock and tray. Nothing else changes: the snackbar's existing `transition: bottom` animates the lift, and the visualizer's own `.fab` class sets its own `bottom`, so the FAB doesn't move. No CSS edit is needed in editor.module.css; the change is one effect in the orchestrator. Verify at 1440 (delete V2, change a photo) and at 768/390 touch.

kept.title: Change photo has no Undo and clears the room's picks
kept.where: Room options › Change photo (a room with no versions)
kept.evidence: s22.cjs: after picking a new photo, the snackbar reads 'Photo changed — its surfaces are marked again' with only close, and pending is reset with history:false.
kept.repro: Add a sample room, then ⋯ › Change photo › pick a JPG.
kept.fix: Keep the previous imageUrl and detection and offer Undo (setRoomPhoto back to them), or confirm before replacing when the room has picks.

verdict.reason:
The code does what the finding says. In `changePhoto` (`components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx` around lines 363–373), a successful `setRoomPhoto` replaces the detection. It then calls `ed.setPending(roomId, () => emptyPending(), { history: false })`, which drops every waiting pick (materials, furniture, style, reference, lighting) outside the editor's undo history. The snackbar is `snack({ message: 'Photo changed — its surfaces are marked again' })` with no action.

Undo is harder than the finding's fix suggests. `setRoomPhoto` in `app/visualizer/actions.ts` (lines 169–176) also clears `sampleKey`, `sourceFileId` and `stateJson` on the server. Calling `setRoomPhoto` again with the old `imageUrl` and detection would not bring the room back. A sample room would lose its `sampleKey`, and with it Remove, Empty the room and the sketch pass, which only work on samples. The saved picks would stay gone too.

The menu does gate the action on the room having no versions, so no renders are lost. The loss is limited to the picks waiting for Generate and to the room's sample status. That is still a silent, unrecoverable loss from one misclick, and it breaks the house rule that a remove answers with Undo (REG-542). Polish is the right severity. I did not check it on :3012; the code path is plain.
verdict.fix:
Give Change photo an Undo that restores the whole room row.

1. In `app/visualizer/actions.ts`, have `setRoomPhoto` read the row first and return the old columns: `{ ok: true, prior: { originalImageUrl, sampleKey, sourceFileId, detectionJson, stateJson } }`. Add `undoRoomPhoto(roomId, prior)`. It writes those columns back under the same guard (refuse if a live render now exists), then calls `touch`.
2. In `components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx` `changePhoto`, capture the old detection (`ed` / `reading`) and `pending` before the swap. Show the snackbar with the house Undo action: `snack({ message: 'Photo changed — its surfaces are marked again', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: … } })`. The action calls `undoRoomPhoto`, restores the old detection and pending with `history: false`, and calls `router.refresh()`. If the undo is refused, name what failed with the sweep's `Couldn’t …` wording.

A lighter alternative is to open the house `ConfirmDialog` before the file picker, only when the room has picks. It would read, for example, "Change the photo? Your n picks for this room will be cleared." The Undo path is still better because it also restores a sample room's `sampleKey`, and the confirm cannot.

kept.title: On a phone the client cannot post a pin: the draft card's 'Pin it' button is clipped under the photo, and pin threads are cut to one line
kept.evidence: 70-client-phone-draft.png: the draft card runs past the photo's bottom edge and its footer ('Your designer…', Cancel, Pin it) is cut off. Measured in s26.cjs: media box y 246→467 with overflow:hidden, 'Pin it' box y 466.9→502.9, and document.elementFromPoint at its centre returns the 'Before and after' button underneath. 69-client-phone-thread.png: the thread body shows 24px of 126px ('Walnut sample is at the showroom —' is cut off) because the reply box takes the space.
kept.repro: Open /renders/17fe84ab2eca47 at 390×844 (isMobile, hasTouch) → Pin a note → tap the photo → type a note → try to tap Pin it (the tap lands on Before and after). Tap pin 1 and try to read the note.
kept.fix: In components/visualizer/share/render-share-page.tsx, render DraftPin and PinThread outside the clipped .media box when (max-width:767px), as a bottom sheet the way the house phone rule does menus and popovers (REG-353), or at least as an in-flow card under the photo. Keep only the numbered dot on the picture. Alternatively remove overflow:hidden from .media in render-share-page.module.css and clamp place() in pin-card.tsx to the card's height. Check at 390 and 320.

verdict.reason:
I reproduced it from the code and the auditor's screenshots. I did not re-run it live.

- **Why it clips:** `.media` in `render-share-page.module.css` has `overflow: hidden` and `aspect-ratio: 3/2`. At 390 wide the photo is about 332×221 px. `PinThread` and `DraftPin` are absolutely positioned inside it, so they can never draw past its edge.
- **Draft card (70-client-phone-draft.png):** `place()` in `pin-card.tsx` clamps `top` to `calc(100% - 120px)` whatever the card's real height. The draft card is about 200 px tall (the DS TextArea with its label, plus a footer row), so its footer lands below the photo's edge. The hint text, Cancel and Pin it are cut off, and a tap there lands on "Before and after". A client on a phone cannot post a pin at all, and that is the shared link's core ask ("pin a note on anything you'd change"). Blocker stands.
- **Thread card (69-client-phone-thread.png):** `max-height: calc(100% - 16px)` is about 205 px. The head (about 52 px) and the fixed footer (a 56 px reply box plus the Reply button, about 125 px) leave the body roughly 24 px. The note shows one clipped line: "Walnut sample is at the showroom —".
- **Same bug in the studio editor:** `visualizer-editor.tsx` (lines 601 and 604) renders the same two cards over the editor's photo, so it very likely clips there on a phone too. The fix belongs in `pin-card.tsx` so both pages get it.

The auditor's second option (drop `overflow: hidden` and clamp `place()`) would only move the overlap onto the buttons under the photo. The house phone rule (REG-353) is that anchored surfaces become bottom sheets, and `components/om/sheet.tsx` already provides one.
verdict.fix:
In `components/visualizer/editor/pin-card.tsx`, branch on `useSheetLayout()` from `components/om/sheet.tsx`, following REG-353.

1. **Phone (≤767):** wrap the card's content (the head, or a "New pin" title for the draft, plus body and footer) in the house `Sheet`, rendered through its portal. It brings the scrim, Esc, focus handling and scroll lock. `onClose` / `onCancel` close the sheet.
2. **Keep the marker on the photo:** leave `DraftPin`'s `.draftDot` and the numbered `.pin` on the picture so the client still sees where the note points.
3. **Unclip the phone card:** inside the sheet, drop `place()` and the absolute position. The card goes `position: static; width: 100%; max-height: none`, with the body scrolling inside the sheet's own height cap.
4. **Desktop:** keep the anchored card. Also tighten `place()` so the vertical clamp uses the card's height: set `max-height` from the room left beside the pin, or anchor the card from the bottom when a fixed 120 px would overflow.
5. **Share page:** no layout change is needed in `render-share-page.tsx` or `render-share-page.module.css`. The studio editor's phone layout is fixed by the same component change.

Verify at 390×844 and 320 with isMobile and hasTouch:
- Draft pin: Pin it can be hit and saves.
- Thread: the full note and its replies can be read, and Reply can be hit.
- At 1440 the output is byte-identical.

kept.title: Deleting a design promises 'Shared links stop working', but the client's link stays open and still accepts notes
kept.evidence: The confirm reads 'Its rooms and versions go to Deleted designs… Shared links stop working.' After confirming (s20.cjs), /renders/17fe84ab2eca47 still rendered the full page ('Open until 2 Oct ’26 / FOR KEVIN / 3 design ideas…', 59-client-after-delete.png). A note sent from it succeeded ('Sent — your designer will see it') and notified the lead's members with a link to the deleted design. In code, fetchShare (lib/visualizer/queries.ts:178) and openLink (app/renders/actions.ts) never read visualizer_designs.deleted_at.
kept.repro: Kevin Ng's design with a live link → ⋮ Design options → Delete design → Delete → open /renders/<token> in another tab → Leave a note → Send.
kept.fix: In fetchShare, join visualizer_designs and return state 'stopped' while d.deletedAt is set (Restore brings the link back). Apply the same check in openLink in app/renders/actions.ts so every client action is refused. Also make stampShareView skip it.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this by reading the code. I skipped the live repro because deleting a design would change the shared :3011 DB.

- `deleteDesigns` (app/visualizer/actions.ts:104-113) only sets `visualizer_designs.deleted_at`. It never touches `render_share_links`.
- `fetchShare` (lib/visualizer/queries.ts:178-194) decides the link's state from `s.revokedAt` and `s.expiresAt` alone, so the /renders/[token] page (force-dynamic) keeps drawing the full design.
- `openLink` (app/renders/actions.ts:20-25) applies the same two checks. So `pickFavourite`, `leaveNote`, `askCallBack`, `clientPin` and `clientReply` all still go through.
- `tell()` then notifies the lead's members with an href to the deleted design.

This breaks the confirm dialog's promise "Shared links stop working" (visualizer-editor.tsx:723). A client can keep writing to a design the studio has binned. Only Delete forever stops the link, because the rows cascade.

`stampShareView` is only called once the page's state is 'open', so fixing `fetchShare` covers it too. Severity major is right: the product breaks a promise it states outright, and client input reaches a deleted record.

One more wrinkle: line 74 brings a lead's deleted design back when someone opens it. With the fix below, that also reopens its links, which is consistent with "Restore brings it back".
verdict.fix:
Treat a deleted design as a stopped link in both read paths. Leave `revoked_at` alone, so Restore brings the links back as the dialog implies.

1. lib/visualizer/queries.ts `fetchShare`: after loading `s`, fetch the design's `deletedAt`: `db.select({ deletedAt: visualizerDesigns.deletedAt }).from(visualizerDesigns).where(eq(visualizerDesigns.id, s.designId))`. Then compute state as `s.revokedAt || design?.deletedAt ? 'stopped' : expired ? 'expired' : 'open'`. The page already renders `RenderLinkClosed state="stopped"`, and it skips `stampShareView` for any state other than 'open', so no new UI or copy is needed.
2. app/renders/actions.ts `openLink`: apply the same design lookup and return null when `deletedAt` is set, so every client action is refused. The existing message says the link has expired, which is acceptable; better still, return the stopped wording that `RenderLinkClosed` uses.
3. app/visualizer/actions.ts `deleteDesigns` / `restoreDesigns`: add `revalidatePath('/renders', 'layout')`, or revalidate each link's token, for tidiness. The page is force-dynamic, so this is optional.

Verify: delete Kevin Ng's design, open /renders/<token> and expect the stopped screen; confirm `leaveNote` returns an error; restore and confirm the link reopens. Make sure the probe restores the DB afterwards.

kept.title: 'Delete forever' on a design breaks the renders saved in the lead's Files › Renders and erases its Activity history
kept.where: Lead › Files › Renders after AI Visualizer › Deleted Designs › Delete Forever
kept.evidence: 80-renders-after-purge.png: 'Render - Kitchen - V3.jpg' (an engine render saved with Save to Files) shows a broken image. Its src /visualizer/img/v/a04f125b…/1 has naturalWidth 0 because render_jobs cascaded away. Every AI Visualizer line also vanished from the lead's Activity, which is derived from those tables (render_jobs count = 0 after the purge). The confirm (79-deleted-row.png) only says 'The design will be removed permanently' and doesn't mention the lead's files or history.
kept.repro: Generate a version (Describe a change → Generate) → ⋮ → Save to Files → Delete design → /visualizer ⋮ → Deleted Designs → Delete Forever → open the lead's Files › Renders.
kept.fix: In app/visualizer/actions.ts fileVersion, when the variant image is a data: URL, copy it into lead_file_images (REG-684's table) and set thumb to /files/img/<fileId>, so a saved file owns its picture. Backfill the existing rows in repair. Word the Delete Forever confirm for a lead's design to say the client's answers and Activity lines go with it, or keep render_jobs rows the lead references.

verdict.reason: The code path confirms it. `fileVersion` in app/visualizer/actions.ts (lines 253–261) inserts the lead_files row with `thumb: renderUrl(jobId, v)`. For any engine render, meaning a data: URL, `renderUrl` (line 242) gives `/visualizer/img/v/<jobId>/<variantId>`. That route (app/visualizer/img/[...key]/route.ts) reads the picture back out of `render_jobs.variants_json` and returns 404 once the job row is gone. `deleteDesignsForever` (lines 119–125) hard-deletes visualizer_designs, and the schema cascades to project_rooms → render_jobs → render_annotations, and to render_share_links → consultation requests. So every render saved with Save to Files, or through Share with client (createShareLink also calls fileVersion), becomes a broken image in the lead's Files › Renders. The file row itself survives, so the studio sees a file it can't open. Sample renders stored as public paths keep working, since thumb is the path itself, so only real generated renders break. That is the case that matters. The Activity half is also real: the visualizer branch of lib/leads/activity.ts (lines 53–61, 121–131) is derived only from render_jobs, render_share_links, render_annotations and consultation requests. After a purge the lead's history of what was rendered and shared, and what the client answered, vanishes without a trace. Other purges in the product leave a lead_events line instead (the REG-613 pattern, e.g. comparison_deleted, contract_archived). I did not re-run the live repro because the code is unambiguous and the server is shared. Severity is major: a client-facing file the studio deliberately kept is silently destroyed by an action whose confirm doesn't mention it.
verdict.fix:
1. app/visualizer/actions.ts `fileVersion`: when `v.imageUrl` starts with `data:`, insert `{ fileId: id, data: v.imageUrl }` into `leadFileImages` (the REG-684 table; files-actions.ts:72 already does this for uploads). Then set `thumb: /files/img/${id}` so the saved file owns its picture. Keep `thumb = v.imageUrl` for public-path samples.
2. scripts/repair-demo-data.ts, as a new idempotent rule: for each live lead_files row whose thumb matches `/visualizer/img/v/<job>/<variant>`, read the variant's data URL from render_jobs. Copy it into lead_file_images if no row exists yet, and repoint thumb to `/files/img/<fileId>`. Add a verification query that counts zero files still pointing at /visualizer/img/v/. Then run `db:baseline`.
3. Keep the history: in `deleteDesignsForever`, for a design with a leadId, write one `logLeadEvent` (lib/leads/events.ts, following the REG-613 pattern, e.g. `design_deleted`, "{who} deleted the AI Visualizer design '{name}' for good"). Add its line in the events branch of lib/leads/activity.ts. Don't keep the orphaned render_jobs rows.
4. components/visualizer/home/visualizer-home.tsx (the Delete Forever confirm on the house ConfirmDialog): for a lead's design, add one line saying that renders saved to the lead's Files stay, and that the client's pins and replies on shared links go with the design. Log the copy as invented copy in REGISTER.md.
Verify: save a render → Delete Forever → Files › Renders still shows the image (naturalWidth > 0), and Activity shows the deletion line.

kept.title: The client's view count is inflated: every like, note or pin counts as two more opens
kept.where: /renders/[token] → the Shared before list and Activity
kept.evidence: The s13.cjs readings of view_count: 2 before the visit, 3 after opening, 5 after one like, 7 after a second like, 9 after a note, 11 after a pin. The studio then sees 'opened 14×' in Shared before (51-shared-before.png) and 'Kevin Ng opened the shared renders (14 times)' in Activity. Cause: app/renders/[token]/page.tsx calls stampShareView during the server render, and each client action both revalidates the path and calls router.refresh(). The studio previewing its own link counts too.
kept.repro: Note the view_count of a link → open /renders/<token> → press I like this one → Leave a note → re-read view_count.
kept.fix: Move the stamp out of the page render. Use a small client component that calls stampShareView once per browser session on mount (sessionStorage key om.renders.seen.<token>), and skip it when a studio session is present. Drop the router.refresh() calls that duplicate the action's revalidatePath, or keep only one.

verdict.reason: The code confirms it, so I didn't need a live run. `app/renders/[token]/page.tsx:26` calls `await stampShareView(token)` on every server render of the page, and `stampShareView` (`app/renders/actions.ts:103`) adds 1 to `viewCount` each time without checking for a repeat. Every client action on the page (`pickFavourite`, `leaveNote`, `clientPin`, `clientReply`, `askCallBack`) ends in `refresh(s)`, which calls `revalidatePath('/renders/<token>')`. A server action that revalidates the current page makes Next send back a fresh render of that page, which is one stamp. Then `render-share-page.tsx` calls `router.refresh()` after each action (lines 36, 101, 111, 131, 177), which renders the page again for a second stamp. That makes +2 per action, which matches the auditor's readings (3 → 5 → 7 → 9 → 11). The inflated number reaches the studio in two places: the share dialog's "opened N×" (`share-dialog.tsx:121`) and Activity's "(N times)" (`lib/leads/activity.ts:136`). Both are what a designer uses to judge interest before a follow-up call, so "major" is fair. The contracts signing page does it differently: it stamps only once, guarded by `!viewedAt` (`app/sign/[id]/page.tsx:26`). One part of the proposed fix does not work in this prototype: "skip it when a studio session is present". The session is the `members.is_you` row and is always there, so the server cannot tell a studio preview from a client opening the link. I'm leaving that part out.
verdict.fix:
1. Take the stamp out of the render. Remove `await stampShareView(token)` from `app/renders/[token]/page.tsx`.
2. Stamp once from the browser. In `components/visualizer/share/render-share-page.tsx`, add a mount effect inside `RenderSharePage` that reads the sessionStorage key `om.renders.seen.<token>` (wrapped in try/catch). When the key is absent, set it and call `stampShareView(data.token)`, which becomes a plain exported server action with no `revalidatePath`. If storage throws, stamp anyway, once per mount. No setState happens in the effect, so the react-hooks rule is respected.
3. Keep the counts fresh for the studio. `stampShareView` should call `revalidatePath` for `/visualizer/<designId>` and the lead layout only, never `/renders/<token>`. Otherwise the stamp itself makes the client's page render again.
4. Drop the duplicate re-render. Remove the `router.refresh()` calls at lines 36, 101, 111, 131 and 177, because each action's `revalidatePath` already refreshes the current page. After step 1, a re-render no longer counts as a view either way.
5. The studio's own preview is out of scope. There is no separate studio session to test for, so no preview flag.
6. Check it on :3011 with a scratch DB: note `view_count`, open the link (+1), like, note, pin and reload in the same tab (all +0), then open it in a new context (+1).

kept.title: 'Open in AI Visualizer' on a render in Files adds a new room made from the render, instead of opening that version
kept.where: Lead › Files › Renders · grid / list / file viewer menu
kept.evidence: From the viewer of 'Render - Living room - V2.jpg' → ⋮ → Open in AI Visualizer, the editor created a sixth room 'Render Living room V2' with 0 versions whose Original is the V2 render (12-render-open.png; DB row project_rooms 63c1c5f7… source_file_id 435c4ace…). The grid and list menus offer the same item on every render (17-list-menu.png). Because leadImages includes Renders, Add room › From the lead's files also lists renders as site photos.
kept.repro: Lead Kevin Ng › Files › Renders → ⋮ on Render - Living room - V2.jpg → Open in AI Visualizer.
kept.fix: Record the version on the file when saving: add lead_files.render_key (jobId:variantId), written by fileVersion. In lead-files.tsx and file-viewer.tsx, a file with a render_key opens /visualizer/<design>?room=<roomId>&v=<key> (the editor selects that version) and is labelled 'Open this version in AI Visualizer'. Exclude files with a render_key from EditorData.leadImages in lib/visualizer/queries.ts.

verdict.reason:
The code path confirms it. `fileVersion` (app/visualizer/actions.ts:253) files a render as a plain `kind: 'image'` lead_files row in Renders and does not record which job or variant it came from. Files › grid / list (`visualize={f.kind === 'image'}`, files-grid.tsx:176/208, files-table.tsx:248) and the viewer kebab (file-viewer.tsx:141) offer "Open in AI Visualizer" on every image, renders included. Both push `/visualizer/<design>?file=<id>` (lead-files.tsx:93, file-viewer.tsx:88).

The page (app/(editor)/visualizer/[designId]/page.tsx:23-24) matches `?file` only against `rooms[].sourceFileId`. A render is never a room's source, so it falls through to `data.leadImages`. That list includes every image with a thumb (lib/visualizer/queries.ts:150), and the editor's `initialFile` effect (visualizer-editor.tsx:539-542) then adds a new room made from the render.

`leadImages` also feeds the Add room dialog's "From the lead's files", so renders show up there as site photos. The editor has no way to arrive on a given version: `viewKeys` starts as `{}` (visualizer-editor.tsx:108). A studio opening "Render - Living room - V2" expects to land on V2 of the Living room. Instead it gets a stray room with 0 versions, and each press adds another room. That is a real, repeatable mess.
verdict.fix:
1. **Record the version on the file.** Add a nullable `lead_files.render_key` text column holding `<jobId>:<variantId>` (additive migration 0055, plus lib/db/schema.ts). `fileVersion` writes it on insert. Repair backfills it on existing Renders rows by matching the thumb `/visualizer/img/v/<job>/<vid>`, or by room name + `Vn` against the design's jobs, so the baseline's filed renders are covered too. Add the column to the baseline lists.

2. **Resolve the key on the page.** In app/(editor)/visualizer/[designId]/page.tsx, look up the file's render_key when `?file` names one (a small helper in lib/visualizer/queries.ts). Find the room owning that job and the version key, then pass `initialRoom` plus a new `initialVersion` prop. Do not pass `initialFile`.

3. **Open on that version.** In visualizer-editor.tsx, seed the view with a lazy initialiser: `useState(() => initialRoom && initialVersion ? { [initialRoom]: initialVersion } : {})`. That respects the no-setState-in-effect rule.

4. **Keep renders out of the room sources.** Exclude rows with a render_key from `EditorData.leadImages`, which also fixes Add room › From the lead's files.

5. **Label the menu.** In files-grid.tsx `FileMenu` and file-viewer.tsx, show "Open this version in AI Visualizer" when the row has a render_key. This needs `renderKey` on `FileRow` from lib/leads/files.ts. Keep "Open in AI Visualizer" for photos. This is invented copy, so log it in REGISTER with the fix.

6. **Handle a deleted version.** If the key's version is gone, land on the room with the snackbar "That version is no longer in the design" (MSG style).

Verify with a Playwright probe: open V2 from Files. Rooms stay at the same count, V2 is the selected version, and Add room lists no renders.

kept.title: Add to a quote: one line per wall instead of per finish, and nothing is ever priced (exact-name match only, Company › Materials' Price book link ignored)
kept.where: Editor › version ⋮ › Add to a quote… dialog → the quote's section
kept.evidence: 19-quote-dialog.png lists 'Walls · Sage Green' twice. The quote got two identical 'Walls — Sage Green' lines at S$0 (24-quote-editor-items.png; DB: 4 items, cost 0 and markup 0, category null). The client page and REG-678 merge by group and finish (one 'Walls · Sage Green' line, 35-client-1.png). No Price book item is named 'Sage Green' or 'Walnut Engineered', so the dialog's promise 'priced from the Price book where an item has the same name' never happens in the demo. addVersionToQuote never reads studio_materials.price_book_item_id, although sm-sage-whisper → 'Painting, whole unit' and sm-walnut-vinyl → 'Vinyl flooring, supply and install' are linked.
kept.repro: Kevin Ng › Living room › V2 ⋮ › Add to a quote… → Add to quote → Open quote.
kept.fix: In app/visualizer/actions.ts addVersionToQuote and in the dialog's lines (visualizer-editor.tsx ~l.711), build lines with changeLines() (one per group + finish) and set the quantity from the number of surfaces. Price each line from 1) the studio material's priceBookItemId when materialId is a studio material, then 2) an exact name match, then 3) the Price book item of the group's category (Walls → Painting, Floor → Flooring). Show 'n of m priced' in the dialog before adding.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed the duplicate lines from the code. addVersionToQuote (app/visualizer/actions.ts:273–301) and the QuoteDialog `lines` prop (visualizer-editor.tsx ~l.711) map `applied.surfaces` one to one. changeLines() in lib/visualizer/model.ts:113, which the share link and Present use, dedupes by group + finish. The demo version has two walls in paint-002 "Sage Green" (fixtures/baseline.json holds several surface entries for it), so the quote gets two identical "Walls — Sage Green" lines at qty 1 while the client page shows one. That mismatch is real and a studio would see it in the quote.

The claim that the studio material's price_book_item_id is ignored is also true: `find` matches exact names only. But fixing that would not price the demo. The Kevin Ng design uses catalogue materials (paint-002, floor-006), not the studio materials sm-sage-whisper / sm-walnut-vinyl, so their links never come into play.

"Nothing is ever priced" is behaviour the code documents. The dialog and the docstring promise pricing only "where an item has the same name", else S$0 for the studio to price, so this part is not a broken promise.

I would not take the auditor's third fallback, the Price book item of the group's category (Walls → "Painting, whole unit"). It would price each wall at a whole-unit painting rate, a wrong number on a client quote, which is worse than an honest zero.

The scratch DB on :3015 does not carry the demo design (render_jobs has only one sketch job), so I verified from the code and the baseline, not live.
verdict.fix:
1. Build both the dialog's lines and the server's lines from one shared helper in lib/visualizer/model.ts, so they cannot drift. Call it `quoteLines(a: Applied)`: it returns changeLines' surface-group + finish entries plus the customized furniture, carrying the surface count and the materialId.
2. In addVersionToQuote, write one line per group + finish.
   - Set qty to the number of surfaces and keep the unit 'Lot', or keep qty 1 and name the count in the description ("2 walls"). Qty times a per-wall Lot is only right if the studio prices per surface, so the description form is the safer choice.
   - Price in this order: the studio material's priceBookItemId when materialId is a studio_materials id (select from studioMaterials where id in the materialIds, not deleted, whose linked item is live), then the exact name match.

3. In QuoteDialog (components/visualizer/editor/dialogs/small-dialogs.tsx), show "n of m lines priced from the Price book; the rest go in at S$0 to price", computed from the same helper plus the viewer's book.
4. Optionally, so the demo shows a priced line: link the catalogue paint and floor to Price book items through a studio material in repair data, or have the demo design use sm-sage-whisper. Pair this with the REG-343 repair rule and db:baseline.
