kept.title: 'Add to a quote' is disabled on a relit version even though it carries the finishes it was made from
kept.evidence: 21-v3-menu.png: 'Add to a quote… — It changed the look, not a finish' is disabled on V3 (Relit · Golden Hour). The DB shows V3.finishes still holds sage walls, walnut floor and the emerald sofa inherited from V2. A studio that wants to quote the version the client liked best (V3 is the one shown last) can't.
kept.repro: Kevin Ng › Living room → V3 ⋮.
kept.fix: Base the menu item's enabled state and addVersionToQuote's lines on the cumulative v.finishes (surfaces + customized pieces) rather than v.applied (this pass only). Keep the disabled meta only when finishes are empty (a pure restyle or a photo with nothing picked).

verdict.reason:
This is real, and I reproduced it from the code and the scratch DB. The menu item (visualizer-editor.tsx:679) and addVersionToQuote (actions.ts:276-278) both look only at `v.applied`, which holds just the one Generate pass that made the version. On a relight, restyle or note pass `applied.surfaces` is empty, so the item is disabled and the server refuses too.

The scratch DB matches the finding. Living room V2 is an edit with 3 surfaces plus a customised piece (living-room-f0 → Emerald Velvet). V3 is a relight with `applied.surfaces` empty, but `finishes.surfaces` still holds s0/s1/s3 and `finishes.customized` still holds the Emerald Velvet sofa.

Other parts of the page already treat those finishes as V3's:
- The Moodboard dialog (moodboard-dialog.tsx:35-36) lists V3's surfaces and pieces from `version.finishes`.
- The Surfaces panel does the same.

So one page shows the finishes and then says "It changed the look, not a finish". That reason is wrong.

The same gap has a quieter form too: a V3 edit that changes only the floor quotes only the floor, even though V2's walls are still in the picture. Quoting the version the client picked is the main job of this flow. Quoting V2 works, but it only helps a studio that knows how the versions chain, so the severity stays major.
verdict.fix:
Put one pure helper in lib/visualizer/model.ts: `quoteLines(finishes: Finishes, detection: Detection | null, applied: Applied)`. It returns `{ what, label, to }[]` built from the version's cumulative finishes:
- For each entry of `finishes.surfaces`, the label is the matching `detection.surfaces` label. If there is no match, fall back to `applied.surfaces`' label or the id. `what` is `groupWord(label)` and `to` is `f.name`. Dedupe on what + name, the same way `changeLines` does.
- Then each entry of `finishes.customized` whose id is not in `finishes.removed`. Take the label from `detection.furniture`, strip the "(…)" suffix, and use `to` = desc.

Use it in two places:
1. app/visualizer/actions.ts `addVersionToQuote`: read the room's detection with `parseDetection(got.r.detectionJson, got.r)` and replace the `a.surfaces` / `a.furniture` line building. Change the empty-case error to "This version has no finishes to quote yet." A version with no finishes, meaning a pure restyle or relight of the photo, stays refused.
2. components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:679: set the item's disabled state and its menuMeta from `quoteLines(mv.finishes, room.detection, mv.applied).length`. When the meta shows, it should read "No finishes picked yet", not "It changed the look, not a finish". Put the helper in a const so the condition isn't written out twice.

Keep the Add-to-quote dialog's subtitle and the group name `${room} · V${n} finishes` as they are. They now describe exactly what gets added.

The moodboard's `where` lookup (moodboard-dialog.tsx:60) takes labels from `applied.surfaces`, so on V3 it loses the "where" words. It should use the same detection labels, and that can share the helper's label lookup.

This needs no new UI or copy beyond that one meta line; log it in REGISTER as a bug fix. To verify: the Kevin Ng › Living room › V3 ⋮ menu shows "Add to a quote…" enabled. Adding V3 to a new draft gives walls, floor and sofa lines. After the check, revert the test quote in the scratch DB.

kept.title: A render_feedback notification opens the design on the wrong room and version, and never shows the pin it is about
kept.where: Bell › 'Kevin Ng pinned a note on a render — Master bedroom · V1…' → editor
kept.evidence: 47-bell.png → click → 48-bell-open.png: it lands on Living room with V3 on screen. The pin on Master bedroom V1 is nowhere in view. The href stored is /visualizer/<design>?from=/leads/<id> with no room or version (sqlite notifications.href). Activity lines use viz(null) for favourites, notes and pins in the same way (lib/leads/activity.ts l.135-150).
kept.repro: As the client, pin a note on Master bedroom V1 of the link → as Dane open the bell → click the entry.
kept.fix: In app/renders/actions.ts tell(), pass the version: href `/visualizer/<design>?room=<roomId>&v=<key>${pin ? `&pin=${id}` : ''}&from=…` (roomId is in the snapshot). Have app/(editor)/visualizer/[designId]/page.tsx read ?v= and ?pin= to select the version and open the thread. Use the same href in activity.ts viz() for favourite, note and pin lines.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this from the code, so I skipped the live check.
- **The bell link carries no room or version.** `tell()` in `app/renders/actions.ts` (l.28-30) builds the href as `/visualizer/${designId}` plus `?from=` only. It is called with the same href for a favourite (l.41), a note (l.51) and a pin (l.86).
- **The page cannot select one either.** `app/(editor)/visualizer/[designId]/page.tsx` reads only `room`, `from` and `file`.
- **So the editor opens on its defaults.** `VisualizerEditor` shows `rooms[0]` and that room's newest live version (`live[live.length - 1]`, l.101-110). It shows only that version's pins (`vPins`, l.238), and `activePin` always starts null (l.135). A client pin on Master bedroom V1 therefore lands on the first room's latest version, with no marker in view and no thread open. That matches the auditor's shots.
- **The Activity tab has the same gap.** In `lib/leads/activity.ts` the favourite, note and pin lines pass `viz(null)` (l.140-150). The per-version map `vn` already holds each version's room name but not its room id.
- **The data needed is already stored.** The share snapshot has `roomId` and `key` per version (`ShareSnapshot` in `lib/visualizer/queries.ts:165`). The pin row has `jobId` and `variantId`.

This is real for a studio: the bell's whole point is to take the designer to what the client said, and today it drops them in the wrong room.
verdict.fix:
1. **`app/renders/actions.ts`**
   - Widen `versionIn`'s type to include `roomId`.
   - Give `tell()` an optional `at?: { roomId: string; key: string; pinId?: string }`.
   - Build the href as `/visualizer/<design>?room=<roomId>&v=<encodeURIComponent(key)>[&pin=<pinId>]&from=…`, keeping today's `?from=` handling when `leadId` is null.
   - Pass `at` from `pickFavourite`, from a version-scoped note, and from the pin action (the new pin's id).

2. **`app/(editor)/visualizer/[designId]/page.tsx`**
   - Accept `v` and `pin` in `searchParams`.
   - Keep `v` only when a live version with that key exists in `data.versions[room]`.
   - Keep `pin` only when `data.pins` has that id on that key.
   - Pass them to the editor as `initialView` and `initialPin`.

3. **`components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx`**
   - Seed the state lazily: `useState(() => initialView && initialRoom ? { [initialRoom]: initialView } : {})` for `viewKeys`, and `useState(initialPin)` for `activePin`.
   - Check that the `selKey`/`selWas` render-phase reset (l.144) starts equal on the first render, so it does not wipe the seeded pin.
   - No new UI is needed: `PinThread` already opens for `activePinRow`.

4. **`lib/leads/activity.ts`**
   - Store `roomId` in the `vn` map.
   - Extend `viz(roomId, key?, pinId?)` to add `&v=` and `&pin=`.
   - Use it for favourite, note (when `versionKey` is set) and pin lines (`${p.jobId}:${p.variantId}`, `p.id`) instead of `viz(null)`.

5. **Housekeeping**
   - Existing notification rows keep their old href and still open the design, so no repair is needed.
   - Log the change as a bug fix in `REGISTER.md` and add a probe step: bell entry → correct room, V1, thread open.

kept.title: 'Ask for a call back' goes through with no phone number, and the task is due within the hour even at 3 a.m.
kept.evidence: Pressing 'Ask for a call back' with the phone field empty (s15.cjs) showed 'Dane will call you back' and wrote render_consultation_requests.client_phone = NULL plus a task 'Call Kevin Ng back about the renders' with an empty description. The field reads 'Your phone number' (required-looking) while the message is '(optional)'. On a personal design's link there is no lead phone at all, so the studio can't call. That task and the one with a number were both due at 19:17 / 19:18 UTC = 03:17 SGT: askCallBack sets dueAt = now + 60 min.
kept.repro: /renders/<token> → scroll to the call-back card → press Ask for a call back without typing a number.
kept.fix: In render-share-page.tsx CallBack, prefill the phone with the lead's number when there is one ('We'll call you on 9688 2109 — change it'), and require a valid SG number otherwise (the same isSgPhone gate). Mirror that in askCallBack: refuse an empty phone when the link has no lead phone. Set dueAt to the next working hour (09:00–18:00 SGT) instead of +60 min.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed both halves by reading the code. I didn't run a live repro; the auditor's s15 run already showed the rows it writes.

1. **No number goes through.** In `CallBack` (components/visualizer/share/render-share-page.tsx:161-196), `bad = !!phone && !isSgPhone(phone)`, so an empty box counts as valid. `askCallBack` (app/renders/actions.ts:56-78) only checks the number when there are digits. It then writes `clientPhone: null` and a task whose description is null when the message is empty.
   - On a lead's link the studio still has the lead's own number, so that case is survivable.
   - On a personal design's link (`s.leadId` null) there is no lead, no members and no number. The result is an unassigned studio task that nobody can act on.
   - The box label "Your phone number" has no "(optional)", while the message box does, so the page implies the number is required.
2. **Due time.** The action's own docstring says "due in a working hour", but the code sets `dueAt = now + 60 min`. A request at 03:17 SGT becomes a task that is already overdue by morning. That contradicts the stated intent.

**Where the proposed fix is off:** prefilling the lead's phone ("We'll call you on 9688 2109") on a public share link would expose the lead's number to anyone holding the link. That goes against the rule set in the X-Ray parity round: no phones in client-facing payloads. `PublicShare` (lib/visualizer/queries.ts:166) deliberately carries no lead phone and should keep it that way.
verdict.fix:
1. **Require a number where there is no lead.** Add a boolean `hasLead` (or `needsPhone`) to `PublicShare` in lib/visualizer/queries.ts. Don't add the lead's phone itself.
2. **The call-back box** (render-share-page.tsx `CallBack`):
   - When `!data.hasLead`, treat an empty box as an error: `bad = needsPhone ? !isSgPhone(phone) : !!phone && !isSgPhone(phone)`. Show the house message `MSG`-style "Enter a Singapore number — 8 digits starting with 6, 8 or 9".
   - When there is a lead, label the box "Your phone number (optional)" so it matches the message box.
   - No prefill.
3. **The action** (app/renders/actions.ts `askCallBack`):
   - Refuse an empty number when `!s.leadId`.
   - When the number is empty on a lead's link, read the lead's phone on the server and write "Call on the lead's number, {phoneLocal}." into the task description, so the task is never blank.
4. **Due time.** Add a small pure helper, e.g. `nextWorkingHour(at)` in lib/visualizer/ or lib/format.ts, that works in SGT (UTC+8):
   - Between 09:00 and 17:00 on a weekday: due in one hour.
   - Otherwise: due at 10:00 on the next weekday.
   
   Use it for `dueAt` so the code matches the docstring's "due in a working hour".
5. **Record it.** Log the change in REGISTER.md as a bug fix.

kept.title: Adding the same version to a draft twice silently duplicates the whole section
kept.where: Add to a quote… → existing draft OM-10010
kept.evidence: 24-quote-editor-items.png: two identical sections 'Living room · V2 finishes' (1 and 2), each with the same 4 lines, after adding V2 twice. The second time the dialog gave no hint that V2 was already in OM-10010.
kept.repro: V2 ⋮ → Add to a quote → A new quote → Add; then V2 ⋮ → Add to a quote → OM-10010 → Add.
kept.fix: In addVersionToQuote, look for an existing group named `${room} · V${n} finishes` (or a stored source key) and return { existed: true }. In QuoteDialog, show the meta 'V2 is already in OM-10010' on that chip with 'Add again' / 'Open quote'.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this by reading the code and did not run it on :3019. `addVersionToQuote` in app/visualizer/actions.ts (lines 273–304) never checks whether the target draft already holds this version. Every call runs `createQuoteItem(qid, { kind: 'group', name: `${room} · V${n} finishes` })` and then adds all the lines under the new section, so a second add makes an identical section. `QuoteDialog` in components/visualizer/editor/dialogs/small-dialogs.tsx (lines 74–100) only receives `{id, number, title, status}` for each quote, so it cannot tell. It also pre-selects `drafts[0]` when it opens. After the first add creates OM-10010, that draft is the default pick, so a second press of "Add to quote" duplicates the section without the user choosing anything. The snackbar then says "4 lines added" with no warning. `quote_items` has no soft delete, so a name match on the group in that quote is a reliable check. A studio would notice this, because the duplicated section doubles the quote total, but it is easy to undo in the editor. Minor is the right severity.
verdict.fix:
1) lib/visualizer/queries.ts: for each draft in `quoteRows`, add `versions: string[]`, the names of its `quote_items` rows where kind='group' and the name ends in ' finishes'. One `inArray(quoteItems.quoteId, draftIds)` query is enough.
2) small-dialogs.tsx `QuoteDialog`: take a new prop `groupName` (the `${room} · V${n} finishes` string the editor already knows). When the picked draft's `versions` includes it, show a hint line using the existing `styles.hint` + info Icon pattern already in the dialog: "V2 is already in OM-10010 — adding again makes a second section". Change the primary label to "Add again". When the dialog opens, pre-select the first draft that does not already hold it; if every draft holds it, pick 'new'. Do not add a new "Open quote" button: the success snackbar already has an Open quote action.
3) app/visualizer/actions.ts `addVersionToQuote`: add a fourth parameter `again = false`. When it is false and the draft already has a group with that name, return `{ error: 'This version is already in that quote.' }`. This guards the server against stale clients.
4) visualizer-editor.tsx `addToQuote`: pass `again` when the dialog says the version is already in the picked draft.
This reuses Chips, Dialog and the hint row that are already there, and adds no new UI pieces. Log it in REGISTER.md as a bug fix, with the hint copy marked as invented copy.

kept.title: Quote lines from the visualizer are inconsistent and print internal wording to the client
kept.evidence: The dialog shows 'Grey Fabric Sofa → Emerald Velvet' (19-quote-dialog.png), but the quote line reads 'grey fabric sofa — Emerald Vel…' in lower case (24-quote-editor-items.png). The server uses f.label raw while the client uses titleCaseLabel. Every description reads 'From the AI Visualizer: white painted back wall → Sage Green.', the engine's detection label, and that prints on the client's quote.
kept.repro: Add V2 to a quote → open the quote → Items.
kept.fix: Use the same titleCaseLabel/groupWord on the server. Make the description client-facing, e.g. 'Sage Green (matte) — living room walls', and keep the provenance in a non-printing place (the line comment or the section's source).

verdict.reason: This is real, and it is a bit worse than the auditor reported. In app/visualizer/actions.ts:277, addVersionToQuote builds furniture lines with `what: f.label.replace(...)`, using the engine's raw lower-case label, for example "grey fabric sofa". The dialog's Changes list (lib/visualizer/model.ts:118, changeLines) runs the same label through titleCaseLabel, so it shows "Grey Fabric Sofa". Line 293 then writes `description: "From the AI Visualizer: ${l.label} → ${l.to}."`. That is the detection label plus internal provenance, and it lands in the quote line's description, which prints wherever the template's Items block shows descriptions. There is a second mismatch the auditor missed. changeLines merges surfaces by group and finish (the "simplicity pass": two walls in Sage Green read as one "Walls · Sage Green" line), but the server does not merge. So the dialog can list N lines while the quote gets N+k lines, such as "Walls — Sage Green" twice. Severity stays minor: it is copy on a draft the studio can edit before sending, but a client would see it on a printed quote.
verdict.fix: In app/visualizer/actions.ts addVersionToQuote, build the lines from the same source as the dialog. Make changeLines (lib/visualizer/model.ts) export a quotable subset, e.g. `quoteLines(a)`: the merged surface lines (groupWord + seen-set) plus the customised furniture through titleCaseLabel with the position hint stripped. Leave out removals, style, palette, lighting and scope, as the server does today. The dialog's count and wording then match the quote exactly. Keep the line name as `${what} — ${to}`. Make the description client-facing and short, e.g. `${to} — ${what.toLowerCase()}, ${room}`, or leave it empty. Do not put the detection label or "From the AI Visualizer" in it. The provenance already lives in the section name ("{room} · V{n} finishes"). If more is wanted, write it where nothing prints: the quote's activity or the line comment. Log it in REGISTER as a bug fix, with the copy flagged as invented, and re-run the visualizer probe's add-to-quote step.

kept.title: The client page lists versions in pick order (V3, V1, V2) and joins rooms with repeated 'and'
kept.where: /renders/[token] header + cards; Share dialog WhatsApp draft
kept.evidence: s12.cjs order: 'V3 · Relit · Golden Hour', 'V1 · Japandi', 'V2 · Walls, Floor +1', … (33-client-top.png shows V3 first). h1 and draft: '5 design ideas for your living room and master bedroom and kitchen'.
kept.repro: Share with client with V3 pre-ticked → tick V1 and V2, Master bedroom V1 and Kitchen V1 → Create link → open the link.
kept.fix: In createShareLink, sort the snapshot's versions by room position and then n. Join room names with new Intl.ListFormat('en-SG',{type:'conjunction'}) in share-dialog.tsx draft() and render-share-page.tsx.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this by reading the code; I did not run it live. createShareLink (app/visualizer/actions.ts:311-318) walks `input.keys` in the order the dialog's `picked` array holds them, which is the order the user ticked. The "V3 pre-ticked, then V1, V2" order goes straight into the snapshot. render-share-page.tsx:28 builds `rooms` by first appearance in `data.versions` and renders each room's versions in snapshot order, so the page shows V3, V1, V2, and rooms can come out of order too. The h1 (render-share-page.tsx:44) and the WhatsApp draft (share-dialog.tsx:46-47) both use `rooms.join(' and ')`, so three rooms read "living room and master bedroom and kitchen". A client would see this on the page itself, and the studio would see it in the message it sends. It is minor copy and order polish.
verdict.fix:
1) In createShareLink, sort `versions` before the insert: first by the room's place in the design's room list, then by the version's index in `versionsOf(...)` (the editor's own V1…Vn order). Add a room position and version index next to each pushed entry, sort on them, then drop them before saving. The dialog's Pick order and the V labels then match the page. The per-version fileVersion side effect can stay where it is.
2) In share-dialog.tsx, build `roomNames` from `rooms.filter(r => r.versions.some(v => picked.includes(v.key))).map(r => r.name)`, which follows room order, not tick order. Join the names with `new Intl.ListFormat('en-SG', { style: 'long', type: 'conjunction' }).format(names)` before `.toLowerCase()`.
3) In render-share-page.tsx, join the h1's room names with the same ListFormat. Links made before the fix keep their pick order (the page has no room positions). Optionally, sort each room's versions by the number in the "V{n}" label as a fallback.
To avoid two copies, put a small `listJoin(names)` helper in lib/format.ts and use it in both places.

kept.title: The client and the bell see the studio's internal version labels ('Walls, Floor +1', 'From a note', 'Kitchen sketch')
kept.where: /renders/[token] card titles; render_feedback bodies; WhatsApp draft
kept.evidence: 35-client-0.png / 67-client-phone-top.png: 'V2 · Walls, Floor +1'. The personal link reads 'V1 · From sketch · Japandi' and the draft says 'a design idea for your kitchen sketch' (s27 output). Bell bodies read 'Living room · V2 · Walls, Floor +1'.
kept.repro: Open any shared link; share the personal design 'Showroom — kitchen concept'.
kept.fix: Give the snapshot a client label: the room name + 'Option A/B/…' (or 'Design 2') with the style or light in plain words ('Sage walls, walnut floor'). Keep the descriptor for the studio. Drop 'sketch' from the room word in the draft and title.

verdict.reason:
The client-facing half holds up in the code. `createShareLink` (app/visualizer/actions.ts:318) freezes `label: v.label` into the snapshot, and that label is the studio's strip descriptor from `descriptor()` in lib/visualizer/model.ts:128-144. Descriptors look like 'Walls, Floor +1', 'From a note', 'From sketch · Japandi' and 'Emptied · …'.

render-share-page.tsx:115-119 prints that label as the client's card title, with only the 'V2' split off in bold, and uses it in the img alt too. It is shorthand ('+1', 'From a note') and means nothing to a homeowner.

A room made from a sample sketch is named `${sample.name} sketch` (actions.ts:141). share-dialog.tsx:47 lowercases the room names into the WhatsApp draft, so the client reads 'a design idea for your kitchen sketch'.

The bell half does not hold up. The `tell()` bodies in app/renders/actions.ts:41/51/86 go to the studio, and the studio's own version label is the right one there, because it lets a designer find the version in the strip. So this is a real copy flaw on the client link and draft only, polish-to-minor. The card already lists 'What changed' in plain words under the photo, which softens it.
verdict.fix:
1) app/visualizer/actions.ts `createShareLink`: add `clientLabel` to each `ShareSnapshot` version and keep `label` as it is for the studio. Make it 'Design {n}', numbered in the order picked within its room. Add the chosen style or light as its tail when `applied` has one (e.g. 'Design 2 · Japandi'). Never use the '+N', 'From a note' or 'Emptied' descriptors there. Also freeze a `clientRoom` = room.name with a trailing ' sketch' removed (/\s+sketch$/i).
2) components/visualizer/share/render-share-page.tsx: print `v.clientLabel ?? v.label` for the card title and alt, and `clientRoom ?? roomName` for the room heading and grouping. The `??` keeps older snapshots readable.
3) components/visualizer/editor/dialogs/share-dialog.tsx:47: build the room words for the draft from the same sketch-stripped name.
4) app/renders/actions.ts: leave the bell bodies on `v.label`, the studio's descriptor, because the designer needs it to find the version.
Log the change in REGISTER.md as invented copy, then check /renders/[token] at 1440 and 390.

kept.title: Pin times on the client page count from when the link was made, not from now
kept.evidence: render-share-page.tsx passes now={data.createdAt} (the link's creation) to PinThread. Anything made after the link reads 'just now' however old it is (Kevin's reply showed 'just now'). The studio's pin made before the link read '40 days ago' against the link's date (s14 output).
kept.repro: Open /renders/17fe84ab2eca47 → tap a pin → compare the times with the DB.
kept.fix: Return now: Date.now() from fetchShare (PublicShare.now) and pass that to PinThread and the notes.

verdict.reason: The code shows the bug directly. render-share-page.tsx:53 passes `now={data.createdAt}` into VersionCard, which hands it to PinThread (line 130). PinThread's `when()` in components/visualizer/editor/pin-card.tsx:12-14 works out `Math.round((now - ms)/60000)` and returns 'just now' whenever the result is under 1, and that includes negative values. So every pin or reply made after the link was created reads 'just now' however old it is. Pins made before the link are aged against the link's date, not against today. fetchShare already works out `const now = Date.now()` (queries.ts:192) but uses it only for `state` and never returns it. The notes list uses an absolute displayDate, so notes are not affected. Severity is minor: the client sees wrong ages on the pin threads, and nothing breaks.
verdict.fix: In lib/visualizer/queries.ts, add `now: number` to the PublicShare type and return the `now` that fetchShare already computes (`now,` in the returned object). This matches VisualizerHome and the design loader, which already return `now: Date.now()`. In components/visualizer/share/render-share-page.tsx:53, pass `now={data.now}` instead of `data.createdAt`. Leave the notes on their absolute displayDate. Optionally, clamp `when()` in pin-card.tsx with `Math.max(0, …)` so clock skew never produces a negative age. Replies the client posts during the visit will still read 'just now' against the load time, which is correct.

kept.title: Activity lines for sharing are wrong or missing: 'You stopped sharing' names nobody, and renew, save-to-Files and replies aren't named
kept.evidence: lib/leads/activity.ts l.137 hard-codes text 'You stopped sharing the renders’ link.' and actor 'You'. render_share_links has no revoked_by column, so a Manager's stop reads as the viewer's. Renew writes no line. Save to Files shows as 'You uploaded the file “Render - Living room - V1.jpg”' (50-activity.png). Kevin's reply on a pin ('Yes please, a bit warmer') has no line.
kept.repro: Stop and renew a link, save a version to Files, reply as the client on a pin → open Activity.
kept.fix: Add revoked_by and renewed_at/renewed_by to render_share_links (additive migration), stamp them with actingMember, and write the stop and renew lines with who(). For a file with a render key, word it 'saved V1 of “Living room” from the AI Visualizer to Files'. Add client reply lines from the pins' comments.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this by reading the code. I didn't run it on :3015.
- **Stop line names nobody.** `lib/leads/activity.ts` hard-codes the text "You stopped sharing the renders’ link." and the actor 'You'. `stopShareLink` (`app/visualizer/actions.ts` ~l.339) sets only `revokedAt`, and `render_share_links` has no column for who stopped it. When a Manager stops a link, every viewer reads it as their own action.
- **Renew erases the stop.** `renewShareLink` stores no record of the renewal, and it resets `revokedAt` to null. After a stop and a renew, the Activity feed shows neither event. This is worse than the finding says.
- **Save to Files reads as an upload.** `saveRender` inserts a plain `lead_files` image into the "Renders" folder, with its thumb from `renderUrl(...)`. The files branch (activity.ts l.247) then words it "uploaded the file “Render - …”". Creating the Renders folder also writes "created the folder “Renders”".
- **Replies are missing.** Pin replies live in `render_annotations.comments_json`. The pins branch only emits the first body ("pinned a note"), so a client's reply never appears.

Severity is minor: this is an audit trail the client reads in demos, but no flow breaks.
verdict.fix:
No migration is needed. Use the existing `lead_events` table (Parity R7, `lib/leads/events.ts`) rather than adding columns.
1. **Stop and renew.** Add the event kinds `render_link_stopped` and `render_link_renewed` to `LeadEventKind`. In `stopShareLink` and `renewShareLink` (`app/visualizer/actions.ts`), call `logLeadEvent(db, s.leadId, kind, { title: <n renders> })` when `s.leadId` is set; it stamps the actor via `sessionMemberSql`.
2. **Activity lines.** In `lib/leads/activity.ts`, drop the `revokedAt` line: once events carry the stop, a renew no longer erases it. Word the two new events in the events branch: "{who} stopped sharing the renders’ link" and "{who} renewed the renders’ link for 7 days". Keep the `viz(null)` link.
3. **Save to Files.** In the files branch, detect a render-saved file by its thumb path from `renderUrl` (the `/visualizer/img` prefix) or by its parent being the Renders folder. Word it "{actor} saved {q(name)} from the AI Visualizer to Files". Use the `wand_shine` icon and keep the file link.
4. **Replies.** In the pins loop, parse `comments_json` and push one line per reply: "{authorName} replied on V{n} of {room}: {body}", with the `comment` icon, at the reply's `createdAt`, with id `viz-pin-${p.id}-${c.id}`.
5. **Record and repair.** Log the change in `REGISTER.md` as `bug fix`, and add a repair rule if the demo data has a revoked link without its event.

kept.title: Shared before: no way to copy or open an existing link, and unsent links read 'sent today'
kept.where: Share with client dialog · Shared before
kept.evidence: 51-shared-before.png / 54-stopped.png: each row only has Stop sharing or Renew. If Kevin loses the link, the studio has to make a new one. A stopped row uses the neutral 'link' glyph, which reads like a live link. A link created and then closed without sending reads 'sent today' (the ago text ignores sentVia null). Pins aren't counted in the row's summary.
kept.repro: Open Share with client on Kevin's design and look at the rows.
kept.fix: Add a Copy link text button (and Open) on live rows, using useCopy + recordShareSent('copy'). Use link_off for stopped rows. Word unsent links 'made today · not sent yet'. Count pins ('2 pins').

verdict.reason: I checked the code and didn't need a live check. In share-dialog.tsx (lines 115–124), each Shared before row only offers Stop sharing (IconButton link_off) on a live link, or Renew on a stopped or expired one. There is no way to copy or open a link that already exists, even though ShareRow carries `token` (lib/visualizer/queries.ts:98) and the dialog already uses `useCopy`. A studio that loses the link has to make a new one, and that leaves a second live link to the same versions. A stopped row uses `Icon name={s.revokedAt ? 'link' : 'send'}`, so a dead link shows the plain link glyph. The line always reads `sent ${ago(createdAt)}` and only adds ' on WhatsApp' when sentVia is 'whatsapp'. A link made and then closed without Copy message or Open WhatsApp (sentVia null) therefore reads 'sent today'. That is false, and it hides the fact that it was never sent. One part is softer: client pins are stored in render_annotations by version (app/renders/actions.ts:85) and are not tied to a share link, so a count per link can only be approximate. The 'note' responses (leaveNote) are already counted.
verdict.fix:
All changes are in components/visualizer/editor/dialogs/share-dialog.tsx.
(1) On live rows (not revoked, not expired), add a DS `Button appearance="text"` "Copy link" before the Stop sharing IconButton. Build the URL as `${window.location.origin}/renders/${s.token}` and copy it with the house clipboard helper, using one `useCopy` hook for the row being copied (the pattern already in the file; track that row's id). On success call `onSent(s.id, 'copy')` only when `s.sentVia` is null, so a real WhatsApp send is never overwritten. Put Open in the same kebab, or as a bare IconButton `open_in_new` with a Tooltip, that calls `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener')`. Keep the row to at most two actions.
(2) Stopped rows use the `link_off` icon, and expired rows could use `schedule`. Check that both glyphs are in public/fonts/ICONS.txt; link_off already is, because the Stop button uses it.
(3) Word the first line from sentVia: 'sent today on WhatsApp' / 'copied today' / 'made today · not sent yet' (null).
(4) Pin counting is optional. If it's done, pass the client's pins on the link's keys created after `s.createdAt` from the editor's `pins` and show 'n pins'. Otherwise leave it, because pins don't belong to a link.
Log the copy as a bug fix / invented copy in REGISTER.md, as every unmocked change is.

kept.title: The 'Stopped sharing' snackbar wraps to two lines and covers the dialog footer; Undo re-opens with a new expiry
kept.evidence: 54-stopped.png: 'Stopped sharing — the link says so to whoever opens it' wraps inside the 344px snackbar and sits over the dialog's '1 of 6 picked' footer. Its Undo calls renewShareLink, which sets a fresh +7-day expiry instead of putting back the old one.
kept.repro: Share with client → Shared before → link_off → Stop sharing.
kept.fix: Shorten the message to 'Link stopped' (fits 344×48). Make Undo clear revoked_at only (add an unstopShareLink action) so the original expiry stands.

verdict.reason:
The Undo half is real. In visualizer-editor.tsx:715, Stop's snackbar Undo calls renewShareLink. At app/visualizer/actions.ts:334 that action sets expiresAt to now + 7 days as well as clearing revokedAt. So a link that was "Open until 30 Sep" comes back with a new expiry a week from today rather than the one the client was given. The snackbar says "Undo", but the action actually renews the link.

The visual half mostly isn't a defect. snackbar.module.css:21 fixes the bar at 344px and its comment says "long messages wrap". That was a user decision on 2026-08-29, so a two-line snackbar is house behaviour. The snackbar host is bottom-left for every page. In 54-stopped.png it only covers the "…1 of 6 picked" caption at the footer's left. Cancel and Create link stay clear and usable, and the snackbar goes away when it times out. A shorter message is fine as polish, but the finding's reason for it doesn't hold. "Link stopped" alone also drops the useful point that the client will see the link has stopped. A one-line wording such as "Stopped sharing this link" keeps most of that.

Severity is minor, and only because of the Undo semantics.
verdict.fix:
1. In app/visualizer/actions.ts, add a `restartShareLink(id)` (or `unstopShareLink`) next to stopShareLink. It looks up the row, sets only `revokedAt: null` and keeps `expiresAt` unchanged, then calls touch(s.designId, s.leadId). It should also refuse or no-op when the link was already expired, so Undo never brings back an expired link.
2. In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:715, point the snackbar's onAction at that new action with `.then(() => router.refresh())`. Leave onRenew on renewShareLink, where "another 7 days" is what the user asked for.
3. Optional polish: shorten the message to one line, e.g. "Stopped sharing this link", on the house Snackbar. Don't change snackbar.module.css; its fixed width and wrapping are the owner's rule.

kept.title: The bell panel's 'Notification settings' link is drawn over the list rows
kept.evidence: 77-bell-foot.png: 'Notification settings' overlaps the row 'Overdue: Draft initial concept boards'. In 47-bell.png it overlaps 'Kevin Ng left a note on the renders'. With the render_feedback rows the list runs past the drawer and .foot has no background or scroll container. The render_feedback glyph is also grey, while other client answers (question_answered) are green.

kept.fix: In notifications-panel.module.css give .list flex:1; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto (or .body overflow) so .foot sits below it, with a surface background. Add .glyph[data-kind='render_feedback'] to the green client-answer rule.

verdict.reason: The overlap is real, and the code explains it. The bell panel's own `.body` has `flex: 1; min-height: 0` and sits inside the Drawer's `.body`, which is a flex column with `overflow-y: auto`. When the list is taller than the drawer, the panel body shrinks to the drawer's height. Nothing clips the list: the panel body has no overflow of its own, so the list spills out of it visibly. `.foot` is placed right after the shrunk box, so it lands in the middle of the rows. It has no background either, so the rows show through it. 77-bell-foot.png shows "Notification settings" printed over "Overdue: Draft initial concept boards". The bug is not specific to the visualizer: any feed longer than the drawer triggers it, and the render_feedback rows just made the demo feed long enough. The glyph point also holds. `render_feedback` (icon `wand_shine`) has no `data-kind` rule, so it falls back to the grey default, while `question_answered`, the other client answer, is green (REG-608 rule).
verdict.fix:
Put the link in the Drawer's own sticky footer instead of fixing the CSS. The house Drawer (`components/om/drawer.tsx`) already has a `footer` prop, which renders a `<footer>` below the scrolling body with the sheet's safe-area padding on a phone.
1. In `components/shell/notifications-panel.tsx`, pass `footer={<Button appearance="text" onPress={...}>Notification settings</Button>}` to `<Drawer>`. Keep the right alignment by wrapping the button in `.foot`, and drop the in-body `<div className={styles.foot}>`.
2. In `components/shell/notifications-panel.module.css`, remove `flex: 1; min-height: 0` from `.body` so the list scrolls in the Drawer's body. Reduce `.foot` to `display: flex; justify-content: flex-end`, since the Drawer footer already draws the border and padding.
3. Add `.glyph[data-kind='render_feedback']` to the green `question_answered` rule (`--om-color-tertiary-green-variant2` / `--om-color-tertiary-green-default`).
4. Check the bell at 1440×1024 and 390×844: the last row should be reachable and the link should stay pinned below the list.

If the owner would rather keep the markup, the CSS-only fix is: `.body { flex: none }`. The link then scrolls at the end of the list instead of staying pinned.

kept.title: The AI Visualizer quick link from inside a Files folder brings you back to All Files, not the folder
kept.where: Lead › Files › Renders → quick link AI Visualizer → Back
kept.evidence: s21 output: from /leads/<id>/files?folder=ecad… the editor's from= is /leads/<id>/files (the query is dropped), and Back lands on All Files.
kept.repro: Lead › Files › open the Renders folder → right rail AI Visualizer → Back.
kept.fix: In app/leads/[id]/overview.tsx openVisualizer, pass the full current URL (pathname + search) as from=, as lead-files.tsx does with `here`.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this by reading the code and did not run it live. In app/leads/[id]/overview.tsx, openVisualizer (line 199) calls `router.push(withFrom(`/visualizer/${r.id}`, href(tab)))`. `href(slug, query?)` (line 195) rebuilds the tab URL from `detailHref(lead.id, slug)` and adds only the lead's own `?from=` origin. Any other query on the current page is dropped, including the Files tab's `?folder=<id>`. So from Files › Renders (`/leads/<id>/files?folder=…`), the editor's `from=` is `/leads/<id>/files?from=…`, and Back lands on All Files.

The Files tab's own entry points get this right. lead-files.tsx line 81 builds `here = pathname + ?search` and uses it for openFile, openComments and the render's "Open in Visualizer" (line 93). The quick link is the only way in that loses the folder. The Quote X-Ray quick link (line 389) makes the same mistake with `href(tab)`.

This is minor: the studio has to open the folder again after Back. That goes against REG-465 ("Back returns where you came from").
verdict.fix:
In app/leads/[id]/overview.tsx, give Back the URL the press happened on instead of `href(tab)`. The current URL already carries any `?from=` and `?folder=`, so nothing else is needed. The value is read inside the event handler, not during render, so the react-hooks lint rules are fine.
- openVisualizer: `const here = window.location.pathname + window.location.search; router.push(withFrom(`/visualizer/${r.id}`, here))`.
- Quote X-Ray quick link (line 389): make the same change to `from=${encodeURIComponent(here)}`.

Another option is `usePathname` + `useSearchParams` to build `here` the way lead-files.tsx does. That needs the hook's Suspense rules checked in a production build.

To check the fix, run a Playwright probe on Lead › Files › Renders folder → AI Visualizer → Back and confirm the URL still has `?folder=`. Log it as a bug-fix line under REG-465 / REG-673 in design-source/REGISTER.md.

kept.title: A malformed renders link shows Next's bare unstyled 404 instead of the studio's notice
kept.evidence: 55-malformed.png: a plain '404 | This page could not be found.' with no letterhead, served with HTTP 200. An unknown well-formed token gets the house notice (55-unknown).
kept.repro: Open /renders/x! (or any token that is too short or has other characters).
kept.fix: In app/renders/[token]/page.tsx, render <RenderLinkClosed state="gone"> for every unknown token instead of notFound().

verdict.reason:
I reproduced it. `app/renders/[token]/page.tsx` calls `notFound()` when a token fails `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,40}$/` ("not a link the app ever made"). The app has no `not-found.tsx` anywhere, so Next's plain default 404 shows. The status is 200 because `loading.tsx` streams the page. I checked this on :3020: `curl /renders/x!` returns 200 with "This page could not be found". A well-formed unknown token gets the studio's `RenderLinkClosed state="gone"`.

The auditor presents it as a slip in the renders page, but it is a deliberate pattern shared with the other client links. `app/sign/[id]/page.tsx:22` and `app/sign/bundle/[id]/page.tsx:22` use the same regex guard and `notFound()`. `app/confirm/[quoteId]` and `app/sign/[id]/quote` also `notFound()` on a miss. Fixing only renders would make the four client links behave differently.

A client only reaches this through a link that was mangled on copy or paste. Tokens are URL-safe, and a clipped token of 8 characters or more still matches the regex and gets the house notice, so this is rare. It stays polish.
verdict.fix: In `app/renders/[token]/page.tsx`, drop the regex and `notFound()`. Every miss should render the existing `<RenderLinkClosed state="gone" expiresAt={null} studio={...fetchBrand()}>`, which also makes the regex check unnecessary. Keep the client links consistent by giving `/sign/[id]` and `/sign/bundle/[id]` the same treatment, using their existing `LinkNotice` (`components/contracts/sign/link-notice.tsx`) in its gone/inactive state rather than `notFound()`. Do the same for `/confirm/[quoteId]` and `/sign/[id]/quote` if they have a matching notice. As an extra, a root `app/not-found.tsx` built from the house pieces would cover anything left. No new copy is needed: reuse the notices' existing wording.

kept.title: The closed-link notice offers only a phone number, and no WhatsApp or designer's name
kept.evidence: 55-expired.png / 56-expired-phone.png: 'Please ask Demo Studio Pte Ltd for an updated link' with only +65 6222 0188. The client arrived from WhatsApp and knows the designer (Dane) by name.
kept.repro: Set a link's expires_at in the past → open it.
kept.fix: Keep sender (and the link's lead) in the closed state. Say 'Ask Dane for an updated link' and add a 'Message on WhatsApp' link (wa.me to the studio's number with a prefilled 'Hi Dane, the design link has ended…').

verdict.reason:
Confirmed in code. The notice is real and it is missing the sender. `fetchShare` already returns `sender` (the name of the member who made the link) for every link state. But `app/renders/[token]/page.tsx` passes only `studio` to `RenderLinkClosed`. So `render-share-page.tsx:209` falls back to "Please ask {studio.name} for an updated link", and the only thing to press is a tel: link. The open page, by contrast, speaks in the sender's first name throughout (`senderFirst`: "ask Dane to call you", "Dane will call you back").

The WhatsApp half of the fix is off. `studio.phone` is the studio's landline (+65 6222 0188, starting with 6), and a wa.me link to a landline opens WhatsApp on a number it can't reach. The member's own phone (`members.phone`, REG-644) is not in `PublicShare`. The page also has no WhatsApp message anywhere: its way back to the studio is the call-back form. A prefilled message like "Hi Dane, the design link has ended…" would be invented copy.

Severity polish is right. The name is a cheap consistency win a client would notice. The WhatsApp button isn't justified as proposed.
verdict.fix:
1. In `app/renders/[token]/page.tsx`, pass `sender={data.sender}` to `RenderLinkClosed`. The 'gone' branch passes nothing, because no link record exists.
2. In `components/visualizer/share/render-share-page.tsx`, give `RenderLinkClosed` an optional `sender` prop and use `senderFirst = sender?.split(' ')[0] ?? studio.name`, the same rule the open page uses. The line becomes "Please ask {senderFirst} at {studio.name} for an updated link", or keeps its current words when there is no sender. Keep the tel: link as it is.
3. Don't add a wa.me link to the studio number: it's a landline, and the message would be invented copy. A WhatsApp link would only be right if `fetchShare` also returned the sender member's phone and `isSgPhone` said it was a mobile (starting 8 or 9). That needs the owner's OK and a REGISTER entry (invented copy), so propose it rather than build it.
4. Log the wording change as a REG bug-fix / consistency line and re-check the 55-expired / 56-expired-phone shots at 1440 and 390.

kept.title: Saved renders: a placeholder upload thumbnail, made-up sizes, no origin in Information, and download names that differ by place
kept.where: Files upload toast · Files list · viewer Information · Download
kept.evidence: 13-uploaded-grid.png: the upload toast shows the stand-in /figma-assets/file-thumb-1.png for original.jpg (upload-toast.tsx l.48). 16-renders-list.png: every sample-path render is '137 KB' (fileVersion hard-codes 140_000). 06-viewer-info.png: Information doesn't say which design, room or version a render came from. verdict.reason:
I confirmed all four points by reading the code. I did not need a live check.
(1) Line 48 of `upload-toast.tsx` hard-codes `/figma-assets/file-thumb-1.png`. Its header comment says this was deliberate: "the thumb is the mock's JPEG" (REG-149). So it follows the mock rather than being a slip. Uploads now keep their real picture (REG-675), so showing the real photo is fair polish, but it is a change to mocked UI and must be logged in the register.
(2) Line 259 of `app/visualizer/actions.ts` stores `sizeBytes` as 140_000 whenever the image is not a data: URL. Every render saved from a sample therefore shows "137 KB", which is made up. This is real.
(3) The line in `visualizer-editor.tsx` that names the editor's download is `${title} - ${room.name} - V${n}.jpg`, where `title` is the design name (e.g. Kevin Ng). `renderFileName` on line 243 of `actions.ts` saves the file as `Render - ${room} - V${n}.jpg`. The same version gets two different names. This is real.
(4) `file-info-panel.tsx` lists only the generic fields. A render file is linked to its origin only through its thumb URL (`renderUrl(jobId, v)`); there is no key column. Adding an origin row is new UI with no mock, so it needs the register as invented copy.
All four are low-impact polish. The naming and size points are the clear wins; the toast thumb and the Info origin row are optional additions.
verdict.fix:
1. Download names: add one helper, `renderFileName(design, room, n)` in `lib/visualizer/`, used by both `app/visualizer/actions.ts` (line 243) and the editor's download (`visualizer-editor.tsx`, about line 433). Pick one pattern, e.g. `{Design} - {Room} - V{n}.jpg` (the Original stays `- Original.jpg`).
2. Size: in the save-to-Files action, when the render lives under `/public/visualizer/...`, `fs.stat` the file and store its real size. If there is no file to read, store `null` so the list shows the house empty value.
3. Upload toast: in `lead-files.tsx`, add a `thumb` field (an object URL, or the data URL already read for the stored picture) to `UploadToastState` for image uploads. `UploadToast` renders it when present and falls back to the mock's JPEG otherwise; revoke the object URL when the toast closes. Log this as REG, user-directed / bug fix.
4. verdict.reason: I confirmed this in the code and didn't test it on :3019, because Duplicate would write to the shared DB. `duplicateDesign` (app/visualizer/actions.ts:92-101) inserts the design and then copies only `project_rooms`, with `stateJson: null`. It never selects or inserts `render_jobs`, so the copy has 0 renders. `hasRenders` is false for every room, and the card shows the untouched site photos. Nothing says the renders stay behind: the snackbar in visualizer-home.tsx:123 reads only "{title} duplicated — a personal copy". A studio that duplicates to branch a concept would expect its V1…Vn to come along. Major is fair: nothing is lost, since the original keeps them, but the copy is useless for what Duplicate is for. The data carries over cleanly. `variants_json` holds each variant's `imageUrl` (data: URLs are served through /visualizer/img/v/{jobId}/{variantId}, so a new job id still works). `parentKey` is `${jobId}:${variantId}` (`versionKey`, lib/visualizer/model.ts:170), so it must be remapped to the new job ids.
verdict.fix:
Change only app/visualizer/actions.ts `duplicateDesign`, inside one `db.transaction`:
1. Copy each live room with a new id, keeping a `roomMap` from old id to new id.
2. Select `render_jobs` where `roomId` is in the old room ids. Give each job a new id and keep a `jobMap`.
3. Insert each job with `roomId: roomMap[old]`, `leadId: null`, and `variantsJson` rewritten so every `parentKey` of the form `oldJob:n` becomes `jobMap[oldJob]:n` (leave the room-original key as it is). Keep `kind`, `style`, `model`, `status`, `createdAt` and `completedAt`, and every variant's `deletedAt`, so version numbers and labels stay the same.
4. Copy each room's `stateJson`, remapping any version keys the same way, or keep it null because pending edits are session-only. Either way the renders must come across.
5. Don't copy `render_share_links`, consultation requests or annotations. Links belong to what was sent to a client, and pins belong to that conversation.

Then update the snackbar in components/visualizer/home/visualizer-home.tsx:123 to count what was copied, e.g. "{title} duplicated with its {n} renders — a personal copy", using `count()` from the card meta. That is invented copy, so log it in REGISTER.md.

Probe: duplicate Kevin Ng on a scratch DB. The card should read "3 rooms · 5 renders", the mosaic should show the renders, the editor's version strip should show V1…V5 with parents intact, and deleting the copy forever should leave the original's render_jobs untouched.

kept.title: New design from inside a folder lands at the root, and Back leaves the folder
kept.where: /visualizer?folder=… > New ▾ > Blank design / From a sample room
kept.evidence: From /visualizer?folder=lf-visualizer-showroom, New > Blank design opened /visualizer/576e…?from=%2Fvisualizer. The DB row 'Design · 25 Sept' has folder_id NULL (s23 log). blank() and fromSample() call createDesign({}) or createDesign({ name }) without the open folder. `open()` hard-codes withFrom(…, '/visualizer'), so the editor's Back returns to the root, not the folder the user was in.
kept.repro: 1. Open the Showroom ideas folder on /visualizer. 2. Choose New ▾ > Blank design. 3. Press Back in the editor: you land on All designs, and the new design is not in the folder.
kept.fix: Read the open folder in VisualizerHome, either with useSearchParams().get('folder') or by exposing the current folder from LibraryGallery through a newMenu(close, folderId) argument. Pass { folderId } to createDesign in blank() and fromSample(), and build `from` from the full current URL (pathname + search), as lib/nav's helpers do elsewhere.

verdict.reason:
The bug is real, and the code alone proves it. In components/visualizer/home/visualizer-home.tsx, blank() calls `createDesign({})` (line 53) and fromSample() calls `createDesign({ name })` (line 66). createDesign in app/visualizer/actions.ts already takes `folderId` (line 58) and writes `folderId: input.folderId ?? null`, but nothing passes it, so a design started inside a folder lands at the root. `open()` (line 47) and forLead() (line 59) hard-code `withFrom(..., '/visualizer')`, so the editor's Back drops `?folder=`.

The severity and scope need correcting. The design is not lost: it appears under All designs and can be moved, so this is a misplaced-context annoyance rather than a major one. It is also not specific to the visualizer. LibraryGallery's `newMenu: (close) => ReactNode` never hands the open folder to its hosts, and the other galleries build `from` from a fixed base (for example contract-templates-gallery.tsx: `const here = '/company/templates/contracts'`). The fix belongs in the shared gallery contract, so every library behaves the same way, not in a one-off `useSearchParams` read in VisualizerHome.
verdict.fix:
1. In components/company/templates/library-gallery.tsx, change the prop to `newMenu: (close: () => void, place: { folderId: string | null; here: string }) => ReactNode`. `folderId` is `openId`, which the gallery already works out from `params.get('folder')`. `here` is `pathname` plus the current search string. Pass both at line 391: `p.newMenu(() => setNewOpen(false), { folderId: openId, here })`. The existing callers ignore the second argument, so the change is backward compatible.

2. In components/visualizer/home/visualizer-home.tsx, take `place` in `newMenu={(close, place) => ...}` and thread it into the actions:
   - `blank(place)` calls `createDesign({ folderId: place.folderId })`.
   - `fromSample(key, asSketch, place)` calls `createDesign({ name, folderId: place.folderId })`. The sample picker's state needs to keep the place captured when the menu opened.
   - `open(id, place.here)` and forLead() use `withFrom(`/visualizer/${id}`, place.here)` instead of the literal '/visualizer', so Back returns to `/visualizer?folder=…`.
   - A lead's design stays unfiled on purpose, because openLeadDesign reopens an existing design. Only its `from` should follow the folder.

3. Optionally, give the other galleries' New handlers the same `folderId` / `here` wiring in a follow-up (templates, price book).

No new UI, and no REG entry beyond a "bug fix" line. Verify with a probe: from `?folder=lf-visualizer-showroom`, New > Blank design should store `folder_id = lf-visualizer-showroom`, and Back should land on the folder. Revert the created rows afterwards.

kept.title: The Colour field rejects hex without '#' and silently throws away a partial value on blur
kept.evidence: Typing 9DB0A0 shows the error 'Six hex digits, like #9DB0A0' (S/85-hex-nohash.png). Typing '#9db0a' and tabbing away silently reverts the field to the previous #604337 without a word (S/87-hex-blur.png). hexOf only accepts a leading '#'; onBlur sets hexDraft null.
kept.repro: New material > Colour > type 9DB0A0; then type #9db0a and press Tab.
kept.fix: Accept 3 or 6 hex digits with or without '#' (normalise to #RRGGBB in hexOf), and filter junk as typed (the numeric-field rule, REG-150). On blur with an invalid draft, keep the draft and show the error rather than reverting.

verdict.reason: The code matches the report. In material-dialog.tsx line 23, `hexOf` only accepts `^#[0-9a-f]{6}$`. So "9DB0A0" becomes a draft and shows the error "Six hex digits, like #9DB0A0" (the value is correct and only lacks '#'). Line 101's `onBlur={() => setHexDraft(null)}` throws any unfinished draft away, so the field goes back to the last good hex without a word. Nothing filters junk as it is typed either (maxLength 7 only), which goes against the house rule that a number-like field filters input rather than flagging it (REG-150). The Brand kit's colour field (brand-kit-view.tsx:54) uses the same strict regex, so studios hit this there too. It is small, but it is real: studios paste hex values from paint suppliers' sites, often without the '#'.
verdict.fix:
1. Add a shared pure helper pair to lib/format.ts, next to `decimalTyped` / `moneyTyped`:
   - `hexTyped(v)` keeps an optional leading '#' plus at most 6 hex characters and drops everything else as it is typed.
   - `hexOf(v)` accepts 3 or 6 hex digits with or without '#', expands the 3-digit form, and returns '#RRGGBB' in upper case or null.
2. In components/company/materials/material-dialog.tsx:
   - Use both helpers: `onChange={(v) => { const t = hexTyped(v); const h = hexOf(t); if (h && t.replace('#','').length === 6) { setHex(h); setHexDraft(null) } else setHexDraft(t) }}`. This way a 3-digit form only commits on blur and does not jump while the user is still typing.
   - On blur, commit the draft when `hexOf(draft)` passes. Otherwise keep the draft so the existing error stays visible; don't revert it.
   - Save should use the committed `hex`, or be blocked while an invalid draft is showing.
3. Point components/company/templates/brand-kit-view.tsx's local `hex` at the same `hexOf`, so both colour fields behave the same way.
4. The error copy can stay as it is. It is existing copy, so no new register entry is needed beyond a bug-fix REG line.

kept.title: Long names are cut silently on save, and Duplicate then loses its '(copy)' suffix
kept.where: Rename design, New / Edit material, Duplicate (designs and materials)
kept.evidence: 'Tan residence — … (client asked for warmer tones)' was stored as '…option B (client as' (80-character cleanName; S/50-deleted-sheet.png). The material name was cut to 60 characters ('…very long suppl', S/95-list.png). Duplicating that material gave a second card with the identical name and no '(copy)', because the suffix was sliced off (S/111-mat-dup.png, the two left cards).
kept.repro: Rename a design to more than 80 characters, or add a material with a name over 60 characters, then Duplicate it.
kept.fix: Give the name fields maxLength (80 for designs, 60 for materials) so the limit is visible while typing. In duplicateDesign and duplicateStudioMaterial, truncate the base name first, then append ' (copy)' (or ' (copy 2)' when that name is taken).

verdict.reason:
Checked in the code. Three of the claims hold and one does not.

- **Material names are cut without warning (holds).** `valid()` and `renameStudioMaterial` in `app/company/materials-actions.ts` store `clean(name, 60)`. Nothing tells the member the name was shortened.
- **Material Duplicate loses "(copy)" (holds).** `duplicateStudioMaterial` passes `${m.name} (copy)` into `createStudioMaterial`, which slices the result to 60. When the original name is already 55 characters or more, the suffix is cut off and the copy gets an identical name.
- **Design names are cut without warning (holds).** `renameDesign` stores `cleanName(name)` (80 characters). The Rename dialog in `components/company/templates/library-gallery.tsx` (line 496) has no `maxLength`, so the member cannot see the limit.
- **Design Duplicate losing "(copy)" (does not hold).** `duplicateDesign` in `app/visualizer/actions.ts` (line 96) inserts `${lead?.name ?? got.d.name} (copy)` directly, without `cleanName`. A long design keeps its suffix and is simply stored at up to 87 characters.

The only affected field in `material-dialog.tsx` is Name (line 94); Colour already has `maxLength={7}`. This is a real but small data-quality problem in the Company › Materials gallery.
verdict.fix:
1. **Show the limit while typing (`components/company/materials/material-dialog.tsx`).** Give the Name TextField `maxLength={60}`. The house `TextField` already forwards `maxLength` to the input.
2. **Rename dialog (`components/company/templates/library-gallery.tsx`).** Add an optional `nameMax?: number` prop to `LibraryGallery` and pass it as `maxLength` to the Rename dialog's TextField. The visualizer designs gallery passes 80 and the materials gallery passes 60. Other libraries leave it unset, so their behaviour does not change.
3. **Material Duplicate (`app/company/materials-actions.ts`).** In `duplicateStudioMaterial`, cut the base name first, then add the suffix: `${m.name.slice(0, 60 - ' (copy)'.length).trimEnd()} (copy)`. That keeps the result within the 60-character limit, so "(copy)" survives.
4. **Design Duplicate (`app/visualizer/actions.ts`).** Optionally cap `duplicateDesign`'s base name the same way at 80, so a copy never goes over the limit that Rename enforces. Its suffix is not lost today, so this is only for consistency.
5. **No "(copy 2)" numbering.** The finding suggests it, but the rest of the app just appends "(copy)" and nothing requires more.

kept.title: Deleted Materials sheet: doubled crumb, 'Used by: Linked', 'Made by'
kept.evidence: The crumb reads 'Materials / Materials /' (S/119-mat-deleted-sheet.png, top-left). The 'USED BY' column shows 'Linked', which is a Price book link state, not a usage. 'MADE BY' should say 'Added by' (the dialog's own words are 'whoever added it').
kept.repro: Delete a material, then open ⋮ > Deleted Materials.
kept.fix: In materials-view.tsx, set deletedUsageLabel='Price book' (or drop usageWord) and deletedByLabel='Added by'. In LibraryDeletedSheet / LibraryGallery, skip the kind.label crumb when it equals the shell title.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed all three points from the code and the screenshot 119-mat-deleted-sheet.png.

1. **Doubled crumb.** `library-gallery.tsx:514` builds the crumb as `${p.shell?.title ?? 'Templates'} / ${kind.label}`. In materials-view.tsx both values are 'Materials' (`shell={{ title: 'Materials' }}`, and `KIND.label` is 'Materials'), so the sheet shows "Materials / Materials / Deleted Materials". Price book is not affected because its shell title ('Price book') differs from its kind labels (My Items / My Sections).

2. **'Used by: Linked'.** The sheet's usage column defaults to the header 'Used by'. Materials pass no `deletedUsageLabel`, and `usageWord` returns 'Linked' / 'Not linked', which is the material's Price book link state, not a count of what uses it.

3. **'Made by'.** For a material the name in that column comes from `uploadedBy` (`lib/visualizer/queries.ts:218`, `author`), which is whoever added it. The file's own doc comment (line 23) says "whoever added one". So 'Made by' is the wrong label.

These are wording slips on a secondary sheet with no functional impact, so the minor rating stands.
verdict.fix:
1. **materials-view.tsx:** pass `deletedByLabel="Added by"` and `deletedUsageLabel="Price book"` to `LibraryGallery`. Quote templates already sets both props the same way. Change the deleted sheet's `usageWord` to 'Linked' / '--' so the column reads as a plain fact under the 'Price book' header. The alternative is 'Quoted as' with the item name, but that is long for the column.

2. **library-gallery.tsx:514:** build the crumb from a variable that avoids the repeat: `const shellT = p.shell?.title ?? 'Templates'`, then `crumb = p.page ? p.page.title : (p.shell && kind.label === shellT ? shellT : `${shellT} / ${kind.label}`)`. The same equality guard should go on `ariaLabel` if it repeats. This is a generic guard, so Price book and Templates keep their two-part crumbs.

3. **Check:** reopen ⋮ › Deleted Materials at 1440×1024. The crumb should read "Materials / Deleted Materials" and the columns should read ADDED BY and PRICE BOOK.

kept.title: Any member can rename or delete the studio's AI Visualizer folders
kept.where: /visualizer folder kebab, viewed as James (Manager) or Sarah (Designer)
kept.evidence: As James, the kebab of Dane's 'Showroom ideas' offers enabled Move, Rename and Delete (s20 innerHTML; S/141-james-folder-kebab.png). As Sarah the New Folder button is enabled (S/60-sarah2-landing.png). visualizer-home.tsx passes `folders={{ …, block: null }}`, while Materials uses folderBlockFor('materials', viewer) and REG-663 says folders are Owners / Admins.
kept.repro: Use View as to switch to James, open /visualizer, then open the Showroom ideas kebab.
kept.fix: Pass `block: folderBlockFor('visualizer', data.viewer)` (add 'visualizer' to lib/company/folder-libraries.ts). If personal folders are meant to be free, record that as a REG decision instead.

verdict.reason: The observation is real, but the finding misreads why. It says the visualizer skips the folder rule by mistake. It does not: `block: null` in visualizer-home.tsx matches the server. `folderBlockFor` in lib/company/folder-libraries.ts already includes 'visualizer' and returns null for it on purpose, with the comment "(REG-673) … anyone files their own (1.0 A B-10)". The organiser() check in app/company/folder-actions.ts uses the same helper, so create, rename, move and delete are open to every member both in the UI and on the server. So the proposed fix, blocking everyone except Owners / Admins, would undo that decision (audit Q-04 / VL-06: personal designs keep their own folders). A Designer could no longer file their own designs. The real gap is narrower. Folders are shared across the studio, and the rule looks only at the library, never at who made the folder. So James or Sarah can rename or delete Dane's "Showroom ideas", and deleting it moves Dane's designs up a level. The designs themselves are stricter: `designChangeBlock` (lib/visualizer/policy.ts) lets only the maker or an Owner / Admin change one. Undo on delete limits the damage, so this is minor. I verified it by reading the code only and did not re-run it on :3017. The auditor's screenshot evidence matches the code path.
verdict.fix: Keep New Folder open to everyone in the visualizer. Apply the design rule to changes on an existing folder: its maker or an Owner / Admin. (1) In lib/company/folder-libraries.ts, add a folder-level check such as `folderChangeBlockFor(library, viewer, createdBy)`. For 'visualizer' it returns `designChangeBlock`-style text (maker or Owner/Admin); every other library keeps `folderBlock(viewer)`. `folderBlockFor` stays the create gate. (2) In app/company/folder-actions.ts, have renameLibraryFolder, deleteLibraryFolder and the folder half of moveToLibraryFolder check that rule against `libraryFolders.createdBy`. (3) Give each visualizer folder its own block in the gallery. Add `createdBy` / `mayChange` to the folders fetched for /visualizer. In components/visualizer/home/visualizer-home.tsx, pass the block per folder, using the existing `LibraryGallery` / `FolderCard` disabled-with-reason menu items (the house "refused choice says why in the row" pattern), not a gallery-wide block. Log it as a REG line refining REG-673: "visualizer folders: anyone makes one; its maker or an Owner/Admin renames, moves or deletes it". If the owner prefers folders to stay fully open, record that as the REG decision instead and change nothing in code.

kept.title: Undo / Restore bumps updatedAt: the card jumps to the front and reads 'edited just now'
kept.where: /visualizer and Company > Materials after Delete > Undo
kept.evidence: Before the delete, Sample · Living room was third ('edited 0 min ago'). After Undo it is first and reads 'edited just now by Dane' (S/46-deleted.png vs S/47-undone.png). restoreDesigns and restoreStudioMaterials set updatedAt: now().
kept.repro: Delete any design, then press Undo on the snackbar.
kept.fix: Don't touch updatedAt in restoreDesigns or restoreStudioMaterials (clear deletedAt / deletedBy only), so Undo puts everything back where it was.

verdict.reason: The code confirms it. restoreDesigns (app/visualizer/actions.ts:116) sets `updatedAt: now()` and restoreStudioMaterials (app/company/materials-actions.ts:70) sets `updatedAt: new Date()`. The gallery sorts designs by updatedAt desc (lib/visualizer/queries.ts:54 and :86), and cards show "edited … ago" from the same column. So pressing Undo right after a delete moves the design to the front and stamps it "edited just now". Undo should put things back exactly as they were. Other restores in the house already leave the stamp alone: text templates (text-actions.ts:101), payment templates (payment-templates-actions.ts:73) and lead files (files-actions.ts:146) clear only deletedAt. The quote and contract restores do bump it, so the house is not consistent. Severity is minor: the row jumps and the date is wrong, but no data is lost.
verdict.fix: In app/visualizer/actions.ts restoreDesigns, drop `updatedAt: now()` and keep `set({ deletedAt: null, deletedBy: null })`. In app/company/materials-actions.ts restoreStudioMaterials, drop `updatedAt: new Date()` and keep deletedAt null plus isActive true. Check that the delete path is what turned isActive false; if it wasn't, don't force isActive either, so Undo restores the prior state exactly. The Deleted sheets' Restore uses the same actions, so a restored entry also comes back in its original place. That matches the text and payment template libraries.

kept.title: 'edited 0 min ago' between 45 and 59 seconds
kept.evidence: The sample design read 'Living room · edited 0 min ago by D…' (S/35-landing-with-sample.png; S/44-dup-kevin.png, third card). ago() returns 'just now' below 45 s, then Math.floor(s/60) = 0.
kept.repro: Create a design and reload the landing about 50 seconds later.
kept.fix: In lib/templates/ago.ts, use `if (s < 60) return 'just now'` (as lib/format.ts relativeTime does), or Math.max(1, m).

verdict.reason: I confirmed this from the code in lib/templates/ago.ts. The function returns 'just now' only while s < 45. Between 45 and 59 seconds it computes m = Math.floor(s/60) = 0 and prints '0 min ago'. That matches the '0 min ago' seen on the sample card. It is deterministic, so I did not need a live check. The helper is shared by every LibraryGallery card foot, the Quote templates gallery, the template editor's Saved stamp and history drawer, the review and proposal bars, the notifications panel, the contract banner and the template picker. The visualizer gallery is not the only place it shows. lib/format.ts relativeTime already uses a 60-second threshold, so ago() is the one that is out of step. This is a copy glitch visible for about 15 seconds after a save, so the severity is polish-to-minor.
verdict.fix: In lib/templates/ago.ts, change `if (s < 45) return 'just now'` to `if (s < 60) return 'just now'`, which matches relativeTime in lib/format.ts. The doc comment already describes the output as "just now · 5 min ago", so it needs no change. There are no other code changes, and every surface that uses ago() picks up the fix.

kept.title: Move dialog lists every entry with an empty grey thumb, including lead designs that can't be foldered
kept.where: Move to Folder dialog (designs and materials)
kept.evidence: Blank 24×18 grey boxes sit beside 'Kevin Ng' (S/22-move-dialog.png) and beside every material (S/113-mat-move.png). LibraryGallery passes entries without `thumb`, and passes the lead design even though it can never be moved.
kept.repro: Open any design or material kebab and choose Move to Folder.
kept.fix: Add an optional `moveThumb?: (t) => string | null` to LibraryGallery (designs: covers[0]; materials: imageUrl), map it into MoveDialog entries, and filter out items for which mayChange blocks a move (lead designs).

verdict.reason:
The empty grey box is real. LibraryGallery builds the Move dialog's entries at library-gallery.tsx:483 as `{ id, name, parentId }` with no `thumb`, so MoveDialog (move-dialog.tsx:187-193) falls back to an empty `<span className={styles.thumb}>`. Screenshot 22-move-dialog.png shows it next to "Kevin Ng". The same happens in every LibraryGallery library, not only designs and materials.

The second half of the finding is wrong. The dialog lists plain entries on purpose, "listed for orientation" (the Files mock 931:39249, move-dialog.tsx:29). They show what is already in a destination and are not choices. A lead design really does sit at the root, so listing it there is accurate. Hiding it would make the root look emptier than the gallery behind the dialog. The row cannot be pressed, so no one can try to move it.

This is polish rather than minor. It is one 24×18 box in a row nobody can press.

In components/company/templates/library-gallery.tsx, add an optional prop `moveThumb?: (t: T) => string | null` and map it into MoveDialog's entries at line 483: `thumb: p.moveThumb?.(t) ?? null`.

Pass it from two places:
- components/visualizer/home/visualizer-home.tsx: `moveThumb={(t) => t.d.covers[0] ?? null}`
- components/company/materials/materials-view.tsx: `moveThumb={(t) => t.imageUrl || null}`

A material with no image, only a hex colour, keeps the empty box. Optionally, extend MoveEntry with a `swatch?: string` background so those rows show their hex, as the card does. That touches the shared components/om/folders/move-dialog.tsx, so check that the Files tab still renders the same.
