kept.title: Copy slips: lowercase sample help text, 'its 0 renders', 'The 1 design inside move up', 'Sept'
kept.where: Sample room dialog; delete-design confirm; delete-folder confirm; new blank design name
kept.evidence: 1. The Kitchen sample tile reads 'an open kitchen with an island…' in lowercase (S/07-samplepick.png, bottom-left), because the replace only handles /^a /. 2. The delete confirm reads 'Sample · Living room and its 0 renders go to Deleted Designs' (S/45-delete-confirm.png). 3. The folder confirm reads 'The 1 design inside move up to All designs' (S/26-folder-delete-confirm.png). 4. A blank design is named 'Design · 25 Sept' (toLocaleDateString en-SG), while every other date in the app prints '25 Sep' (S/35-landing-with-sample.png).
kept.repro: See each screenshot.
kept.fix: 1. Capitalise the first character: s.context.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + s.context.slice(1). 2. Word deleteMessage without the count when renders is 0. 3. In library-gallery.tsx use 'moves' when the count is 1 ('The 1 design inside moves up…'). 4. Build the default name with lib/format's displayDate-style 'd MMM' helper.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed all four slips in the code. I didn't need the live server because every cause is plain in the source.
1. `visualizer-home.tsx:146` renders `s.context.replace(/^a /, 'A ')`. The Kitchen sample's context in `lib/visualizer/samples.ts:81` is 'an open kitchen with an island…', so the tile starts lowercase.
2. `visualizer-home.tsx:127` always interpolates `count(t.d.renders, 'render', 'renders')`, so a design with no renders reads 'and its 0 renders go to Deleted Designs'.
3. `library-gallery.tsx:488` always says 'The ${c} inside move up'. `folderCount` can return '1 design' or '1 folder', which gives 'The 1 design inside move up'. This is in the shared gallery, so every library's folder delete (templates, Price book) has the same slip, not only the visualizer.
4. `app/visualizer/actions.ts:61` names a new design with `toLocaleDateString('en-SG', {day:'numeric', month:'short'})`. Node here prints '25 Sept'. The rest of the app uses the `MONTHS` table in `lib/format.ts` ('Sep'). The name also depends on the server's ICU version.
verdict.fix:
1. In `components/visualizer/home/visualizer-home.tsx:146`, capitalise the first letter of any context instead of only matching 'a ': `s.context.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + s.context.slice(1)`. If the same `.replace(/^a /…)` pattern appears elsewhere in `components/visualizer`, apply the same fix there.
2. In the same file, line 127, drop the count when it is 0: `t.d.renders ? \`${t.title} and its ${count(...)} go to Deleted Designs — you can restore them there.\` : \`${t.title} goes to Deleted Designs — you can restore it there.\``.
3. In `components/company/templates/library-gallery.tsx:488`, pick the verb from the total. Compute `const total = items.filter(t => placeIdOf(t) === f.id).length + foldersIn(flist, f.id).length`, then write `The ${c} inside ${total === 1 ? 'moves' : 'move'} up to …`. Because the gallery is shared, this fixes every library's folder delete. It is a bug fix, so log it in the register as such.
4. In `lib/format.ts`, add a small exported helper next to `displayDayMonth`: `displayDayShortMonth(d) => \`${d.getDate()} ${MONTHS[d.getMonth()]}\``. Use it in `app/visualizer/actions.ts:61` to build `Design · ${displayDayShortMonth(at)}`. This gives '25 Sep' and no longer depends on the server's locale data.

kept.title: Server restores and material rename skip the permission check; refusals report success
kept.evidence: Code: restoreDesigns and restoreStudioMaterials update any id with no designChangeBlock / materialChangeBlock and no lead-visibility check. deleteDesignsForever does check. materials-view.tsx passes onRename={(t, name) => renameStudioMaterial(t.id, name)} and onDelete={(t) => deleteStudioMaterials([t.id])} without throwing on { error }. LibraryGallery's run() ignores the returned value, so a refused rename still shows 'Material renamed'. The designs view throws correctly (visualizer-home.tsx:124-126).
kept.repro: Code path: call restoreStudioMaterials([id]) as a Designer for a material someone else deleted; it succeeds. Or race a rename after the role changes: the snackbar says renamed.
kept.fix: Filter restore ids through the same block as delete-forever (and visibleLeadIds for lead designs). In materials-view.tsx wrap the actions: `const r = await renameStudioMaterial(…); if ('error' in r) throw new Error(r.error)`, and the same for onDelete.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this by reading the code. I did not run a live repro, because both cases need a role change or a direct server-action call.

**Restores skip the check.** `restoreDesigns` (app/visualizer/actions.ts:114) and `restoreStudioMaterials` (app/company/materials-actions.ts:68) run a bare `UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (ids)`. They apply no `designChangeBlock` / `materialChangeBlock`, no `canOpenLead` check for designs on a lead, and no `deletedAt` filter. Their siblings do check: `deleteDesigns` goes through `designFor` and the block, and both delete-forever functions filter through the block. The UI hides Restore for entries the viewer may not change (`restoreBlock={(t) => t.mayChange}`), so a normal Designer won't hit this. It is a server-side hole, and it breaks the house rule that every action enforces its rule on the server.

**Refusals report success.** In materials-view.tsx:56-57, `onRename` and `onDelete` return the server's `{ error }` without throwing. `LibraryGallery`'s `run()` (library-gallery.tsx:268, 499) only shows the failure snackbar when the promise throws. So if the rule refuses a rename or delete, the snackbar still says "Material renamed" / "X deleted" with Undo, and nothing changed. That breaks the sweep rule (REG-656…660): a refused save must say "Couldn't <do what>". The designs view already throws correctly (visualizer-home.tsx:124, 126). The menu also gates on `mayChange`, so this only shows up in a race, for example a View as switch or a changed role with a stale page. Real, but minor.
verdict.fix:
1. **app/visualizer/actions.ts, `restoreDesigns`:** load the rows and keep only ids where `d.deletedAt` is set, `!designChangeBlock(viewer, d.createdBy)`, and, for a design on a lead, `canOpenLead(viewer, d.leadId)`. Update only those, then call `touch(id, leadId)` for each so the lead's pages revalidate too. Return `{ restored: n } | Err`, with the block message when a single id is refused, mirroring `deleteDesigns`.
2. **app/company/materials-actions.ts, `restoreStudioMaterials`:** filter the same way through `materialChangeBlock(viewer, m.uploadedBy)` and `m.deletedAt`, and return `{ restored } | Err`.
3. **components/company/materials/materials-view.tsx:** wrap the actions the way visualizer-home.tsx does:
   - `onRename={async (t, name) => { const r = await renameStudioMaterial(t.id, name); if ('error' in r) throw new Error(r.error) }}`
   - the same wrap for `onDelete`
   - `onRestore`: throw when the result has `error`
4. **components/visualizer/home/visualizer-home.tsx:** give `onRestore` the same throw, so the Undo and Deleted-sheet paths report "Couldn't restore …".

No new UI or copy is needed: the refusals reuse the existing `DESIGN_RULE` / `MATERIAL_RULE` messages through `run()`'s house failure snackbar.

kept.title: 'For a lead…' picker doesn't say which leads already have a design
kept.evidence: Kevin Ng is listed as 'Kevin Ng · Met · Landed — Semi-D' like every other lead, and the button always says 'Open design' (S/06b-leadpick-kev.png). fetchVisualizerHome computes `hasDesign` for each lead but loadLeads never uses it.
kept.repro: New ▾ > For a lead… and open the Lead list.
kept.fix: In loadLeads, append ' · Has a design' (or the room / render count) to `sub` when l.hasDesign. Optionally sort leads with designs first, and switch confirmLabel between 'Open design' and 'Start design'.

verdict.reason: The code confirms it, so I didn't run a live check. `fetchVisualizerHome` (lib/visualizer/queries.ts:89) sets `hasDesign` on every lead, but `loadLeads` in visualizer-home.tsx:72 builds `sub` from stage and property type only. Every lead looks the same in the 'Design for a lead' picker. Picking one calls `openLeadDesign`, which opens the lead's existing design or creates one; the list doesn't say which will happen. The gap is real but small: nothing breaks and the right design opens either way. One detail matters for the fix: `byLead` also counts lead designs with no rooms. A lead whose design was opened but left empty would be tagged 'Has a design' even though the home grid doesn't show that design (the grid needs rooms > 0).
verdict.fix:
1. In components/visualizer/home/visualizer-home.tsx `loadLeads`, add the tag to `sub` when the lead has a design, e.g. `[l.stage, l.propertyType, l.hasDesign ? 'Has a design' : null].filter(Boolean).join(' · ')`. Don't sort leads with designs first; keep the list order.
2. So the tag matches what the home grid shows, count only designs that have rooms: in lib/visualizer/queries.ts, build `byLead` from the room-bearing `cards` (kind 'lead', not deleted) instead of from all of `designs`.
3. Keep the single `confirmLabel` 'Open design'. It is right for both cases. `PickOneDialog` only takes one static label, and making it depend on the selection would mean changing a shared house component for a small gain.
4. Log the added words as a REG entry (invented copy).

kept.title: 'edited … by' and the 'Updated by' column show the creator, not the last editor
kept.evidence: The card foot reads 'edited 13 Sep ’26 by Dane' and the list column 'UPDATED BY' shows Dane (S/13-in-folder-list.png). DesignCard.author is members[d.createdBy] (queries.ts:77), while updatedAt is the latest render's time.
kept.repro: Have another member render on Dane's design, then look at the card.
kept.fix: Take the author from the latest render job's createdBy (it's already in `jobs`) when it is newer than the design's own update, or relabel the column 'Made by'.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed in the code. In `fetchVisualizerHome`, `card()` (lib/visualizer/queries.ts ~l.77) sets `author = byMember.get(d.createdBy)`, which is the person who made the design. `updatedAt` is the time of the latest version across the design's rooms. `LibraryGallery` puts both in one line: the card foot reads "edited {ago(updatedAt)} by {author}" (library-gallery.tsx:448), and the list's "Updated by" column (l.600) shows `t.author`. So the time comes from the last render but the name comes from the creator.

The rest of the house fills this slot with the last editor:
- quote templates use `t.updatedBy`
- price book items and sections use `updatedBy ?? createdBy` as author and keep `maker` for the Deleted sheet.

The demo data can show the mismatch. On the scratch DB, Kevin Ng's design (created by dane) has renders by michelle (14 Aug, 11:25 and 11:40). Right now the newest render there is dane's, from 25 Sep, so the card happens to read correctly. Any time another member renders last, the card and list would name Dane anyway. It is a small copy/trust issue: polish.
verdict.fix:
In lib/visualizer/queries.ts `card()`, track who made the latest version alongside `latest`. For each room's non-deleted versions `vs`, if `last.createdAt > latest`, set both `latest` and `lastBy = last.createdBy`. Start `lastBy` at `d.updatedBy ?? d.createdBy` if the design table has an updated-by column; it doesn't, so start at `d.createdBy`. Then set `author` / `authorColor` from `byMember.get(lastBy)`. `VersionView` already carries `createdBy`, so no new query is needed.

Keep `createdBy` (and `mayChange`, which rightly keys off the creator) unchanged. If the Deleted sheet should name the maker, add `maker` / `makerColor` the way lib/company/price-book.ts does and map them in visualizer-home.tsx's deleted rows.

Don't relabel the column. "Updated by" is the shared `LibraryGallery` head across every library, so the data should be fixed to match it.

kept.title: Materials: New ▾ opens a menu with one item; read-only dialog invites an upload; kebab says Edit for read-only
kept.evidence: 1. New ▾ opens a dropdown whose only row is 'New material' (S/81-new-menu.png), an extra press. 2. Viewed as Sarah, Dane's Sage Whisper opens read-only, yet the 'Upload a photo' button looks active and the help line says 'Add a photo of the sample so the team knows it on sight' (S/71-sarah-material-readonly.png). 3. Her kebab still offers 'Edit' (S/72-sarah-material-kebab.png).
kept.repro: Open /company/materials; then use View as to switch to Sarah and open Sage Whisper paint.
kept.fix: 1. Make the toolbar's New a direct primary 'New material' button, if LibraryNewButton supports an onPress. 2. In readOnly, hide the well's actions and the help line (show the photo or colour only). 3. Pass openLabel={(t) => t.mayChange ? 'Open' : 'Edit'}.

verdict.reason:
Points 2 and 3 are real. Point 1 is not.

**Point 2 is real.** In material-dialog.tsx the photo well sits inside `ReadOnlyScope`, and that scope only puts a `<fieldset disabled>` around the dialog. The native button is blocked, but the DS Button keeps its active outlined look. The help line is also hardcoded: 'Add a photo of the sample so the team knows it on sight.' Screenshot 71 shows both under Sarah, under a read-only note that says she cannot change the material. The Note textarea also still shows dark, editable-looking text.

**Point 3 is real.** materials-view.tsx passes `openLabel="Edit"` for every viewer. The library's sister gallery, price-book-sections.tsx, already uses `openLabel={runsBook ? 'Edit' : 'Open'}`, and LibraryGallery accepts `(t) => string`. So Materials is the one that drifted. The auditor's proposed code is backwards: `t.mayChange` is a *block reason* string (the dialog reads `readOnly={edit.m?.mayChange ?? null}`), so a truthy value means read-only.

**Point 1 is refuted as a defect.** A New ▾ with a single row is the house LibraryNewButton contract. LibraryNewButton has no direct-press mode; its only alternative is `block`. Price book › My Sections ships the same one-row menu ('New section'). Changing it for Materials alone would break the shared toolbar pattern (REG-541). It would have to be a change to LibraryNewButton applied across every library, which is outside this finding.

Severity stays polish.
verdict.fix:
1. **materials-view.tsx:** change `openLabel="Edit"` to `openLabel={(t) => (t.mayChange ? 'Open' : 'Edit')}`. `mayChange` holds a block reason, so a non-null value means read-only. This matches price-book-sections.tsx's Edit / Open split and the REG-653 rule that the card's words are the menu's.

2. **material-dialog.tsx:** when `readOnly` is set:
   - render the well's `wellActions` span as null;
   - drop the 'Add a photo…' help line, or swap it for the photo line when a photo exists;
   - keep the swatch or photo and the title.

   Also check that the TextArea honours `ReadOnlyContext` so the note reads as disabled, like the other fields in screenshot 71.

3. **Leave New ▾ as it is.** A one-row menu is the shared LibraryNewButton pattern, and Price book › My Sections does the same. If a direct-press New is wanted, it should be an `onNew` option on LibraryNewButton / LibraryGallery applied to every single-row library, logged as a REG.

kept.title: List views and Deleted sheets show generic glyphs where the cover or swatch would identify the row
kept.where: /visualizer list view · Materials list view · both Deleted sheets
kept.evidence: Every design row carries the same wand glyph (S/14-list.png, S/50-deleted-sheet.png), and every material row the same hatched 'texture' glyph beside a separate colour dot (S/95-list.png, S/119-mat-deleted-sheet.png).

kept.title: Editor Compare slider can't be dragged (touch or mouse): the slider box gets `.fill { pointer-events: none }`
kept.where: Editor canvas › Compare (all widths, incl. 390 touch and 1440 mouse)
kept.evidence: s4-slider.cjs: pointerdown target is `stage-module__frame`, never the compare box; aria-valuenow stays 50 after an 80–100px touch drag (p390) and a 200px mouse drag at 1440 (s5-slider-mouse.cjs prints `pointer-events none`). Screenshot phone-tablet/p390-03-compare-dragged.png shows the divider still at the centre. In Present the same CompareSlider works (touch drag moves it 50→27), so the cause is stage.tsx: `<CompareSlider className={styles.fill} …>` and stage.module.css `.fill { pointer-events: none }`.
kept.repro: Open /visualizer/b46000d1-… on a phone (or desktop), tap the Compare button in the canvas bar, then drag the handle. It doesn't move. Only the keyboard arrows work.
kept.fix: components/visualizer/editor/stage.tsx: give the CompareSlider its own class (e.g. `.compareFill { position:absolute; inset:0; width:100%; height:100% }` without pointer-events:none) in stage.module.css, or add `.fill[data-testid='viz-compare'] { pointer-events: auto }`. Add a touch-drag probe to the verify script.

verdict.reason: The code confirms it without needing a live run. In stage.tsx:112 the editor renders `<CompareSlider className={styles.fill} …>`, and stage.module.css:10 sets `.fill { pointer-events: none; }`. CompareSlider appends that class to its root `.box` (compare-slider.tsx:33), and that root is where onPointerDown/Move/Up are attached. `pointer-events` is inherited, and none of the slider's children set it back to auto: `.img` and `.cap` set none themselves, and `.divider` and `.handle` don't set it at all. So nothing inside the slider can be hit, and the pointer goes to `.frame` underneath. That matches the auditor's probe, where the target was `stage-module__frame`. Only keyboard arrows on the role="slider" divider still work. Present uses CompareSlider without `.fill`, which is why dragging works there. It is a blocker because Compare is a main demo moment and can't be dragged with mouse or touch at any width. There is also a smaller issue that shows up once pointer events work. When zoom > 1, onFrameDown (stage.tsx:71-76) only skips targets inside `[role="slider"]`. A press on the compare box away from the divider therefore also starts a frame pan and takes pointer capture away from the slider.
verdict.fix: 1. components/visualizer/editor/stage.module.css: add `.compare { position: absolute; inset: 0; }` and leave out `pointer-events: none`. Keep `.fill` for the preview/highlight/svg overlays, which should stay click-through. 2. components/visualizer/editor/stage.tsx:112: change `className={styles.fill}` to `className={styles.compare}`. 3. components/visualizer/editor/stage.tsx:72 (onFrameDown): add `[data-testid="viz-compare"]` to the early-return selector, or better, bail out whenever `compare` is set. This stops the frame's pan or capture from stealing a drag started anywhere on the compare box while zoomed. 4. Add a probe to the ai-visualizer verify script. It should mouse-drag at 1440 and touch-drag at 390 with isMobile/hasTouch, then check that aria-valuenow moves off 50.

kept.title: Surfaces / Furniture lists get squashed and clipped. Pieces past the first few can't be reached, and the panel body doesn't scroll
kept.where: Editor tray (390, 375, 768, 1024 touch) and the desktop rail at 1440×800
kept.evidence: s6-list.cjs measures list clientHeight vs scrollHeight, with panelBody scrollHeight == clientHeight (nothing to scroll): p375 Surfaces 48/159, p375 Furniture 96/497 (7 of 9 pieces unreachable), p390 Furniture 174/477, t768 Furniture 270/477, desktop 1440×800 Furniture 382/497. Screenshots phone-tablet/list-p375-Furniture.png (only Sofa and Armchair visible, card border cuts the third row) and p390-10-tray-Surfaces.png (Ceiling cut in half). Cause: panels.module.css `.list { overflow: hidden }` is a flex item of `.panelBody { display:flex; flex-direction:column }`, so it shrinks (its min-height:auto resolves to 0) instead of the body scrolling.
kept.repro: On 375×667 touch, open Kevin Ng's design and tap the Furniture tab. Only 2 pieces show. Scrolling the tray doesn't reveal Oak TV Console…Sheer Curtains.
kept.fix: components/visualizer/editor/panels/panels.module.css: add `flex-shrink: 0` to `.list` (and to `.cards`, `.grid`, `.section` for safety), or in rail.module.css set `.panelBody > * { flex-shrink: 0 }` so the body is what scrolls.

verdict.reason: I reproduced this on :3014 using the auditor's measurement against the same design. At 375×667 touch, the Furniture list is 96px tall but its content is 497px, and the panel body is 118/118, so there is nothing to scroll. The other sizes fail the same way: Surfaces at p375 is 48/159, Furniture at p390 is 174/477, Furniture at t768 is 270/477, and Furniture at desktop 1440×800 is 382/497. My screenshot shows only Grey Fabric Sofa and Upholstered Armchair, and the card border cuts the second row. The other 7 pieces can't be reached at all, which blocks the whole Furniture job on a phone. The auditor's cause is right. In rail.module.css, `.panelBody` is a flex column (`flex:1; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto`). In panels.module.css, `.list` has `overflow: hidden`, which makes its automatic minimum height 0, so the list shrinks to fit instead of the body overflowing and scrolling. At 1440×1024 there is enough height, which is why it went unnoticed.
verdict.fix: Fix it once where the panels are hosted instead of patching each panel class. In components/visualizer/editor/rail.module.css, add `.panelBody > * { flex-shrink: 0; }`. This makes every direct child of the panel (section, list, cards, grid) keep its natural height, so the body grows past its frame and its existing `overflow-y: auto` scrolls. It changes nothing for a child that uses flex-grow. Keep `.list { overflow: hidden }` in panels.module.css, because it clips the rounded corners. If `.list` sits inside a `.section` rather than directly in the body, `.section` is itself a flex column, so also add `flex-shrink: 0` to `.list` (and `.cards` / `.grid`) in panels.module.css. After the fix, `.list`'s clientHeight should equal its scrollHeight and `.panelBody`'s scrollHeight should exceed its clientHeight at p375, p390, t768 and 1440×800. Check that 1440×1024 is unchanged, then tap-scroll the tray to Sheer Curtains at 375.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this from the code and from the evidence screenshot. In components/visualizer/editor/stage.tsx (lines ~147-167), the `running` overlay (`.running` > `.runCard`) is rendered inside `.frame`. In stage.module.css line 8, `.frame` has `overflow: hidden` and sits inside the zoom-transformed `.viewport`. The frame takes the photo's aspect ratio, so at 390 px wide it is only about 218 px tall. The run card is much taller: a 56 px glyph, the title, the bar, four steps and the button, plus 20 px padding at ≤767. So the card gets cropped. phone-tablet/g01-running.png shows the wand glyph cut off at the top and the button reduced to a 2 px sliver at the bottom edge. The button is not reachable, so a studio on a phone cannot cancel a render. One small correction to the finding: the button's label is "Cancel", not "Stop". Two side effects of the same placement: the card also scales with zoom and moves with pan on desktop, because it sits inside the transformed `.viewport`. Severity major is right, because a primary control cannot be reached on phones.
verdict.fix:
In stage.tsx, move the whole `<AnimatePresence>{running ? <motion.div className={styles.running}…>…</motion.div> : null}</AnimatePresence>` block out of `.frame`/`.viewport` and make it a direct child of `.area`, after the viewport and before the toolbar. `.area` is already `position: relative; overflow: hidden`, so `.running { position:absolute; inset:0 }` will cover the whole stage and will not scale with zoom or move with pan. Leave the markup and the DS `Button` as they are. In stage.module.css:
- Give `.runCard` `max-height: calc(100% - 32px); overflow-y: auto;`, so that on very short stages (375×667) the card scrolls instead of clipping.
- Keep z-index 6 on `.running` so it stays above `.chip` (3) and `.banner` (4).
- Optionally raise the toolbar's z-index, or let the overlay cover it. Covering it is fine, because zoom and tools are inert during a run.
Check the fix with Playwright at 390×844 and 375×667 (touch), with the Cancel button fully visible and pressable. Also check that 1440 looks unchanged at 100% zoom.

verdict.reason:
I reproduced this from the code and the screenshots. `.card` in pin-card.module.css is `position: absolute` inside the photo frame (`.frame` in stage.module.css and `.media` in render-share-page.module.css). Both frames have `overflow: hidden`. The card also has `max-height: calc(100% - 16px)`, so on a phone it can only be as tall as the photo, about 218px at 390. The body is `flex: 1; min-height: 0`, so it shrinks to almost nothing.

What the screenshots show:

- **p390-s04-pin-draft.png (client link):** the photo's bottom edge cuts the hint, Cancel and Pin it in half.

verdict.fix:
In components/visualizer/editor/pin-card.tsx, check `useSheetLayout()` from components/om/sheet.tsx in both PinThread and DraftPin. On a phone (≤767), render the same content in the house `Sheet` instead of the absolute card. Sheet already portals to body, sits above the dock, and handles Esc, focus and the scrim.

- **PinThread on a phone:**
  - `title` = author name.
  - `subtitle` = "Client · 3 days ago" (the existing `when()` line).
  - `headActions` = the Resolve / Reopen and Remove IconButtons.
  - `children` = the note, replies and Resolved line.
  - `footer` = the Reply TextArea and button.
  - `onClose` = the existing handler.

- **Above 767:** leave the anchored card as it is. It fits there, so there's no need to portal it.

The guard `closest('button, [data-card], textarea')` has to match the sheet. Either put `data-card` on the Sheet content wrapper or check `e.currentTarget.contains(e.target)`. kept.title: The snackbar covers the editor's dock and sits on the Generate footer on phones
kept.where: Editor ≤767 after Generate / Save to Files
kept.evidence: phone-tablet/g02-done.png ('V2 is ready · Compare') and g03-saved-files.png ('V2 saved to Files › Renders · Open'): the 358×48 snackbar at y 780–828 hides the Surfaces…Tools labels and sits against the Generate footer. snackbar.module.css rises by `--app-mobile-dock-height + --bottom-dock`, but the editor (a rail-less fixed frame with its own footer + dock) sets neither.
kept.repro: 390×844: pick a finish, tap Generate and wait for 'V2 is ready'.
kept.fix: visualizer-editor.tsx / editor.module.css: when narrow, set `--bottom-dock` on the editor root (or on document.documentElement while mounted) to the footer + dock height (~128px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)), so the house snackbar host rises above them.

verdict.reason:
The finding is real and reproduces in code and in the screenshot. The editor route (`app/(editor)/layout.tsx`) has no `[data-om-l1-header]`, so the ≤767 rule in `app/globals.css` (~line 298) sets `--app-mobile-dock-height` to just the safe-area inset. Nothing in the visualizer sets `--bottom-dock`. At ≤767 `.host` in `snackbar.module.css` therefore sits at `bottom: 0 + 16px`, which puts the 48px bar at y 780–828 on an 844px screen. In `phone-tablet/g02-done.png` the "V2 is ready · Compare" bar covers the Surfaces / Furniture / Style / Lighting / Tools labels and touches the Generate footer.

The editor already knows its own height here: `editor.module.css` line 40 lifts the FAB by `60px + 68px + 12px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` (footer + dock), but it never passes that offset to the snackbar.

Severity is overstated. The snackbar is short-lived and can be dismissed, and no data or flow is lost. For about 4 seconds it hides the dock's labels and taps on it, and the Compare action sits right on top of the tab bar. That is a clear visual defect but minor, not major.

The suggested fix is slightly off too. Setting `--bottom-dock` on the editor root does nothing, because the SnackbarProvider host sits in the layout outside `.editor`. Writing it on `document.documentElement` from an effect works, but a pure-CSS rule scoped by `:has` is simpler and needs no cleanup.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this by reading the code. I did not run it live because the code path is clear. In components/visualizer/editor/stage.module.css, the only `touch-action` rule anywhere in components/visualizer is `.area[data-mode='draw'] .frame { touch-action: none }` (line 5). `.viewport[data-grab] .frame` (line 7) only sets `cursor: grab`. So in view mode at zoom > 1, a one-finger drag goes to the browser's own pan or scroll handling. The browser then fires pointercancel, and stage.tsx's `onPointerCancel` clears `drag.current`, so the pan stops after the first few move events. That matches the reported translate of about -16px, 4px. stage.tsx has no multi-pointer tracking at all: zoom comes only from `zoomTo` through the −/+ buttons, Ctrl/⌘ + wheel (`onWheel`) and `onDoubleClick`. app/layout.tsx sets `maximumScale: 5`, so a two-finger pinch on the photo zooms the whole fixed editor frame, rail and bars included. verdict.fix:
1. stage.module.css: add `.viewport[data-grab] .frame { cursor: grab; touch-action: none; }` so the app owns the one-finger pan once zoomed. Give the frame in view mode `touch-action: none` (or `pinch-zoom` excluded, `pan-y` only if the phone layout scrolls the stage) so a pinch on the photo never zooms the page. Leave the draw, place and pin rules as they are.

With two active pointers in view mode, record the start distance, the start zoom and the midpoint. On move, apply a live zoom of startZoom × dist / startDist, clamped to 1…3, and let `zoomTo` snap it to the 0.25 step on release. Keep the pan anchored to the midpoint, and cancel any one-finger drag while two pointers are down. At one pointer and zoom > 1, keep the current drag.

kept.title: Client link: the full-width Before/after box traps vertical swipes (touch-action: none), so scrolling over it moves the divider
kept.evidence: s11-share-int.cjs: a purely vertical 150px swipe over the compare box moved the slider 50→68. compare-slider.module.css `.box { touch-action: none }` and `down()` jumps the divider on any pointerdown. On a phone the box spans the width of a long scrolling page.
kept.repro: On /renders/17fe84ab2eca47 at 390, tap 'Before and after' on V2 and swipe up over the photo to scroll the page.
kept.fix: components/om/compare-slider.tsx/.module.css: `touch-action: pan-y` on `.box`. Start dragging only on the handle or after horizontal movement exceeds vertical (track down point, commit on |dx| > |dy| and 6px).

verdict.reason: The code matches the report. In compare-slider.module.css, `.box` sets `touch-action: none`. In compare-slider.tsx, `down()` captures the pointer and calls `at(e.clientX)` on every pointerdown, and `move()` follows every pointermove while a drag is on. It does not check direction, so a vertical swipe that starts on the photo jumps the divider to the touch point and then drags it, and the page does not scroll. The shared CompareSlider is used in three places: the client link (render-share-page.tsx:123, a long page where the box fills the width on a phone), the editor stage (stage.tsx:112) and the Present dialog. The client link is where it matters most, because a homeowner on a phone mostly scrolls. I checked the code only and did not re-run the live test. The auditor's probe (divider moved 50 to 68 on a 150px vertical swipe) fits the code exactly. Severity minor is right: nothing breaks, but the page feels sticky on a phone.
verdict.fix:
1. components/om/compare-slider.module.css: change `.box` from `touch-action: none` to `touch-action: pan-y`, so the browser still owns vertical scrolling and the component gets the horizontal moves.
2. components/om/compare-slider.tsx: on pointerdown, set up the gesture but do not jump the divider.
   - Touch and pen: store the start x/y in a ref. On pointermove, commit to a drag only once |dx| > |dy| and |dx| >= 6px. Then call setPointerCapture and follow `at(clientX)`.
   - Vertical movement or pointercancel (the browser taking the scroll): drop the gesture without moving the divider.
   - A tap with no movement: on pointerup, place the divider at the tap point, so tap-to-place still works.
   - Mouse (`e.pointerType === 'mouse'`): keep today's behaviour (jump and drag at once), so desktop is unchanged.
3. Keyboard handling stays as it is.

This fixes the share page, the editor stage and the Present dialog at once, with no new UI. Log it in REGISTER.md as a bug fix against REG-673. Verify at 390×844 with isMobile and hasTouch:
- a vertical swipe scrolls the page and leaves aria-valuenow at 50;
- a horizontal swipe moves the divider;
- a tap places the divider;
- at 1440, mouse dragging is unchanged.

kept.title: With the tray open, the stage chip overlaps the photo's top-left corner
kept.evidence: phone-tablet/p390-10-tray-Surfaces.png, p375-sk02-tools.png and t768-p02-picked.png: 'V3 · Relit · Golden Hour' sits over the photo corner, because the frame now fills the short stage and the chip is absolutely placed at the area's top-left.
kept.repro: 390×844: tap any dock tab.
kept.fix: stage.tsx: reserve the chip's height in the fit (top pad), or hide the chip while the tray is open (the tray heading already names the version).

verdict.reason:
This is real, and it is a matter of geometry. The chip (`.chip` in stage.module.css) is absolutely placed at top 16px and is 28px tall (`.stageChip`), so its bottom edge sits 44px from the top of the stage. The fit in stage.tsx (`pad = 32`, `fh` limited by `areaSize.h - 64`) centres the frame. When the stage is short, height sets the frame's size, so the frame's top lands at y = 32 and the chip covers the photo's top 12px. The short-stage case happens whenever the tray is open on a phone or tablet. The saved shots show it. At 375 ('V1 · From sketch · Japandi') the chip covers the photo's top-left corner. At 768 it overlaps the photo's corner. At 390 it just touches the top edge (the photo is width-bound there, so it barely clears). On a wide desktop stage the frame is width-bound and has room above, so the problem does not show there. Severity is polish: nothing is blocked, but it looks careless in a live demo.

I would not hide the chip while the tray is open. The tray heading names the tab (Surfaces, Tools and so on), not the version, so hiding it would drop 'V3 · Relit · Golden Hour' from the phone entirely.
verdict.fix:
Reserve room for the chip in the stage's content box instead of changing the chip:
- In stage.tsx, add `data-chip={chip ? '' : undefined}` to the `.area` div.
- In stage.module.css, add `.area[data-chip] { padding-top: 24px; }` (or `calc(var(--om-spacing-4) + 28px + var(--om-spacing-3) - 32px)`, which is the chip's bottom plus a 12px gap, minus the existing 32px pad).

The ResizeObserver reads `contentRect`, which excludes padding. So `areaSize.h` shrinks by 24px on its own, the fit shrinks with it, and flex-centring happens inside the padded box. The frame's top can then never sit above 24 + 32 = 56px, clear of the chip's 44px bottom. No change to the math is needed, and a wide desktop stage stays almost the same (the frame drops 12px, still centred).

Leave the absolutely placed banner alone: it sits on top of the chip only during place / draw / remove modes, as today. Verify at 390×844, 375 and 768 (touch) with the tray open on Surfaces and Tools, and check that the 1440 stage shows only the 12px shift.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this by reading the code. I did not need to run it live. `file-viewer.tsx:88` pushes `withFrom('/visualizer/{id}?file={fileId}', '/leads/{leadId}/files/{fileId}')`. In `visualizer-editor.tsx:97`, `backLabel` returns `Back to ${data.lead.name}` for any `from` that starts with `/leads/`. The Back press still goes to `back`, which is the file. So the tooltip and aria-label say "Back to Kevin Ng", but the press opens the photo. The same mismatch happens from the Files tab's grid and list: `lead-files.tsx:93` passes `here`, which is `/leads/{id}/files` plus an optional folder. Back lands on Files, not on the lead. This is copy only: navigation is correct. Severity stays at polish.
verdict.fix:
In `components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx`, change the `backLabel` line so the lead's name is used only when `from` is the lead's own page. The editor's data may not carry the file's name, so use the section instead:
```ts
const fromPath = from?.split('?')[0]
const backLabel = !from ? 'Back to AI Visualizer'
  : /^\/leads\/[^/]+\/files\/[^/]+$/.test(fromPath ?? '') ? 'Back to the file'
  : /^\/leads\/[^/]+\/files$/.test(fromPath ?? '') ? 'Back to Files'
  : /^\/leads\/[^/]+$/.test(fromPath ?? '') && data.lead ? `Back to ${data.lead.name}`
  : `Back to ${fromLabel(from) ?? 'where you were'}`
```
If the file viewer's `from` should name the photo, pass the file name through the editor data (`VisualizerEditorData.file?.name`, since `?file=` is already read) and use `Back to ${name}`. Otherwise "Back to the file" is enough. Leave `lib/nav.ts` `fromLabel` as it is: its `'Lead'` return drives the L2 crumb, and changing it would affect other pages. verdict.reason:
The finding holds up in the code and in the screenshots. DraftPin and PinThread (components/visualizer/editor/pin-card.tsx) render a 280px `.card` with `position: absolute` inside the photo. In the editor that parent is `.frame` (stage.module.css:8), and on the client link it is `.media` (render-share-page.module.css:25). Both have `overflow: hidden`.

`place()` clamps `top` only to `calc(100% - 120px)`. `.card` has `max-height: calc(100% - 16px)`, but that doesn't stop a card that starts partway down the photo from running past its bottom edge. At 390px the photo is about 220px tall. The draft card needs a label, a textarea (56px minimum) and the Cancel / Pin it footer.

- **m-pin-draft.png (editor):** the card starts at y≈345 and the photo ends at y≈480, so the textarea is cut off and the whole Cancel / Pin it footer is hidden. The only way out is Escape, which a phone doesn't have, so the pin can't be saved.
- **sm-thread.png (client link):** the page's sticky bar covers pin 2's author line and part of the card, and the height cap shrinks the body to one clipped line ("Is the velvet easy to keep clean? We").
- **sm-pindraft.png (client link):** the draft's label and top are cut off at the top of the picture.

This is observable on a phone for both the studio and the client, and it blocks a core action (pinning a note). Major is the right severity.
verdict.fix:
On a phone (≤767 wide), move both cards into the house bottom sheet, per REG-353 (panels become bottom sheets on a phone).

- **pin-card.tsx:** call `useSheetLayout()` from components/om/sheet.tsx. When it is true, return the draft dot (DraftPin) or nothing (PinThread) inside the photo, and render the card's head, body and foot in the house `Sheet`, so the textarea and buttons sit above the keyboard. Keep the pin dot and its `data-active` ring on the photo so the client can see which spot the note belongs to. The sheet's close calls `onCancel` / `onClose` (this also replaces the Escape-only way out). Keep `data-testid` on the sheet content. To do this, split out the card's inner markup (e.g. `PinThreadBody` / `DraftPinBody`) and wrap it either in the positioned `.card` or in `Sheet`. Nothing changes in stage.tsx or render-share-page.tsx:130-132, because both hosts already render these components.

It already anchors with `bottom` for y ≥ 0.55; change the top clamp so the card never starts below `100% - card height`, for example by giving the top-anchored branch `max-height: calc(100% - top - 8px)`. kept.title: Esc does nothing while typing a pin note or a reply
kept.evidence: kb2.cjs output: 'B draft after Esc in textarea: 1'. The draft stays open after Esc, and Esc on the Cancel button does close it ('A … 0'). Focus lands in the textarea by autoFocus, so Esc is dead in the most common case. The cards' onKeyDown Escape handlers (pin-card.tsx:45 and :80) never run because the DS TextArea (react-aria) stops keydown propagation. The window handler in visualizer-editor.tsx returns early while typing.
kept.repro: Editor, click the pin tool, click the photo. Focus is in 'Pin a note here'. Type anything and press Esc: the card stays. The same happens in an open pin thread's Reply box.
kept.fix: Handle Escape on the TextArea itself (onKeyDown: if e.key === 'Escape' call onCancel / onClose), or use onKeyDownCapture on the card's root, which runs before react-aria stops propagation. Mirror the fix on the client link, which uses the same components.

verdict.reason: The bug is real. I confirmed it from the code; I didn't run it on :3012. Both cards pass an `onKeyDown` to the DS `TextArea` (pin-card.tsx:62 and :81) for the Cmd/Ctrl+Enter shortcut. react-aria wraps that handler with `createEventHandler` (node_modules/react-aria/dist/private/interactions/createEventHandler.mjs), which calls `e.stopPropagation()` on every key unless the handler calls `continuePropagation()`. So Escape never reaches the card root's `onKeyDown` (lines 44–45 and 77–78). The window handler in visualizer-editor.tsx:503–509 returns early while the target is a textarea, so its `if (draftPin) setDraftPin(null)` never runs either. `DraftPin` autofocuses its textarea, so Esc is dead in the usual case. The same components are used on the client share page (components/visualizer/share/render-share-page.tsx), so it has the same bug. I'd lower the severity to minor: Cancel and the close button still work, and nothing is lost or blocked. Only the Esc shortcut fails.
verdict.fix: The fix is only in components/visualizer/editor/pin-card.tsx. Inside each `TextArea`'s existing `onKeyDown`, handle Escape first: `if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.preventDefault(); onCancel() /* PinThread: onClose() */; return }`, then keep the Cmd/Ctrl+Enter branch. react-aria still stops propagation, so the window handler won't also fire. An alternative is to change the card roots' `onKeyDown` to `onKeyDownCapture`, which runs before react-aria. Either way, keep the root handler for Esc when focus is on the card's buttons. The client share page imports the same `DraftPin` / `PinThread`, so this one change fixes it too. Probe: open a draft pin, type, press Esc and expect `[data-testid=viz-pin-draft]` count 0. Open a thread, focus Reply, press Esc and expect `[data-testid=viz-pin-thread]` count 0.

kept.title: Keyboard focus drops to <body> after Generate, after a render lands, and after closing a pin
kept.evidence: gen2.cjs: 'focus during run: BODY' and 'focus after run: BODY' (Generate disables itself, so the running card's Cancel is never focused). kb.cjs 6c: after 'Close the pin' focus is BODY. kb2.cjs A and C: after Esc or Cancel on the draft pin focus is BODY. A keyboard user has to Tab from the top bar again, and can't reach the running card's Cancel quickly (motion-a11y/running.png).
kept.repro: 1) Tab to Generate with a pending finish and press Enter, then check document.activeElement. 2) Open pin 1 on V2 with Enter and press the thread's Close.
kept.fix: In stage.tsx, when running goes from null to set, focus the running card's Cancel (a ref plus useEffect). When the run ends, focus the new version's strip tile (data-testid viz-version, key saved.keys[0]) or the Generate button. Keep an opener ref for pins: PinThread onClose and DraftPin onCancel/onSave return focus to the pin button, or to the pin tool when drafting.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this by reading the code and did not re-run it live. The auditor's traces fit what the code does.
- **During a run:** `generate()` sets `running`, and `GenerateFooter` gives Generate `isDisabled={... || busy}` (rail.tsx:78/98). The button that had focus becomes disabled, so focus falls to `<body>`.
- **In the running card:** stage.tsx:148-161 renders the card with a Cancel button, but nothing moves focus there.
- **When a run ends:** `stop()` / `cancelRun()` just call `setRunning(null)` and focus nothing.
- **Pins:** `PinThread` / `DraftPin` are `role="dialog"` cards that unmount on Close, Escape, Cancel or Save (`setActivePin(null)` / `setDraftPin(null)` at visualizer-editor.tsx:487/494/509-510/602/604), and nothing records or restores what opened them.
- **The house pattern:** the house already has the contract the editor skips. om/dialog, drawer and sheet all return focus to the opener through `useDialogFocus` in components/om/surface.ts, but the visualizer's pin cards don't use it.

Keyboard users lose their place on the main Generate loop, so major is fair.
verdict.fix:
Reuse the house focus contract rather than hand-rolled refs where possible:
1) **Pin cards.** In pin-card.tsx, have PinThread and DraftPin each call `useDialogFocus(true, cardRef, { trap: false })` from components/om/surface.ts on their root div, the same way Drawer does. Focus then moves into the card on open (the Reply / note field) and goes back to the opener on unmount. This covers Close, Escape, Cancel and Save in one place. If the opener unmounts because a draft saved into a new pin, fall back to that new pin's marker button: after `savePin` sets `activePin`, the thread opens and its own unmount will return to the marker. Otherwise fall back to the pin tool, `data-testid="viz-pin-toggle"`.
2) **During a run.** In stage.tsx, add a ref on the running card's Cancel Button. Add a `useEffect` keyed on `!!running` that focuses it when the run starts, but only if `document.activeElement` is body or the now-disabled Generate. That way a mouse user's focus isn't taken.
3) **After a run.** In visualizer-editor.tsx, keep a "focus after run" flag. It is set when Generate was pressed by keyboard, or when focus was lost to body. When `stop()` lands with a saved version, focus that version's strip tile (versions-strip.tsx `data-testid="viz-version"` for `saved.keys[0]`, via a ref or `querySelector`). On cancel or error, focus the Generate button, which `busy` has re-enabled by then.
4) Extend the visualizer keyboard probe (the auditor's gen2 / kb / kb2 checks) to assert `activeElement` after each of the three flows at 1440.

kept.title: Client link: 'Your favourite' is a disabled, half-opacity button, which reads as unavailable and fails contrast
kept.evidence: motion-a11y/final-d-share.png and sm-thread.png: the chosen card's button is washed-out lilac. Computed style: bg rgb(85,0,255) at opacity 0.5 with white text ≈ 2.9:1 against the white card (WCAG AA needs 4.5:1). The aria snapshot reads 'button "Your favourite" [disabled]'. Code: render-share-page.tsx:136, isDisabled={favourite}. The selected state is shown as the disabled state, and the client can't take the pick back.
kept.repro: Open /renders/17fe84ab2eca47 and look at V2's first action button.
kept.fix: Keep the button enabled with aria-pressed={favourite}. Style the pressed state as the house selected chip (primary-variant background, primary text, filled star), matching the favBadge at the card's top. Pressing it again can say 'Already your favourite' or unpick. Never use isDisabled for a chosen state.

verdict.reason:
The observation is real. At render-share-page.tsx:136 the chosen card's button is `<Button appearance="filled" variant="primary" … isDisabled={favourite}>Your favourite</Button>`, and the vendored DS rule `._button_…[data-disabled]{opacity:.5}` renders it as washed-out primary at half opacity. Assistive tech announces it as "[disabled]". So the picked state is presented as an unavailable control, and a client can reasonably read it as "this didn't work".

Two parts of the finding overstate it:
1. **The contrast claim.** WCAG 1.4.3 exempts inactive (disabled) components, so this is not a formal AA failure. The problem is how the state reads, not a compliance violation.
2. **"The client can't take the pick back."** Not accurate. `like(key)` just calls setFav(key) and pickFavourite(token, key), so pressing "I like this one" on another version moves the favourite. There is one favourite per share, and it moves between versions.

The card already shows the choice with the primary border and the favBadge ("Your favourite", filled star). The button only needs to stop looking dead. Severity: minor, not major.
verdict.fix:
1. In components/visualizer/share/render-share-page.tsx:136, drop `isDisabled={favourite}` and add `aria-pressed={favourite}` (pass it through, or wrap it if the DS Button won't forward it). Keep the existing filled primary look and the filled star, which is the DS's own selected look. This needs no new CSS, so skip the invented chip styling from the finding.
2. In `like()` (around line 30), return early when `key === fav`, so pressing the chosen button again neither re-posts nor re-snacks.
3. Don't add an unpick action. The favourite already moves when the client picks another version, and an "un-favourite" flow would be invented UI.

render-share-page.module.css needs no change.

kept.title: Pin mode has no banner and no toggle state; pin and place modes are pointer-only
kept.where: Editor canvas bar and stage, 1440 and 390
kept.evidence: motion-a11y/pin-draft.png and m-pin-mode.png: after pressing the pin tool only the icon tints. No banner says what to do, although place and draw modes get one (stage.tsx banner) and the client link shows 'Tap the picture where you’d like a change' (render-share-page.tsx:133). The toggle has no aria-pressed (kb2.cjs C2 outerHTML: IconButton emits only data-selected), and neither do the compact Compare or tune toggles. kept.fix: Add kind 'pin' to Stage's banner ('Click the photo where the note goes' with Cancel, and 'Tap…' on touch), using the client link's wording. Keyboard alternative: in place or pin mode make the frame focusable; Enter drops at the centre, and arrows move a crosshair before Enter.

verdict.reason: The code confirms the observation. stage.tsx:90-92 builds a banner only for place, draw and remove. Its own header comment (line 28) says "remove and pin modes own the pointer with a banner", yet pin mode gets none, so pressing the pin tool only tints the icon (visualizer-editor.tsx:582). The client share page does show a hint for the same action ("Tap the picture where you’d like a change", render-share-page.tsx:133), so the editor is out of step with it. IconButton (components/om/icon-button.tsx) emits only data-selected, never aria-pressed. The narrow Compare and Pin toggles pass `selected` alone, while the wide Compare button already sets aria-pressed. Place, pin and draw are handled only in the stage's pointer handlers (stage.tsx:73-75), and the stage has no tabIndex or onKeyDown. So the finding is real. I would lower it from major to minor. The Pin button's tooltip already reads "Stop pinning", a click anywhere on the photo gives a visible result right away, and the missing banner is a small gap next to the other modes. The proposed keyboard crosshair (arrow keys, then Enter) is new interaction design that no mock or house rule asks for. It goes beyond the stated intent for a demo prototype.

1. In stage.tsx, add pin to the banner ternary, reusing the place/draw banner pattern and the client link's wording: `mode.kind === 'pin' ? { text: 'Tap the photo where you’d like the note', cancel: mode.onCancel }` with the push_pin icon. Add `onCancel` to the pin mode type. In visualizer-editor.tsx:241, pass `onCancel: () => { setPinning(false); setDraftPin(null) }` and hide the banner while a draft pin is open (the same `!draft` rule the share page uses). Fix the header comment to match.
2. Pass `aria-pressed` at the call sites rather than changing IconButton globally, since `selected` also marks non-toggle states elsewhere. The attribute goes through because IconButton spreads `...rest`. Add `aria-pressed={pinning}` on viz-pin-toggle, `aria-pressed={compare.on}` on the narrow viz-compare-toggle, and the same on the narrow tune toggle.
3. For keyboard reach, keep it minimal. In place or pin mode, make the stage frame focusable (tabIndex=0, an aria-label from the banner text) and let Enter call onPlace or onAdd at the centre of the view; Escape already cancels. Do not build the arrow-key crosshair unless the owner asks, and log it as a REG entry if it is built.
Then run a Playwright check at 1440 and 390: the banner appears and cancels, and the pin toggle's aria-pressed flips.

kept.title: Editor route ghost doesn't match the editor, and the swap is a hard cut (no PageReveal)
kept.evidence: motion-a11y/ghost-d-editor.png vs final-d-editor.png: the photo bone is 900x600 at x84,y176, while the real photo is 1004x672 at x32,y160. The rail has four 56px bones where the real rail is one accordion card. The rail foot is one 40px bone where the real foot (Describe, Generate, hint and options) is ~210px. The Share bone is 96px against the real 169px, and the strip has no VERSIONS head. ghost-m-editor.png vs final-m-editor.png: no rooms row, no go bar, and the top bar's 96px end bone runs past 390. The editor isn't wrapped in PageReveal, unlike quote-editor.tsx:525 and file-viewer.tsx:102, so the ghost snaps to content.
kept.repro: Load the editor on a slow network (or render only the streamed fallback: ghosts3.cjs) and compare with the loaded page.
kept.fix: Rebuild VisualizerEditorSkeleton from the real metrics: stage padding 32, photo 3:2 filling the stage, rail = tab row + one card + foot (describe 60 + Generate 40 + 2 caption lines), strip = 72px head + 128x80 tiles with labels, Share bone 169. ≤1024: add the rooms row and go bar, and drop the wide Share bone for a 36px icon. Wrap VisualizerEditor's return in <PageReveal skeleton={<VisualizerEditorSkeleton/>}>, with GhostSheet in the skeleton so the clock stamps.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds up in the code and in the screenshots. `VisualizerEditor` (components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:618) returns its editor div directly, with no PageReveal. The quote editor (quote-editor.tsx:525) and the file viewer (file-viewer.tsx:102) both wrap theirs, and skeletons.module.css line 1 itself says these ghosts exist "so the PageReveal crossfade lands in place". So the loading.tsx ghost is swapped for the page in a hard cut. `VisualizerEditorSkeleton` is also a bare div rather than a `GhostSheet`. That means it never stamps `ghostClock` or syncs the sweep delay, and a later PageReveal could not detect a warm navigation.

Comparing ghost-d-editor.png with final-d-editor.png:
- **Photo:** the photo bone (900 wide, 24px padding, centred) sits inset from the real photo, which fills the stage from x≈35.
- **Rail:** the rail has four 56px bones where the real rail has a two-line section head plus one accordion card.
- **Rail foot:** one 40px bone stands in for a ~210px block (DESCRIBE label, textarea, Generate, two caption lines).
- **Share button:** its bone is 96 wide against the real ~169.
- **Strip:** there is no VERSIONS/count column, and the tiles have no label line.

At 390 (ghost-m-editor.png) the top bar's end bones overflow the right edge (the 96px Share bone is clipped). The ghost also has no rooms-chip row and no go bar, even though the real phone layout renders a `roomsRow`. The hint note can't be ghosted because it depends on per-viewer state, and leaving it out is correct.

Severity is minor: this only shows on a cold load or navigation and does not block anything. It is still real polish drift from the house rule that every screen ships a matching ghost plus PageReveal (CLAUDE.md rule 4).
verdict.fix:
1. **components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:** wrap the returned tree in `<PageReveal skeleton={<VisualizerEditorSkeleton />}>`, importing it from '@/components/shell/page-reveal', as quote-editor.tsx does. Keep the `.editor` fixed frame inside it.

2. **components/visualizer/skeletons.tsx:** render `VisualizerEditorSkeleton` inside `GhostSheet` (label "Loading the design") so the clock stamps and the sweep stays in phase. Add a skeleton class that neutralises GhostSheet's page-body padding if needed, so the fixed frame still covers the viewport. Rebuild it from the editor's real metrics:
   - **Top bar:** back 24 · title 120 + chip 40 · three room chips + more + an Add room 120 bone · end = undo/redo 2×24 + a Share bone of 169×36.
   - **Stage:** padding 32 (top 60 for the version pill bone ~160×28), with the photo filling the stage width at 3:2 (drop the 900 cap). Add a 430×44 tool-bar bone under the photo.
   - **Rail:** a tab row of 5 icon+label bones (~52×36) · a head block (title 140×16 + caption 2 lines) · one bordered card with three 48px rows · a foot pinned to the bottom with a caption label, a 60px textarea bone, a 40px Generate bone and two centred caption lines.
   - **Strip:** a left head column (VERSIONS 60×12 + count 16×20) in place of the 104px padding hack, plus 128×80 tiles, each with a 90×12 label bone below.

3. **components/visualizer/skeletons.module.css:** add rules for the new pieces using --om-spacing and --om-radius tokens. At ≤1024:

   - swap the Share bone for a 36×36 icon bone and drop the undo/redo bones;
   - keep the go bar above the dock (describe + Generate bones);
   - give `.top` `min-width: 0; overflow: hidden` and let the title bone shrink, so nothing runs past 390.

4. **Verify** ghost against final at 1440 and at 390 touch, plus the 320 overflow gate, with the audit's ghosts3.cjs.

kept.title: Client link ghost is 120px short of the real page and has no crossfade
kept.evidence: motion-a11y/ghost-d-share.png vs final-d-share.png: the ghost card starts at y248 but the real first card is at y368, because the ghost lacks the tip line and the 'Living room' heading. The ghost top bar has no logo and no 'Open until' pill. The page isn't wrapped in PageReveal, so the client sees a hard jump. This is the first impression a homeowner gets from WhatsApp.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this by reading the code and comparing the 1440 ghost and final screenshots. The ghost's card starts at about y248 and the real first card at about y368. Two things cause the gap:
- `RenderShareSkeleton` (`components/visualizer/skeletons.tsx`, lines 36–46) has no bone for the tip line (`.how`, the "Tap I like this one…" line), which the page always renders.

In `components/visualizer/skeletons.tsx` `RenderShareSkeleton`, make the ghost match the real page:

The ghost then crossfades into the page instead of cutting. Check the result with the slow-network probe (`ghosts3.cjs`) at 1440 and 390, and with reduced motion on.

kept.title: Panning a zoomed photo lags far behind the pointer
kept.evidence: pan.cjs: while dragging 200px, the computed translateX read 0,0,1,3,6,9,12,17,21,27, and it settled to 200 only after release. stage.module.css .viewport has `transition: transform var(--motion-toggle)` always on, so every pointermove animates for 150ms and the photo trails the hand.
kept.repro: Editor, Zoom in twice, drag the photo sideways.
kept.fix: Set data-panning on .viewport while drag.current is set and add `.viewport[data-panning] { transition: none; }`. Keep the transition for button and wheel zooms.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this from the code; I didn't re-run it live because the code path settles it. In stage.module.css line 6, `.viewport` always has `transition: transform var(--motion-toggle)`, which is 150ms ease per globals.css:276. In stage.tsx, `onFrameMove` calls `setPan` on every pointermove (line 80), and that writes a new inline `transform: translate(...) scale(...)` onto the same `.viewport` (line 107). Each move restarts the 150ms ease from the photo's current in-between position, so the photo trails the pointer while dragging and only catches up after release. That matches the auditor's translateX samples. Nothing in the code turns the transition off during a drag: `data-grab` only reflects zoom > 1 in view mode and only sets the cursor. Studios will feel this on every pan at 125–300%. Minor severity is right. One detail in the proposed fix needs changing: `drag` is a ref, and the house ESLint rule forbids reading refs during render. `data-panning` must come from state, not from `drag.current`.
verdict.fix:
In components/visualizer/editor/stage.tsx, add `const [panning, setPanning] = useState(false)`. Set it true in `onFrameDown` in the same place `drag.current` is set (the zoom > 1 branch). Set it false in `onFrameUp` and in the `onPointerCancel` handler, next to `drag.current = null`. On the `.viewport` div, add `data-panning={panning || undefined}` next to `data-grab`. Don't read `drag.current` in render.

In components/visualizer/editor/stage.module.css, add:

- `.viewport[data-panning] .frame { cursor: grabbing; }`, so the hand closes while dragging.
