I read the code and it matches the report. `fileVersion` (app/visualizer/actions.ts:253-261) looks for an existing file only by the name `Render - ${room} - V${n}.jpg` inside the Renders folder. `renameRoom` (line 151) never checks for duplicate names, while `addRoom` (lines 139-141) adds a suffix. Share goes through the same `fileVersion` (line 319). So once two live rooms share a name, the second room's matching V-number never gets filed: the snackbar says it is "already in Files", and Open lands on the other room's picture. The auditor's screenshots (f-dup-names.png, f-save-dup.png, f-opened-file.png) show this. The same name key causes two more problems the finding doesn't mention: 1. Rename room A after it has been filed, then give room B A's old name, and B's V3 matches A's old file. 2. Renaming a room and saving again files the same render a second time under the new name. Why minor: the only way to get two rooms with the same name is for a user to rename one to match another. Nothing is lost, because the render stays in the editor and Share still works; the harm is a misleading filing.
verdict.fix:
1. In app/visualizer/actions.ts, make `renameRoom` refuse a name another live room in the same design already has, excluding the room itself. Return `{ error: 'Another room in this design is already called “X”.' }` so the rename field shows it, the same way other duplicate-name errors do. Don't auto-suffix: `addRoom`'s suffix is for default names the user didn't type.
2. Look filed renders up by the version, not by the file name. No migration is needed. `renderUrl(jobId, v)` is already stored in `lead_files.thumb`, and for uploaded or generated images (data: URLs) it is `/visualizer/img/v/${jobId}/${v.id}`, which is unique per version. In `fileVersion`, match on `thumb = renderUrl(jobId, v)` inside the Renders folder and keep the name for display only.
3. Sample renders keep their static image path, which may repeat across rooms. For those, match on thumb and name together, or add an additive `lead_files.render_key` column (`jobId:variantId`, migration 0055, added to the baseline lists) if the two sample rooms can share a path.
4. Log the change in design-source/REGISTER.md as a bug fix.
5. Add these checks to the visualizer probe: rename a room to a taken name and it is refused; two rooms' V3 each file separately; renaming a room and saving again does not file a duplicate.

kept.title: Deleting a design says “Shared links stop working” but the client link keeps working
kept.evidence: ConfirmDialog copy in visualizer-editor.tsx (‘Its rooms and versions go to Deleted designs… Shared links stop working.’, b-confirm.png). deleteDesigns() only stamps deleted_at; fetchShare()/openLink() never look at the design (or the lead) — live: after Delete (deleted_at=1790359823) /renders/17fe84ab2eca47 still rendered all 3 versions with pins and actions (b-share-after-delete.png) and the client could still like/pin/call back.
kept.repro: Open Kevin Ng's design › ⋮ › Delete design › Delete; open /renders/17fe84ab2eca47 in another tab.
kept.fix: In lib/visualizer/queries.ts fetchShare() and app/renders/actions.ts openLink(), join visualizer_designs (and leads.deleted_at) and return state 'stopped' when the design is deleted; restoreDesigns() brings them back automatically. Alternatively revoke live links in deleteDesigns() and un-revoke those same ids on restore (store `revoked_by_delete`).

verdict.reason: I confirmed this from the code and did not repeat the live delete, because other agents share the :3011 DB. The Delete dialog in components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:723 promises "Shared links stop working." But deleteDesigns() in app/visualizer/actions.ts:104-113 only sets visualizer_designs.deleted_at and deleted_by. It never touches render_share_links. The share page app/renders/[token]/page.tsx takes its state from fetchShare() in lib/visualizer/queries.ts:178-204. That state comes only from s.revokedAt and s.expiresAt, with no read of visualizer_designs.deletedAt, so a deleted design's link still shows as 'open', with its versions and pins. The client's writes go through openLink() in app/renders/actions.ts:20-25, which also checks only revokedAt and expiresAt. So after a delete, pickFavourite, leaveNote and askCallBack all still succeed. askCallBack also creates a Follow-up task, and each of the three sends a render_feedback notification whose href points at a design that is in the trash. Only Delete forever, which removes the rows by cascade, actually stops the link. The copy is false and the client can keep writing into a trashed record, so major is the right severity (it is a broken promise more than a data leak).
verdict.fix: Work the design's deleted_at into the link's state when it is read, rather than revoking the links. That way Restore brings the links back on its own and no extra column is needed. (1) In lib/visualizer/queries.ts fetchShare(), also select visualizerDesigns.deletedAt for s.designId (and leads.deletedAt when s.leadId is set). Return state 'stopped' when either is set: `state: s.revokedAt || designGone ? 'stopped' : expired ? 'expired' : 'open'`. The page then shows the existing RenderLinkClosed 'stopped' screen, so no new UI is needed. (2) In app/renders/actions.ts openLink(), join or look up the same design (and lead) and return null when it is deleted. Every client action and stampShareView then refuses with the existing "This link has expired…" error. A 'stopped' wording would be nicer if the Err copy already has one. (3) restoreDesigns() in app/visualizer/actions.ts should also revalidatePath each live link's `/renders/${token}` path, or just rely on force-dynamic, which is already set, so no change is strictly needed. (4) Optional: the editor's Shared links list can show deleted designs' links as stopped. No schema change and no new copy.

kept.title: Switching rooms during Generate shows the other room's render running over the wrong photo
kept.where: Editor, Generate in progress, then a room chip · 1440
kept.evidence: `running` and `inFlight` are editor-global (visualizer-editor.tsx generate()), not per room. Live: started a Kitchen Generate, clicked Master bedroom: the progress card ‘Rendering… Laying your finishes’ sits over the bedroom photo and a ‘Rendering…’ ghost tile appears in the bedroom's strip (i-switch-during-run.png); when done the snackbar says ‘V4 is ready’ with Compare while the bedroom has only V1 (i-switch-after.png) — Compare then acts on the bedroom.
kept.repro: Kitchen › pick Floor › Cool Grey › Generate › immediately click ‘Master bedroom’ in the top bar.
kept.fix: Store the run with its room: `running: { roomId, … }`; pass `running` / `inFlight` to Stage and VersionsStrip only when `running.roomId === roomId` (show a small ‘Rendering in Kitchen…’ chip on the Kitchen room chip otherwise); the success snackbar names the room and its Compare action first does setRoomPick(room.id).

verdict.reason:
The code matches what the auditor described. In visualizer-editor.tsx, `running` / `inFlight` (lines 148–149) are single editor-wide useState values with no room attached. They are passed to Stage (line 590) and VersionsStrip (line 608) whatever `roomId` is on screen. The success snackbar's Compare (`setCompare({ on: true, key: null })`) acts on whichever room is showing when it is pressed.

The generate() closure does capture the Kitchen's `room`, `patch`, `all` and `viewKey`, so the new versions, viewKeys and afterRender all correctly go to the Kitchen. The data is right; only what the screen shows is wrong.

The auditor's screenshots show it:
- i-switch-during-run.png: the Kitchen's 'Rendering… Laying your finishes' card sits over the blurred Master bedroom photo. The bedroom strip shows a 'Rendering…' ghost tile, and the bedroom's Generate button says 'Rendering…'.
- i-switch-after.png: the bedroom has only V1, yet the snackbar says 'V4 is ready' with Compare. That Compare would open on the bedroom.

A few more knock-on effects:
- Cancel on the bedroom stops the Kitchen's run.
- The bedroom's Generate is blocked (`busy={!!running}`) with no reason given.
- The bedroom photo is blurred for the whole run.

In a live demo a studio moving between rooms while a render runs will see the wrong room "rendering" and a V4 that isn't there. That is major for a pitch prototype, even though no data is lost.
verdict.fix:
In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:
1. Add `roomId: string; roomName: string` to the Running value that generate() stores: `setRunning({ title, step: 0, steps, roomId: room.id, roomName: room.name })`. Keep `inFlight` next to it, or fold it into running as `count`.
2. Derive `const here = running && running.roomId === roomId ? running : null`.
   - Pass `here` to Stage (running=) and `here ? inFlight : 0` to VersionsStrip.
   - Gate the lighting preview (`!running` in hlKey / pvKey / preview) on `here` instead of `running`, so the other room's photo isn't blurred and its lighting preview keeps working.
   - Leave the Generate button disabled while any run is going (one run at a time is fine), but when `running && !here` show the hint "Rendering in {running.roomName}…" through the existing error/hint line of the Generate panel. Don't add a new chip.
3. Give the success snackbar the room's name when it isn't the room on screen, e.g. `Kitchen · V4 is ready`. Its Compare should first call `setRoomPick(room.id)` and then `setCompare({ on: true, key: null })`. That uses the closure's `room`, which is the Kitchen.
4. Leave cancelRun as it is. It is only reachable from the Stage card, which now shows only in the room that is running.

In stage.tsx / versions-strip.tsx, extend the `Running` type in stage.tsx with the optional room fields. No other prop changes are needed, and no new UI is invented.

Verify: Kitchen › Floor › Cool Grey › Generate, then click Master bedroom.
- The bedroom should show no card, no ghost and no blur.
- The snackbar should say "Kitchen · V4 is ready".
- Compare should land on the Kitchen, showing V4 against its parent.

kept.title: A removed swatch or material leaves a dangling pick; Generate then keeps a no-change version
kept.where: Editor › Surfaces picker ‘Your studio’ (own swatch ×, or a studio material deleted in Company › Materials) · 1440
kept.evidence: removeOwnSwatch()/deleteStudioMaterials() never prune pending.materials; resolve() returns null and runPass skips it (run.ts ~151 `if (!def || !picked) continue`), but intentFor still counts it. Live: after removing the swatch the rail still shows ‘Walls → a finish’ and ‘Now: As in the photo · →’ (c-swatch-undo.png); pressing Generate saved ‘V2 · Edit’ with applied.surfaces [] — a copy of V1 (d-dangling.png, DB variants_json materials []), and Activity now reads ‘You rendered V2 of “Kitchen” — Edit.’
kept.repro: Kitchen › Walls › Have a sample? › upload › switch off ‘Save to the studio’ › Use in this design; remove the swatch tile (×); Generate.
kept.fix: (1) In removeOwn/removeOwnSwatch and when library materials change, drop pending.materials entries whose id no longer resolves (patch with history so Undo restores both). (2) intentFor() should count only resolvable picks (pass resolve in). (3) runPass should return `fail('Nothing changed…')` when applied has no surfaces/furniture/style/light, so no empty version is saved.

verdict.reason:
The bug is real, and I reproduced it from both the code and the auditor's screenshots. `removeOwn()` (visualizer-editor.tsx:394) calls `removeOwnSwatch` and refreshes, but it never clears `pending.materials` entries that point at `own:<id>`.

Three things follow from that dangling pick:
- **Rail and button still count it.** `intentFor()` (model.ts:149) counts any pick on a visible surface without checking that it resolves, so it returns kind 'edit' and a live Generate. The rail's changes list shows 'Walls → a finish' (the `resolve(mid)?.name ?? 'a finish'` fallback at editor:279).
- **Generate saves a copy.** `editPass` skips the pick (`if (!def || !picked) continue`, run.ts:~153) and returns a variant with `applied.surfaces` empty. `generate()` (editor:160-165) saves any non-error output, so 'V2 · Edit' is kept as a copy of the version it came from. d-dangling.png shows exactly this: V2 · Edit, every surface 'As in the photo', 'V2 is ready'.
- **Activity records it.** Activity then logs a render that changed nothing.

Two corrections to the report:
- **The Company › Materials path is theoretical.** `pending` lives only in editor state and is never persisted (the only localStorage key is the recents list). To get a dangling pick that way, a material would have to be deleted in another tab and the editor tab refreshed. The own-swatch × inside the editor is the realistic trigger.
- **Severity should be minor, not major.** Nothing is lost or corrupted. The result is one redundant version the studio can delete, but it looks broken in a demo.

The fix stays small and uses no new UI.
verdict.fix:
1. **Stop dangling picks at the source.** In `visualizer-editor.tsx`, derive the live picks once: `const livePending = useMemo(() => ({ ...pending, materials: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(pending.materials).filter(([, m]) => resolve(m))) }), [pending, resolve])`. Use `livePending` for `intentFor`, the changes list, `marks`, the markers and the `pending` passed to `runPass`. This covers both the own-swatch × and a library row that vanished after `router.refresh()`, without an extra history entry.
2. **Clean up on remove.** In `removeOwn()`, also `patch((p) => ({ ...p, materials: omit(p.materials, Object.keys(p.materials).filter((k) => p.materials[k] === `own:${id}`)) }))`. The snackbar's Undo then restores the swatch and calls `ed.undo(roomId)` to put the pick back, the same way `forget()` already does.
3. **Guard in the engine.** At the end of `editPass` in `lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts`, return `fail('Nothing changed — pick a finish, a style or a light first.')` when every variant's `applied` has no surfaces, no furniture, no style, no lighting and no note. That way the engine never hands back an empty version. The wording reuses `intentFor`'s existing "Pick a finish, a style or a light first."

Log it in REGISTER.md as a bug fix.

kept.title: Undo after removing an uploaded swatch silently does nothing
kept.where: Editor › Surfaces › Your studio › swatch × › snackbar Undo · 1440
kept.evidence: The page's own swatches carry `/visualizer/img/d/{designId}/{id}` addresses (queries.ts ownImage); Undo re-sends that object to saveOwnSwatch(), whose cleanImage() only accepts data URLs or sample paths → returns { error } which is `void`ed. Live: custom_json after add = [{…data:image/jpeg…}], after remove = [], after Undo = [] (c-payload.cjs output; c-swatch-undo.png shows no swatch back and no error).
kept.repro: Upload a swatch into the design (not the studio), press its ×, press Undo in the snackbar.
kept.fix: Make it a soft remove: keep the swatch in custom_json with `removedAt` and have removeOwnSwatch/restoreOwnSwatch(designId, id) flip it (parseOwn filters removed); or keep the removed entry (with its stored data URL) server-side for Undo. Surface a ‘Couldn’t bring back …’ snackbar when the restore returns an error.

verdict.reason: The code path matches the report exactly. `fetch…` in lib/visualizer/queries.ts:142 swaps each own swatch's stored data URL for `/visualizer/img/d/{designId}/{id}` through `ownImage`. In visualizer-editor.tsx:394-397, `removeOwn` hands that client copy `s` back to `saveOwnSwatch` on Undo. In app/visualizer/actions.ts:218-221, `saveOwnSwatch` runs `cleanImage(s.imageUrl)`, which only accepts `data:image/...;base64` or `/visualizer/(samples|demo)/…jpg`. So an image swatch returns `{ error: 'We can read JPG, PNG and WebP swatches up to 10 MB.' }`, and `void …then(() => router.refresh())` throws that away. The swatch is gone for good because its data URL was deleted from custom_json by `removeOwnSwatch`, the Undo snackbar says nothing, and surfaces that used `own:{id}` are left pointing at nothing. Only hex-only swatches (imageUrl null) come back through Undo, and even they return at the end of the list. It breaks the house rule that Undo on every remove works and that a refused write says what failed, so major is fair. I didn't rerun it live because the code shows it without doubt and the auditor's payload trace agrees.
verdict.fix: Make the remove soft on the server instead of re-uploading from the client. (1) lib/visualizer/materials.ts: add an optional `removedAt?: number` to `OwnSwatch`. (2) app/visualizer/actions.ts: `removeOwnSwatch(designId, id)` sets `removedAt: Date.now()` on the entry instead of filtering it out, and returns `{ ok: true } | Err`. Add `restoreOwnSwatch(designId, id)` that clears `removedAt` so the swatch goes back in its original place with its stored data URL. `saveOwnSwatch` counts and trims (`slice(-40)`) only live entries, and purges entries removed more than about a day ago on the next write. (3) lib/visualizer/queries.ts: filter `removedAt` entries out of `design.own` (and anywhere else `parseOwn` feeds the UI or `resolveMaterial`). Leave the `/visualizer/img/d/[...key]` route serving the entry so a restored swatch's picture loads. (4) components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx `removeOwn`: check the remove result (on an error, `snack({ message: 'Couldn’t remove <name>' })` and stop). Undo calls `restoreOwnSwatch(data.design.id, s.id)` and on `{ error }` or a throw shows `Couldn’t bring back <name>`, else runs `router.refresh()`, using the house snackbar pattern from the UI sweep.

kept.title: The client link's view count counts the client's own clicks (and every revalidation)
kept.where: /renders/[token]; Share dialog ‘opened N×’; Activity ‘opened the shared renders (N times)’
kept.evidence: stampShareView() runs inside the page's server render (app/renders/[token]/page.tsx), and every client action calls revalidatePath('/renders/token') plus router.refresh(). Live: view_count 3 → 4 on open, → 6 after one ‘I like this one’ (a-views.cjs). Activity now says ‘Kevin Ng opened the shared renders (7 times)’ (k-activity.cjs) after 3 real opens; the share dialog shows the same inflated number to the studio.
kept.repro: Note view_count for 17fe84ab2eca47; open /renders/17fe84ab2eca47; press I like this one; re-read view_count.
kept.fix: Count from the browser once per page load: a tiny client effect in RenderSharePage calls stampShareView(token) on mount (guarded with a ref / sessionStorage key per token per day), and remove the call from page.tsx; skip counting when a studio session opens it (Preview) if that can be told apart.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed from the code. `app/renders/[token]/page.tsx:26` calls `await stampShareView(token)` while the page renders on the server, and the page is `force-dynamic`. Every client action in `app/renders/actions.ts` (pickFavourite, leaveNote, askCallBack, clientPin, clientReply) ends with `refresh(s)`, which calls `revalidatePath('/renders/' + token)`. A server action that revalidates the page it was called from re-renders that page, and that re-render stamps a view. `render-share-page.tsx` then also calls `router.refresh()` (lines 36, 101, 111, 131, 177), which renders it again. So each client action adds about 2 to the count. That matches the auditor's live numbers (open 3→4, one "I like this one" 4→6).

`lastViewedAt` is also moved on every action, so two places read inflated data: the Activity line in `lib/leads/activity.ts:136` ("opened the shared renders (N times)", timed at the last action) and the share dialog's "opened N×" (`share-dialog.tsx:121`). The studio treats that number as a signal of client interest, so a wrong count misleads them. I'm keeping it at major because it feeds the Activity feed and the dialog directly.

I did not re-run the live probe. The code path is clear and the auditor's numbers are consistent with it.
verdict.fix:
1. Remove `await stampShareView(token)` from `app/renders/[token]/page.tsx`, so the server render never writes.

2. In `components/visualizer/share/render-share-page.tsx` (RenderSharePage, which already has `'use client'`), add one mount effect that calls `stampShareView(data.token)` once per page load.
   - Guard it with a `useRef` so StrictMode's double mount doesn't count twice.
   - Also guard it with a per-tab `sessionStorage` key, `om.renders.viewed.<token>`, wrapped in try/catch, so a reload in the same tab doesn't count again.
   - Ignore errors; nothing in the UI changes.
   - Keep the rule "no setState in the effect body". This effect only fires the action.

3. In `app/renders/actions.ts`, keep `stampShareView` as the only writer. Have it check `openLink(token)` first, so a closed or expired link isn't counted. It must not call `revalidatePath` on `/renders/<token>`.

4. Optional: to stop the studio counting its own opens, skip the stamp when the viewer is the studio. For example, when the share dialog's own preview opens the link it could add `?preview=1`, and the effect would skip on that. Only do this if the dialog has a preview path.

No new UI or copy. The dialog's "opened N×" and the Activity line then read true counts.

kept.title: Reference and piece photos are stored as data URLs in the room state and shipped in the page props
kept.where: Editor › Style › Upload a reference photo; Furniture › Replace › photo · any width
kept.evidence: addReference()/addPiecePhoto() put readFileAsDataUrl() results into pending.transfer.refs[].url / furniture[id].refImage; saveRoomState() writes them into project_rooms.state_json and fetchVisualizerEditor returns them as `pending`. Live: one reference → state_json 150,685 chars with data:image; the editor HTML grew from 72,667 to 223,494 bytes (c-payload.cjs). Up to 3 refs + piece photos per room, per room, and the whole blob is re-POSTed on every 900 ms autosave.
kept.repro: Kitchen › Style › Upload a reference photo › wait for ‘Saved’ › reload and compare the document size.
kept.fix: Store reference / piece photos like room photos: an action `saveRoomAsset(roomId, dataUrl)` writes them to a table (or a `room_assets` JSON column read only by the image route) and returns `/visualizer/img/ref/{roomId}/{id}`; pending keeps only that address. Serve through app/visualizer/img/[...key]/route.ts.

verdict.reason:
The mechanism is real, and it breaks the design's own rule. REG-673 built app/visualizer/img/[...key]/route.ts so that "a page's payload carries addresses" for room photos (room/), versions (v/), materials (m/) and own swatches (d/). Reference photos and piece photos were left out.

- **References.** addReference() (visualizer-editor.tsx:399-405) puts readFileAsDataUrl(f, 900) straight into pending.transfer.refs[].url.
- **Piece photos.** addPiecePhoto() (:408-412) puts readFileAsDataUrl(f, 600) into furniture[id].refImage.
- **Autosave.** The loop in use-editor-state.ts:52-67 sends the whole pending, data URLs included, to saveRoomState 900 ms after any change on that room, even a slider nudge.
- **Storage and reload.** saveRoomState (actions.ts:178-182) writes it to project_rooms.state_json. fetchVisualizerEditor (queries.ts:144) returns readPending(state_json) for every room in the page props.
- **Renders don't clear them.** afterRender (model.ts:96) keeps transfer.refs, so references stay in state for good.

I did not re-run the live size measurement. The scratch DB currently holds no data-URL refs (the auditor's test row was reverted), but the code path is plain.

Severity is overstated. On a local demo, a few hundred KB per room is not something a studio feels as slowness until several rooms carry three references each. At that point the page grows by about 0.5–1.5 MB and every tweak re-posts about 450 KB. It is a robustness and consistency gap, not a blocker, so I rate it minor. The fix belongs with the REG-673 rule.
verdict.fix:
Follow the REG-673 pattern.

1. **Migration.** Add an additive column `project_rooms.assets_json`: a JSON map of id to data URL, read only by the image route.
2. **Upload action.** Add `saveRoomAsset(roomId, dataUrl)` in app/visualizer/actions.ts. It runs cleanImage(), checks the room through roomFor(), writes the entry into assets_json and returns `{ id, url: '/visualizer/img/a/{roomId}/{id}' }`.
3. **Image route.** In app/visualizer/img/[...key]/route.ts, add a branch `kind === 'a'` that reads assets_json and hands the entry to send().
4. **Editor.** In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx, addReference() and addPiecePhoto() upload first and put only the returned address into refs[].url and refImage.
   - Compute the palette from the local data URL before the upload, as today.
   - If the upload fails, show a snackbar in the house style: "Couldn’t add that reference".
5. **Server guard.** In saveRoomState / readPending, drop any refs[].url or refImage that starts with `data:`, so state_json only ever holds addresses.
6. **Existing rows.** Add a repair rule in scripts/repair-demo-data.ts that moves any data-URL refs or refImages already in state_json into assets_json. Include assets_json in the baseline snapshot.

Removing a reference can leave its asset orphaned. That is acceptable, or it can be pruned in saveRoomState against the ids still referenced.

kept.title: Picks made in the last 900 ms are lost on Back or tab close; a failed autosave never retries
kept.evidence: The debounce effect's cleanup clears the timer on unmount and there is no flush/beforeunload. Live: picked Walls → Cool Grey (rail showed the change) and pressed Back within ~200 ms: state_json stayed null and reopening the room showed no changes (h-autosave.cjs). On an error the label stays ‘Not saved yet’ until the next edit.
kept.repro: Master bedroom › Walls › Cool Grey › immediately press the top-left Back.
kept.fix: In useEditorState: keep a `flush()` that saves every dirty room now; call it from the timer, from the effect cleanup on unmount (fire-and-forget), from `pagehide`/`visibilitychange` (navigator.sendBeacon is not available for server actions, so call the action), and from the Back handler before router.push. On error, schedule a retry (e.g. 3 s backoff) and show ‘Not saved — retrying’.

verdict.reason:
The code matches the finding exactly. In components/visualizer/editor/use-editor-state.ts, lines 55–68 hold the whole autosave: an effect keyed on `revs` sets a 900 ms timer and its cleanup is `return () => clearTimeout(t)`. There is no pagehide listener, no flush on unmount, and no flush path the editor can call. Every way out of the editor calls router.push straight away and unmounts the hook: the topbar Back (visualizer-editor.tsx:620, `onBack={() => router.push(back)}`), line 472, the room menu's "Open the lead" (693) and the snackbar "Open" actions (439, 479). So any pick made in the last 900 ms is thrown away. On failure the effect sets `error: true` but only runs again when `revs` changes, so nothing retries until the next edit. The label stays "Not saved yet" (line 621) with no sign it will try again. I didn't re-run the live check: the code path is deterministic, and the auditor's h-autosave.cjs already showed state_json null after Back.

The house already solves this in two other editors. The quote editor (quote-editor.tsx:189–208) keeps a `flushRef`, calls it on `pagehide` and in the unmount cleanup of an effect with empty deps. The template editor (template-editor.tsx:248) runs `await flush()` before `router.push`. The visualizer is the odd one out. Losing a colour pick a designer just made in front of a client is a real problem in a demo, so "major" stands.
verdict.fix:
Copy the quote editor's pattern; no new UI is needed.

1) In use-editor-state.ts, move the timer body into `flush = async () => {...}`. It clears any pending timer and saves every room whose `rev` is greater than `saved.current[id]`, as the timer does now. Hold it in `flushRef`, updated in an effect.

2) The revs effect keeps its debounce but only calls `flushRef.current()` from the timer.

3) Add a second effect with `[]` deps. It adds a `pagehide` listener that calls `void flushRef.current()`, and its cleanup removes the listener and fires `void flushRef.current()` on unmount. Put this in a separate effect so the per-change cleanup doesn't flush on every keystroke.

4) Return `flush` from the hook. In visualizer-editor.tsx, have onBack (line 620), the leave path at 472, "Open the lead" (693) and the snackbar router.push actions `await ed.flush()` before navigating, the way template-editor.tsx:248 does.

5) On error, let the flush schedule one retry after about 3 s by setting a `retry` tick in state that the debounce effect also depends on. Keep the existing label, or use the snackbar's house wording "Couldn’t save the room" (lib/forms.ts style), rather than adding new chrome.

Probe: pick Cool Grey, press Back within 200 ms, check that state_json is written. Then force an error and check that a later retry clears it.

kept.title: Any member can delete another member's room — the maker / Owner / Admin rule isn't applied
kept.where: Editor › Room options › Delete room (View as a Designer)
kept.evidence: lib/visualizer/policy.ts says ‘a design, a room's delete and a studio material are changed by whoever made them, an Owner or an Admin’, but deleteRoom() (actions.ts:158) only checks roomFor(); the menu item has no mayChange meta. Live: View as Sarah (Designer, not the maker) deleted Kitchen (created_by michelle) — deleted_at set (e-sarah-room-deleted.png).
kept.repro: Demo Studio › View as › Sarah; open Kevin Ng's design › Kitchen › Room options › Delete room.
kept.fix: deleteRoom(): `const block = designChangeBlock(got.viewer, got.r.createdBy ?? got.d.createdBy); if (block) return { error: block }`; return `mayDelete` per room from fetchVisualizerEditor and disable the menu item with the rule as meta (the design menu's pattern). Apply the same to restoreRoom.

verdict.reason:
The code confirms it. lib/visualizer/policy.ts says "a design, a room's delete and a studio material are changed by whoever made them, an Owner or an Admin". But deleteRoom() in app/visualizer/actions.ts (lines 158–162) only calls roomFor(). That checks the lead is visible to the viewer and the design isn't deleted, and nothing else: no designChangeBlock.

restoreRoom() (lines 163–167) is weaker still. It reads the row by id and clears deleted_at with no roomFor/canOpenLead check at all. So a restore call can bypass Who sees leads, not just the maker rule.

In the editor, the Delete room item (visualizer-editor.tsx:690) is gated only by readOnly. The design menu's Rename and Delete design items next to it carry `mayChange` meta and are disabled.

project_rooms has a created_by column (schema ~1193), but EditorRoom in lib/visualizer/queries.ts doesn't expose it or any per-room block.

The auditor's screenshot code-robustness/e-sarah-room-deleted.png exists. The live repro wasn't re-run, to avoid mutating the shared server.

Severity: major is fair. A written rule is broken, and Delete room is one press, though Undo exists and the delete is soft. For consistency, renameRoom and setRoomPhoto have no maker check either; the policy text only names delete, so leave those.
verdict.fix:
1. app/visualizer/actions.ts, deleteRoom: after roomFor, add `const block = designChangeBlock(got.viewer, got.r.createdBy ?? got.d.createdBy); if (block) return { error: block }`. Use the room's maker, falling back to the design's.
2. restoreRoom: go through roomFor, not the bare select. Apply the same block and return `{ ok: true } | Err`, so the Undo snackbar can say "Couldn't restore the room" when refused, per the house rule on refused optimistic writes. The load has to allow a deleted room: pass a flag so roomFor skips only the room's own deletedAt, which it doesn't check today anyway.
3. lib/visualizer/queries.ts: add `mayDelete: string | null` to EditorRoom, computed as `designChangeBlock(viewer, r.createdBy ?? d.createdBy)`.
4. components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:690: `disabled={!!room.mayDelete || readOnly}`, with the rule as `styles.menuMeta` in a `styles.menuRow`, exactly like the Delete design item at line 698.
Log it as a bug fix in REGISTER.md and add a probe step: View as Sarah shows Delete room disabled on a room Michelle made, and the server call is refused.

kept.title: Files uploads that aren't JPG/PNG/WebP (BMP, GIF, AVIF, HEIC) show a floor plan and are recorded as JPEG
kept.where: Lead › Files › Upload Files (REG-684) → grid, viewer and Open in AI Visualizer
kept.evidence: lead-files.tsx reads the picture with readFileAsDataUrl(file, 2000), which returns the raw data URL when the image is already ≤2000 px; uploadFile() only keeps jpeg/png/webp and otherwise writes thumb '/figma-assets/file-thumb-1.png' (a floor plan) with mime 'image/jpeg' and size 728064. Live: uploaded a 400×300 room.bmp → thumb /figma-assets/file-thumb-1.png, mime image/jpeg, 728064 B; the grid shows a floor plan for it (j-bmp-upload.png), and Open in AI Visualizer would make a room of that floor plan. The same stand-in shows on 20 seeded image files.
kept.repro: /leads/1f12cbd1-…/files › Upload Files › any small .bmp/.gif/.avif.
kept.fix: In lead-files.tsx always re-encode images through a canvas to JPEG (add a `force` option to readFileAsDataUrl or a sibling `toJpegDataUrl`), so every decodable image arrives as jpeg; in uploadFile() record the real `file.type`/size passed from the client, and when no picture could be read use a neutral image-file glyph (thumb null) instead of an unrelated floor plan. Hide ‘Open in AI Visualizer’ when the file has no real picture.

verdict.reason:
The code path is real. For an image at or under 2000 px, `readFileAsDataUrl` (lib/templates/files.ts) returns the raw FileReader data URL. So a small GIF or BMP arrives as `data:image/gif` or `data:image/bmp`. `uploadFile` (app/leads/files-actions.ts:69–71) only keeps jpeg/png/webp, so it falls back to the mock's stand-in: thumb `/figma-assets/file-thumb-1.png`, 728064 B, `image/jpeg`. Open in AI Visualizer then opens that stand-in. An image the browser can decode is thrown away for no reason, and that is a genuine bug.

The rest of the finding overreaches. The stand-in thumbnail, 711 KB size and `image/jpeg` mime are the deliberate REG-149 convention for bytes the prototype never stores. The attach-files modal, the Return Lead wizard, `createLead` files and the quote's files-actions all use it, and so do the 20 seeded image files. Redesigning that convention (a neutral glyph, the real mime and size, hiding the Visualizer entry) goes beyond this bug and would diverge from the mock's tile.

HEIC and AVIF are mostly moot. Chrome can't decode HEIC, but iOS Safari converts HEIC to JPEG on upload. AVIF over 2000 px is already re-encoded. So in practice this only affects small GIF and BMP files, which are rare for studio renders. Minor, not major.

I did not re-run it live: the code is unambiguous, and the auditor's live result matches it exactly.
verdict.fix:
In lib/templates/files.ts, give `readFileAsDataUrl` an optional third parameter, `opts?: { web?: boolean }`. When `web` is set and `file.type` is not jpeg, png or webp, go through the canvas even when `scale >= 1`. Output PNG for gif (it keeps transparency and the first frame) and JPEG 0.9 otherwise. If decoding fails (`img.onerror`, e.g. HEIC in Chrome), keep the current resolve.

In components/leads/files/lead-files.tsx:152, call `readFileAsDataUrl(file, 2000, { web: true })`. Every image the browser can decode then reaches `uploadFile` as jpeg or png, and the existing guard stores the real picture, size and mime.

Leave `uploadFile`'s REG-149 stand-in for undecodable files and the seeded stand-ins as they are, since that is the house convention for bytes the prototype doesn't store. Log the change as a bug fix under REG-684 in design-source/REGISTER.md.

kept.title: Several writes skip every check: restore, stop / renew / sent, material restore
kept.evidence: restoreDesigns(), restoreRoom(), restorePin() (no designFor / Who sees leads / maker rule), recordShareSent(), renewShareLink(), stopShareLink() (no designFor, so a link of a deleted design or of a lead the member may not see can be renewed or stopped), and restoreStudioMaterials() (no materialChangeBlock — a Designer can bring back a material an Owner deleted). Each is exported from a 'use server' module, so it is a public endpoint.
kept.repro: Code path; e.g. as a Designer call restoreStudioMaterials(['sm-calacatta']) after an Owner deletes it (the Deleted sheet offers Restore to everyone).
kept.fix: Route each through the same guards as its delete: designFor(design) + designChangeBlock for restoreDesigns/restoreRoom; versionOf()/pinFor() for restorePin; a `linkFor(id)` helper that loads the link's design with designFor(write) for the three share-link actions; materialChangeBlock + `deletedAt` check for restoreStudioMaterials. Return { error } and let the callers show it.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds on the server. In app/visualizer/actions.ts, restoreDesigns (line 114) clears deletedAt on any id it is given. It checks neither lead visibility (canOpenLead through designFor) nor the maker rule, even though deleteDesigns (104) needs designChangeBlock. So a Designer can undo an Owner's delete of a design the Designer did not make.

The other writes have the same gap:
- restoreRoom (163) and restorePin (386) load the row directly and skip roomFor and pinFor. Their deletes do go through those helpers.
- recordShareSent (328), renewShareLink (334) and stopShareLink (339) load the link by id and write to it with no designFor. A link on a deleted design, or on a lead the member cannot see, can still be renewed or stopped.
- restoreStudioMaterials (materials-actions.ts 68) skips materialChangeBlock, which deleteStudioMaterials and deleteStudioMaterialsForever both apply.

One detail in the repro is off. For materials, the UI already hides this: materials-view.tsx:39 passes restoreBlock={(t) => t.mayChange}, so the Deleted Materials sheet does not offer Restore to a Designer. There the gap is server-only.

The UI does expose it for designs:
- visualizer-home.tsx passes no restoreBlock to LibraryGallery, so Deleted Designs offers Restore on every row.
- The editor's deleted-design note (visualizer-editor.tsx:626) shows Restore without checking design.mayChange.

It stays minor because this is a prototype and the members are demo members. But it breaks the stated rule (policy.ts: "changed by whoever made them, an Owner or an Admin") and the house rule on server guards.

A side note, outside the finding: emptyDesignTrash/deleteDesignsForever also skips canOpenLead.
verdict.fix:
Put each restore behind the guard its delete already uses, and return { ok: true } | Err so callers can show the refusal as `Couldn't <do what>` (the UI sweep's rollback rule).

1. **restoreDesigns** (app/visualizer/actions.ts)
   - For each id, load the row and check lead visibility with canOpenLead(viewer, d.leadId) (write=false, because the design is deleted).
   - Require d.deletedAt.
   - Require !designChangeBlock(viewer, d.createdBy).
   - Restore only the ids that pass; with a single id, return the block as the error.

2. **restoreRoom**
   - Use roomFor(roomId) (visible, design not deleted) and require r.deletedAt.

3. **restorePin**
   - Use pinFor(pinId) and require p.deletedAt and authorRole === 'studio', the same as deletePin.

4. **Share links**
   - Add `async function linkFor(id)`: load the renderShareLinks row, then `designFor(s.designId)`, and return null if either is missing.
   - Route recordShareSent, renewShareLink and stopShareLink through it.
   - renew and stop return Err ('That design is gone.').

5. **restoreStudioMaterials** (app/company/materials-actions.ts)
   - Load the rows and keep those with m.deletedAt && !materialChangeBlock(viewer, m.uploadedBy), mirroring deleteStudioMaterialsForever.
   - With a single id, return the block as the error.

6. **UI parity**
   - visualizer-home.tsx: pass `restoreBlock={(t) => t.d.mayChange}` to LibraryGallery.
   - visualizer-editor.tsx:626: show the note's Restore only when data.design.mayChange is null; otherwise say DESIGN_RULE in the note, not in a native title.
   - visualizer-editor.tsx:454/495/715: the Undo handlers should snack on an error result.

No new UI; all wording comes from lib/visualizer/policy.ts.

kept.title: A room photo under the 10 MB promise fails with a 500 when it isn't downscaled
kept.where: Editor › Add room › upload (also Change photo, Files upload)
kept.evidence: okPhoto allows 10 MB, but readFileAsDataUrl returns the raw file when it is already ≤1600 px, so a 9.9 MB PNG becomes a ~13.2 MB data URL — over serverActions.bodySizeLimit '12mb' (next.config.ts) and cleanImage's 11,000,000. Live: noise.png (9,927,158 B, 1575 px) → server 500 and ‘Couldn’t read that photo — please try another’ (g-bigpng.png) — the helper text promised ‘up to 10 MB’.
kept.repro: Add room › upload a ≤1600 px PNG of ~9–10 MB.
kept.fix: Always re-encode room photos to JPEG q0.9 at ≤1600 px in the browser (never pass the original through), and if the result is still > 10 MB of base64 say so in the house words; keep bodySizeLimit ≥ 3 × the per-image cap for saveRender.

verdict.reason:
The code confirms it. `readFileAsDataUrl` in lib/templates/files.ts calls `resolve(url)` on the raw FileReader result whenever `scale >= 1`, so a photo that is already 1600 px or smaller is never re-encoded. `okPhoto` allows up to `PHOTO_MAX_BYTES` (10 MiB, in lib/visualizer/policy.ts). A 9.9 MB PNG therefore becomes a base64 data URL of about 13.2 MB. That is over `serverActions.bodySizeLimit: '12mb'` in next.config.ts and over `cleanImage`'s `< 11_000_000` in app/visualizer/actions.ts. The action call throws, and `addPhotoRoom` / `changePhoto` catch it as "Couldn’t read that photo — please try another". That contradicts the Add room helper ("up to 10 MB"), which is the copy in dialogs/add-room.tsx:28.

The auditor's screenshot g-bigpng.png shows only the dialog after the attempt, not the snackbar. I didn't rerun the upload because the code arithmetic is unambiguous.

Two more things point the same way:
- A PNG larger than 1600 px is re-encoded as PNG, not JPEG. A noisy or photographic PNG can still come out large.
- The Files path has a mismatched cap. `files-actions.ts` accepts pictures up to 14,000,000 chars at 2000 px, but the 12 MB body limit refuses them first.

Real studio photos are usually JPEGs over 1600 px and get downscaled, so this only hits large PNG or WebP files that are already small in pixels. That keeps it minor, not major.
verdict.fix:
1. lib/templates/files.ts: add an optional third parameter to `readFileAsDataUrl`, `opts?: { jpeg?: boolean }`. When `jpeg` is true, always draw to a canvas at scale `min(1, max / long side)` and return `toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.9)`, including when the scale is already 1. Other callers (logos, brand kit) keep today's behaviour and their PNG transparency.
2. components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx: pass `{ jpeg: true }` in `addPhotoRoom` and `changePhoto`. Room photos need no alpha channel.
3. After encoding, if the data URL is still over about 10.5 M chars, show the existing house words, "That photo is over 10 MB — try a smaller one", and don't call the action. It shouldn't happen at 1600 px JPEG q0.9.
4. Make the server-side error reachable: wrap the `addRoom` / `setRoomPhoto` call so that a thrown body-limit error maps to that same message rather than "Couldn’t read that photo".
5. components/leads/files/lead-files.tsx: use the same JPEG option for image pictures (max 2000) when the file is not PNG with transparency. Or lower files-actions.ts's `< 14_000_000` to sit under the 12 MB body limit, so the two caps agree.
6. Keep `bodySizeLimit` at '12mb' or above. Check `saveRender`'s multi-version payload against it: three 1600 px JPEGs at q0.9 is about 1.5 MB, well within it.

No new UI or copy is needed; this reuses the existing snackbar wording.

kept.title: Stored JSON is parsed without guards — one bad row takes down the editor or the client link
kept.evidence: Unguarded JSON.parse on project_rooms.state_json (queries.ts:144), render_annotations.comments_json (queries.ts:148 and 202, actions.ts:369, renders/actions.ts:95) and render_share_links.snapshot (queries.ts:149 and 187, renders/actions.ts:33). parseVariants checks only Array.isArray, so a variant without `applied` crashes descriptor() in versionsOf; parseDetection doesn't check `furniture` is an array before currentSampleReading filters it; saveRoomState slices detection.furniture without checking.
kept.repro: Code path: set a room's state_json to '{' (or a pin's comments_json to 'x') in a copy DB and open the design / its /renders link.
kept.fix: Add safe readers beside parseVariants: `parseJson<T>(raw, fallback)`, `parseComments`, `parseSnapshot` (fallback { versions: [] }), filter variants to those with an `applied` object and numeric id/n, and default detection.surfaces/furniture to []. Use them everywhere the raw JSON is read.

verdict.reason: The code observation holds. There are unguarded JSON.parse calls at lib/visualizer/queries.ts:144 (state_json), :148 and :202 (comments_json), and :149 and :187 (snapshot). There are more at app/visualizer/actions.ts:369 and app/renders/actions.ts:33 and :95. parseVariants and parseDetection only check the outer shape, and saveRoomState (actions.ts:183) calls s.detection.furniture.slice without checking it is an array. But every one of these columns is written only by the app itself through JSON.stringify. No import path, client form or migration writes raw JSON into them. A bad row can only come from someone editing the DB by hand, so no studio would ever meet this. On the demo data it is not reproducible, and I did not corrupt the shared :3012 DB to force it. The file's own helpers (parseVariants, parseOwn, parseDetection) already use try/catch, so this is a consistency gap, not a user-facing defect. The one input that does come from outside is saveRoomState's `s.detection`, a server-action payload from our own client. That is also only reachable through a crafted request. Real, but it is polish, not minor.
verdict.fix: In lib/visualizer/queries.ts, add one small reader next to parseVariants: `const parseJson = <T,>(raw: string | null | undefined, fallback: T): T => { try { return raw ? (JSON.parse(raw) as T) : fallback } catch { return fallback } }`. Export it and use it at queries.ts:144 (readPending(parseJson(r.stateJson, null))), :148/:202 (comments: filter parseJson(p.commentsJson, []) with Array.isArray), and :149/:187 (parseJson(s.snapshot, { versions: [] }), keeping `versions` only if it is an array). Use it too at app/renders/actions.ts:33/:95 and app/visualizer/actions.ts:369. Tighten parseVariants to keep only entries with an `applied` object and numeric id/n. In parseDetection, default `furniture` to [] when it is not an array. At actions.ts:183, use `Array.isArray(s.detection.furniture) ? … : []`. No UI change and no register entry are needed, beyond a bug-fix line if the owner wants it logged.

kept.title: Activity misses or misstates visualizer events
kept.evidence: Live Activity (k-activity.cjs): renders saved to Files read ‘You uploaded the file “Render - Living room - V3.jpg”’ and ‘You created the folder “Renders”’ as if uploaded by hand; deleting / restoring the design, deleting a room (Sarah's delete in e-roles) and deleting versions leave no line (no lead_events, REG-613); removed pins are still listed (vPins has no deleted_at filter); the stop line is hard-coded ‘You stopped sharing…’ (no revoked_by column); the inflated ‘opened (7 times)’.
kept.repro: Delete a room / a pin / the design, then open /leads/1f12cbd1-…/activity.
kept.fix: Log lead_events (design_deleted/restored, room_deleted, version_deleted, share_stopped/renewed with actor) from the actions via logLeadEvent and read them in the events branch; add `revoked_by` to render_share_links; filter vPins by deleted_at; in the Files branch word files whose thumb starts with /visualizer/img/v or that sit in Renders as ‘saved V3 of “Living room” from the AI Visualizer to Files’.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this from the code. I did not run anything live, because each point is plain in the source.

1. **Removed pins still show.** In `lib/leads/activity.ts` (lines 59–61), `vPins` loads every row of `renderAnnotations` for the lead's jobs. That table has a `deleted_at` column (`schema.ts:1280`) and `deletePin` / `restorePin` use it, but the query never filters on it. A pin removed in the editor keeps its line "X pinned a note on V2 of …".
2. **Deletes leave no trace.** `deleteRoom`, `deleteVersion` / `restoreVersion`, `deleteDesigns` / `restoreDesigns` / `deleteDesignsForever`, `stopShareLink` and `renewShareLink` in `app/visualizer/actions.ts` never call `logLeadEvent`. `LeadEventKind` in `lib/leads/events.ts:11-13` has no visualizer kinds at all. Worse, the jobs branch drops a job's line once all its variants carry `deletedAt`. So deleting versions removes the rendered line and adds nothing in its place. That breaks REG-613's rule that removals leave a trail.
3. **The stop line always says "You".** It is hard-coded: `text: 'You stopped sharing the renders' link.', actor: 'You'` (line 137). Nothing stores who stopped the link. Under View as (REG-667) Hui Min's stop would still read "You". A renewal also clears `revokedAt`, so a stop followed by a renew leaves no line at all.
4. **Saved renders read as manual uploads.** `saveVersionToFiles` → `ensureRendersFolder` + insert `leadFiles` (actions.ts:245-259) with `ownerId: me` and `thumb: renderUrl(...)`. The generic Files branch (line 247) then prints "You uploaded the file "Render - …"" and "You created the folder "Renders"".
5. **The view count is inflated.** `stampShareView` runs on every server render of `app/renders/[token]/page.tsx:26`, so refreshes and a studio member's own look at the link are counted. This one is the weakest point.

Severity minor is right: the Activity tab is wrong about the trail but no data is at risk. The auditor's fix is sound. I would make two changes to it:
- Record the stop / renew actor with a lead_events row instead of a new `revoked_by` column. That avoids a migration and matches how REG-613 handles actions that have no row of their own.
- Word the Files lines from the thumb prefix, not a folder-name heuristic. A folder named "Renders" can be made by hand.
verdict.fix:
1. **`lib/leads/activity.ts`, pins.** Add `isNull(renderAnnotations.deletedAt)` to the `vPins` query. Filter `vRooms` by `deletedAt` too, or keep "added the room" as history but point its link at the design with no `room=`.
2. **`lib/leads/events.ts`.** Extend `LeadEventKind` with `design_deleted | design_restored | room_deleted | room_restored | version_deleted | version_restored | share_stopped | share_renewed`. Carry `{ name, room, n }` in the detail.
3. **`app/visualizer/actions.ts`.** Call `logLeadEvent(db, leadId, kind, detail)` only when the design has a `leadId`, in:
   - `deleteDesigns` / `restoreDesigns` / `deleteDesignsForever`
   - `deleteRoom` / `restoreRoom`
   - `setVariantDeleted` (via `deleteVersion` / `restoreVersion`)
   - `stopShareLink` / `renewShareLink`
   The actor comes from the session automatically (REG-667). A restore should delete the matching `*_deleted` event, or log a restored line, the same way `undoStageMove` handles its rows.
4. **Read the new kinds in the events branch of `activity.ts`,** for example "{actor} removed V3 of "Living room" from the AI Visualizer." and "{actor} stopped sharing the renders' link." Then drop the hard-coded `viz-stop-${id}` line. Keep it only as a fallback for older rows with `revokedAt` and no matching event.
5. **Files branch in `activity.ts`.** When `f.thumb` starts with the render URL prefix (`renderUrl`, `/visualizer/img/`), word the line as "{actor} saved "Render - …" from the AI Visualizer to Files." Word the Renders folder the actor made in `ensureRendersFolder` the same way. Detect it from the folder's first child being a render, not from the folder's name.
6. **Optional, `app/renders/[token]/page.tsx` / `stampShareView`.** Skip the stamp when the request comes from the studio's own Preview, for example a `?preview=1` the visualizer's Open link adds. That stops members' looks from counting as client views.

No schema change is needed (`lead_events` is already generic), and no new UI. Add a repair rule only if demo designs need a backfilled deleted trail.

kept.title: Undo of ‘Stop sharing’ gives the link a fresh 7 days instead of putting it back
kept.where: Share dialog › Stop sharing › snackbar Undo
kept.evidence: The Undo calls renewShareLink(id) (visualizer-editor.tsx ShareDialog onStop), which sets expires_at = now + 7 days — a link that had 1 day left comes back with 7, and a link stopped after it expired comes back open.
kept.repro: Stop a link that expires tomorrow, press Undo, read expires_at.
kept.fix: Add `unstopShareLink(id)` that only clears revoked_at (keeping expires_at) and use it for the Undo; keep renewShareLink for the explicit Renew button.

verdict.reason:
The main claim holds, and I confirmed it in the code (I didn't need a live run for this). visualizer-editor.tsx:715 wires the Stop sharing snackbar's Undo to renewShareLink(id). In app/visualizer/actions.ts:334, renewShareLink sets expiresAt = Date.now() + SHARE_DAYS days and clears revokedAt. So Undo does not put the link back as it was: a link with 1 day left comes back with 7. That is a quiet extension of a client-facing link, and the snackbar says nothing about it.

The second half of the evidence ("a link stopped after it expired comes back open") is mostly not reachable. share-dialog.tsx:122 only shows the Stop sharing (link_off) button when the link is neither stopped nor expired; expired or stopped links show Renew instead. The only way to hit it is if the link happens to expire while the dialog or snackbar is still open, which is an edge case.

So the bug is real but narrower than reported: minor.
verdict.fix:
1. In app/visualizer/actions.ts, add `unstopShareLink(id)`. It loads the row the same way stopShareLink does, sets only `revokedAt: null` and keeps `expiresAt` as it is, then calls `touch(s.designId, s.leadId)`. If the link's date passed while it was stopped, it simply shows as Expired and the dialog offers Renew as usual; no special case needed.
2. In components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx:715, point the snackbar's onAction at `unstopShareLink(id)` instead of `renewShareLink`, followed by `router.refresh()`.
3. Keep renewShareLink for the explicit Renew button only (line 716).

No UI or copy change.

kept.title: Pin times on the client link are measured from the link's creation, so new pins always say ‘just now’
kept.evidence: render-share-page.tsx passes `now={data.createdAt}` to VersionCard → PinThread; when() computes now − createdAt, which is negative for every pin or reply made after the link was created → ‘just now’ for days.
kept.repro: Open /renders/17fe84ab2eca47, open pin 1 (made after the link).
kept.fix: Pass the server's render time (add `now: Date.now()` to PublicShare in fetchShare) instead of createdAt.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds, confirmed from the code and the scratch DB. I didn't need a screenshot, because the times are fully determined by the data.

- **Where the clock comes from.** `render-share-page.tsx` line 53 passes `now={data.createdAt}` (the link's creation time) to VersionCard, which hands it to PinThread at line 130.
- **How the time is worked out.** PinThread's `when(ms, now)` in `components/visualizer/editor/pin-card.tsx` computes `Math.round((now - ms)/60000)`. Any minutes value below 1, including a negative one, prints 'just now'.
- **The demo data.** Link 17fe84ab2eca47 was created at 1790182795. Pin 702a146d was made at 1790269675, about a day later, and its reply by Dane at 1790279995, a few hours after that. Both print 'just now' on the client page, and they will keep doing so however old they get.
- **The other direction is wrong too.** Pin 19ca1094 was made at 1786706100, about 40 days before the link. It prints '40 days ago' forever, instead of its real age growing over time.

The studio-side screens are correct. `fetchVisualizerHome`, the editor and Materials all pass a server `now: Date.now()`, so only the public share payload is missing it. Impact is minor: only the pin and reply times on the client link are wrong.
verdict.fix:
Take the time the page was rendered on the server instead of the link's creation time.
1. In `lib/visualizer/queries.ts`, add `now: number` to the `PublicShare` type and set `now: Date.now()` in `fetchShare`'s return. This is the same pattern `VisualizerEditorData` and `VisualizerHome` already use.
2. In `components/visualizer/share/render-share-page.tsx` line 53, pass `now={data.now}` instead of `data.createdAt`.
3. Optionally, in `pin-card.tsx`'s `when`, treat a negative difference as 'just now', which it already does. No other change is needed there.

Do not read `Date.now()` in render: the ESLint react-hooks rule forbids it, and the server-supplied value keeps SSR and hydration consistent.

kept.title: Fire-and-forget actions fail silently; the version Undo is optimistic with no rollback
kept.where: Editor: pin Resolve/Reopen, Undo of version / room / pin delete, Stop / Renew / sent, swatch remove
kept.evidence: `void setPinStatus(...).then(() => router.refresh())`, `void restoreVersion(...)`, `void restoreRoom(...)`, `void restorePin(...)`, `void stopShareLink/renewShareLink/recordShareSent(...)`, `await removeOwnSwatch(...)` — no catch, no snackbar; the version-delete Undo flips `deleted:false` locally before restoreVersion and never puts it back on failure (visualizer-editor.tsx removeVersion). The UI sweep's house rule (REG-656…660) is ‘an optimistic write puts the value back when the server refuses and the snackbar names what failed’. setPinStatus/restoreVersion return void so a refusal can't even be seen.
kept.repro: Code path (e.g. restore a version while the design is deleted in another tab).
kept.fix: Make those actions return `{ ok } | { error }`; wrap each call site in the house pattern: await, on error roll back the local change and snack `Couldn’t <do what>`; only then router.refresh().

verdict.reason:
The code shows exactly what the auditor describes. In app/visualizer/actions.ts, `restoreVersion` (line 215), `restoreRoom` (163), `restorePin` (386), `setPinStatus` (374), `recordShareSent`, `renewShareLink` and `stopShareLink` (328–343), and `removeOwnSwatch` (228) all return `Promise<void>` and quietly `return` when the record is gone. `restoreVersion` also ignores the null from `setVariantDeleted`. So the caller has no way to tell a refusal from a success.

The call sites in components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx are all fire-and-forget with no catch and no snackbar:
- line 447: the version Undo flips `deleted:false` locally, then `void restoreVersion(...).then(router.refresh)`
- lines 454 and 495: the room and pin Undo
- line 601: `setPinStatus`
- lines 714–716: sent / Stop / Renew. Stop shows its "Stopped sharing" snackbar only after the call succeeds; on a network error nothing is shown at all.
- line 396: `await removeOwnSwatch(...)` has no try, so a throw skips the snackbar and leaves an unhandled rejection. Its Undo (`void saveOwnSwatch(...)`) also ignores the `{error}` that `saveOwnSwatch` does return.

This breaks the UI sweep's house rule (REG-656…660: roll back when the server refuses and name what failed). The same file already uses that pattern elsewhere, e.g. line 445 for `deleteVersion` and the `Couldn’t …` snackbars at 164 and 351–372, so the drift is local.

In practice the local version flip mostly corrects itself when `router.refresh()` runs after a null return. It stays wrong only when the call rejects (the network drops, or the server throws), and then nobody is told. The trigger is rare in a demo (the design deleted in another tab, or a dropped connection), so minor is the right severity.
verdict.fix:
1. app/visualizer/actions.ts: make `restoreVersion`, `restoreRoom`, `restorePin`, `setPinStatus`, `stopShareLink`, `renewShareLink`, `recordShareSent` and `removeOwnSwatch` return `Promise<{ ok: true } | Err>`. Use the existing `Err` shape and the existing wording: 'That version is gone.', 'That room is gone.', 'That pin is gone.', 'That link is gone.', 'That design is gone.' `restoreVersion` maps `setVariantDeleted`'s null to an error, the way `deleteVersion` already does.

2. components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx: add one small local helper, e.g. `run(p, what, undo?)`. It awaits `p.catch(() => ({ error: `Couldn’t ${what} — please try again` }))`, runs `undo` and snacks `r.error` when the result is an error, and calls `router.refresh()` otherwise. Route every call site through it:
   - Version Undo (line 447): keep the optimistic `deleted:false`; the rollback sets `deleted:true` again, and the message is 'Couldn’t bring back V{n}'.
   - Room Undo (454): on failure, clear the pick so it goes back to the previous room.
   - Pin Undo (495) and `setPinStatus` (601): 'Couldn’t reopen/resolve the pin'.
   - Stop / Renew / sent (714–716): show the success snackbar only on `ok`.
   - `removeOwn` (396): show the "removed · Undo" snackbar only on `ok`. Its Undo checks `saveOwnSwatch`'s `{error}` too.

No new UI: use the existing `snack` and the house message wording (`lib/forms.ts` style). Afterwards, extend the ai-visualizer probe with one forced-failure case, e.g. restoring a version after deleting its design in a second context.

kept.title: A Cancel pressed while the render is being kept burns a V number and the next labels drift from the server's
kept.where: Editor › Generate › Cancel during ‘Keeping the version’
kept.evidence: generate(): if the token changed after saveRender returned, it soft-deletes the saved variants (still consuming their n) yet says ‘Stopped — nothing was kept’; the next Generate labels its versions `top + i + 1` from the client's list (which never saw the burned job) while saveRender numbered them from the DB, so the strip/snackbar can say V4 for what the server stored as V5 until the refresh lands.
kept.repro: Code path; Cancel is visible during the save step.
kept.fix: Have saveRender return each variant's `n` and use it for `made`; hide Cancel (or make it a no-op) once the save has started, or, if kept, say ‘Stopped — V5 was removed’. Optionally hard-delete a job cancelled before anyone saw it so its numbers are free.

verdict.reason:
The code path is as described. In `generate()` (visualizer-editor.tsx lines 150–180), `saveRender` numbers the variants from the DB: in actions.ts line 197 it takes the highest `n` over the room's jobs, deleted ones included. It then returns only `{ jobId, keys }`, with no `n`.

If the run token changed while that save was in flight, the client fire-and-forgets `deleteVersion` for each saved variant. That is a soft delete, so each number "stays taken", as the comment at actions.ts line 213 says. It returns without a refresh. `cancelRun` has already shown "Stopped — nothing was kept".

The Stage's Cancel stays live for the whole run, including the last step, "Keeping the version". Nothing in `stage.tsx` hides it on that step.

The next Generate labels its versions `top + i + 1` from the client's `versions` state (line 167), which never received the cancelled job. So the strip label and the snackbar ("V4 is ready") can say V4 while the server stored V5.

The drift is short-lived. `router.refresh()` right after reseeds `useEditorState` from `data.versions`, which carries the deleted versions' real numbers. After that the strip corrects itself to V5, but the snackbar has already said V4. The same drift happens with no cancel at all when another tab or teammate generates on the same room. So the client should read the number from the server, not work it out.

Severity is minor: the timing window is narrow, and it only corrupts a label and one snackbar, never stored data.
verdict.fix:
1. `app/visualizer/actions.ts` `saveRender`: return the numbers it gave, `{ jobId, keys, ns: variants.map((v) => v.n) }`, and widen the return type to match.

2. `components/visualizer/editor/visualizer-editor.tsx` `generate()`: build `made` from `saved.ns[i]` for both `n` and the `V${n}` label. Drop the `top` computation. Then the strip and the snackbar always match the server, including when another tab generates at the same time.

3. Once the save has started, Cancel should not be offered. Set a `saving` flag on `running` when the step moves to the last one, "Keeping the version". Have `stage.tsx` leave out the Cancel button while `running.saving` is set. The house rule is to answer only what the user can act on, and a save already under way can't be taken back cleanly.

Keep the existing soft-delete branch only as a safety net for a token that changes for other reasons, such as a room switch. When it runs, follow the deletes with `router.refresh()` so the client's list learns about the removed numbers.

No hard delete is needed. Stable numbers that are never reused are the documented rule (actions.ts line 213).

kept.title: Unbounded in-browser image caches grow with every version viewed
kept.evidence: imgCache (a module-level Map, never evicted) holds a decoded RGBA buffer per URL — ~7.7 MB for a 1600×1200 photo — keyed by the full data URL string; every version shown, every highlight (regionOverlay), light preview and swatch adds one, and loadImg clones the whole buffer on each hit. The editor's `local` map keeps every generated data URL (~150 KB each, 3 per high-variant run) for the life of the page. It survives client navigations because it is module state.
kept.repro: Code path; generate and flip through a dozen versions, watch the tab's memory.
kept.fix: Make imgCache an LRU (e.g. 8 entries) keyed by a short hash / the version key rather than the data URL; drop `local[key]` once router.refresh brings the server address for that key; avoid cloning when the caller only reads (regionOverlay/previewLight).

verdict.reason:
The code matches the claim, but the auditor overstates the cost. `imgCache` in lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts:24 is a module-level Map with no eviction. Its keys are full URL strings, which are data URLs for generated versions and swatches. It holds one decoded RGBA buffer per URL, and every hit returns a `cloneImg` copy (line 27). In the editor, `local` (visualizer-editor.tsx:104/172) keeps every generated data URL for the life of the page. `urlOf` keeps preferring it even after `router.refresh()` brings the server's URL, so later loadImg calls for that version stay keyed by the data URL.

What is overstated:
(1) Size. The sample rooms are 900×603, about 2.2 MB per decoded entry, not 7.7 MB. Only a large uploaded photo gets near the auditor's figure.
(2) Just looking at a version does not decode it. An entry is added only when you generate from a version, highlight regions on it (`regionOverlay`), preview light on it (`previewLight`), read a swatch, or open the moodboard.
(3) `maskCache` is already bounded (it is cleared past 120 entries, line 69).

A realistic demo session (a dozen versions, highlighted and previewed) holds a few tens of MB and does not slow anything down that a studio would feel. It only matters in a very long session with large uploads. This is real hygiene, but polish, not minor.
verdict.fix:
In lib/visualizer/engine/run.ts, make `imgCache` a small LRU: cap it at about 12 entries, and on a hit delete and re-set the entry to refresh its order. Key it by a short key rather than the full string, for example `url.length > 200 ? url.length + ':' + url.slice(-120) : url`, the same idea `regionOf` already uses. Split out an internal `readImg(url)` that returns the cached Img without cloning. Use it in `regionOverlay` and `extractPalette`/`dominantColour` callers, which only read. Keep `loadImg` (which clones) for passes that mutate (`previewLight`'s grade, the render passes).

Leave the editor's `local` map alone, or at most prune entries for versions that were deleted or never saved. It is what keeps a new version on screen while the refresh round-trip runs, and each entry is only about 150 KB of string. No UI change and no REGISTER entry are needed beyond a bug-fix line if it is built.

kept.title: Every gallery, editor and Activity load reads every render's base64 out of variants_json
kept.evidence: Pictures live inside render_jobs.variants_json (≈146 KB per kitchen variant in the scratch DB after three Generates); the gallery selects variants_json for ALL jobs of ALL designs just to count versions and pick covers, the editor page runs fetchVisualizerEditor twice per request (generateMetadata + page), and Activity parses them again.
kept.repro: Code path; sqlite3 … 'select length(variants_json) from render_jobs' after a few Generates.
kept.fix: Store each variant's picture in its own table (render_images(job_id, variant_id, data), like lead_file_images) and keep variants_json small; make generateMetadata read only the design/lead name.

verdict.reason:
The code path is real. fetchVisualizerHome selects renderJobs.variantsJson for every job in the studio (lib/visualizer/queries.ts:56) just to count versions and pick covers. The editor route calls fetchVisualizerEditor twice per request, once in generateMetadata and once in the page, and neither call is wrapped in React cache(). fetchLeadActivity parses variantsJson twice (lib/leads/activity.ts:124 and :128). The /visualizer/img/v route also parses a whole job's JSON to serve one variant. Sizes match the finding: the scratch DB holds 9 jobs, about 443 KB, with a 147 KB maximum, and local.db holds 2 jobs at about 324 KB.

The finding overstates the impact, though. The base64 never reaches the browser: versionsOf, roomImage and variantImage turn stored data URLs into /visualizer/img/... addresses, and the gallery HTML on :3020 contains 0 data:image strings. The heavy work is server-side only, a local SQLite read plus JSON.parse. Measured on :3020, the gallery answers in about 9–11 ms and the editor in about 11–25 ms (a 75 KB page). A studio would not notice this at demo scale. It becomes a cost only with hundreds of renders (about 150 KB each), so this is polish or scale hygiene, not a minor bug. The one cheap, clearly worthwhile part is the duplicate full load in generateMetadata.
verdict.fix:
1. The cheap fix to apply now: in app/(editor)/visualizer/[designId]/page.tsx, make generateMetadata read only the name. Add a small visualizerTitle(designId) helper in lib/visualizer/queries.ts that selects visualizerDesigns.name, leadId and the lead's name and nothing else. Alternatively, wrap fetchVisualizerEditor in React `cache()` so the metadata and the page share one load per request.
2. Optional, for scale: move the pictures out of variants_json. Add a render_images(job_id, variant_id, data) table as an additive migration, mirroring lead_file_images. Generate and the other writers in app/visualizer/actions.ts store the data URL there and keep imageUrl as the /visualizer/img/v/{job}/{variant} address inside variants_json. Change the img route to read render_images by key. Add a repair rule that moves existing data URLs, and add the table to the baseline lists (lib/db/baseline.ts, scripts/snapshot-baseline.ts). With that, the gallery, the editor and Activity parse a few hundred bytes per job.
Nothing changes on the client; the page payload is already addresses only.

kept.title: New designs ignore the open folder; a failed sample start leaves an empty design
kept.where: /visualizer › New ▾ (Blank design, From a sample room…, For a lead…)
kept.evidence: createDesign's doc says ‘in the folder open in the gallery’ but blank()/fromSample() call createDesign({}) with no folderId; fromSample() runs createDesign then addRoom as two actions, so an addRoom refusal leaves an empty ‘Sample · …’ design behind (the owner's :3000 already has a stray ‘Sample · Kitchen sketch’); forLead() awaits openLeadDesign with no catch (unhandled rejection on a network error).
kept.repro: Open a folder in the gallery › New › Blank design → it lands at the root.
kept.fix: Pass the gallery's current folder id into blank()/fromSample(); give createDesign an optional `sampleKey/asSketch` so the room is added in the same action (one transaction); wrap forLead in the house try/snackbar.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed all three claims by reading the code. I did not run anything live, because each one is plain from the source.

1. **New designs ignore the open folder.** `createDesign` (app/visualizer/actions.ts:57-62) says it creates the design "in the folder open in the gallery" and accepts `folderId`. But `blank()` calls `createDesign({})` (visualizer-home.tsx:53) and `fromSample()` calls `createDesign({ name })` (:66), so neither passes a folder id. The open folder is only in LibraryGallery's `?folder=` URL param (library-gallery.tsx:160-164), and VisualizerHome never reads it. A design started from inside a folder therefore always lands at the top level.

2. **A failed sample start leaves an empty design.** `fromSample()` makes two separate server calls, `createDesign` then `addRoom`. If `addRoom` refuses (it returns `{error}` when `designFor` fails or the image is bad) or the network fails in between, the "Sample · …" design is already written and has no room. The code shows a snackbar and returns without removing it. The stray "Sample · Kitchen sketch" is consistent with this, though it could also have come from an ordinary start that was abandoned.

3. **`forLead()` has no error handling.** It awaits `openLeadDesign` with no try/catch (:55-59), so a thrown server action becomes an unhandled rejection and the user gets no snackbar. It also skips the `busy` guard that `blank()` has, so a double pick can fire twice (harmless, because `openLeadDesign` is idempotent).

Severity stays minor. Nothing is lost and the design can be moved afterwards, but a studio would notice designs ending up at the top level while they are working inside a folder.
verdict.fix:
1. **Folder.** In visualizer-home.tsx, read `useSearchParams().get('folder')` the same way LibraryGallery does. Use `liveFolder(data.folders, …)` so a stale id falls back to the top level. Pass the result as `folderId` from both `blank()` and `fromSample()`. On the server, `createDesign` should check that `folderId` is a live `library_folders` row in the 'visualizer' library, and store null otherwise. It currently trusts the client.

2. **One action for sample starts.** Extend `createDesign`'s input to `{ name?, folderId?, sample?: { key, asSketch } }`. Check the sample with `sampleByKey` before inserting anything, then insert the design and its first room together in one `db.transaction`. To do that, factor the room-insert body of `addRoom` into a shared helper that both actions call. `fromSample()` then makes a single call and opens the design only when it succeeds.

3. **Lead picks.** Put `forLead()` behind the same `busy` guard and try/catch/snackbar as `blank()`, with the message "Couldn’t open the lead’s design — please try again". Or route it through the existing `useRun()` `run('open the design', …)` that the sample tiles already use.

This adds no new UI or copy beyond the house `Couldn’t …` snackbar pattern from lib/forms.ts / REG-656…660.

kept.title: A lead can get two lead designs (no unique constraint)
kept.where: openLeadDesign (quick link, Files › Open in AI Visualizer, gallery For a lead…)
kept.evidence: openLeadDesign selects then inserts; visualizer_designs has only a plain index on lead_id (drizzle/0053_ai_visualizer.sql). Two tabs / two members opening a lead's visualizer for the first time at once insert two kind='lead' rows; leadDesignId then picks either.
kept.repro: Code path (concurrent first opens).
kept.fix: Add a partial unique index on visualizer_designs(lead_id) WHERE kind='lead' (additive migration) and use insert … on conflict do nothing then re-select.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this in the code; I didn't run it live, since a race between two first opens can't be reproduced reliably with read-only checks. In app/visualizer/actions.ts, openLeadDesign (lines 72–80) looks for a kind='lead' row for the lead and inserts one if none is found, with nothing guarding the gap between the two steps. drizzle/0053_ai_visualizer.sql:122 and lib/db/schema.ts:1174 give visualizer_designs only a plain index on lead_id (visualizer_designs_lead_idx), with no uniqueness. If two tabs or two members open a lead's visualizer for the first time at the same moment, both can insert, and the lead ends up with two lead designs. After that, openLeadDesign and leadDesignId (lib/visualizer/queries.ts:159) each take whichever row the database returns first. The two can pick different rows, so rooms and renders get split between two designs, and the gallery shows two cards for one lead. It only happens on a truly simultaneous first open, which is rare in a demo, so polish is the right severity.
verdict.fix:
1. Add an additive migration, drizzle/0055: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX visualizer_designs_lead_one_idx ON visualizer_designs (lead_id) WHERE kind = 'lead';`. Mirror it in lib/db/schema.ts with `uniqueIndex('visualizer_designs_lead_one_idx').on(t.leadId).where(sql\`kind = 'lead'\`)` and keep the existing plain index. Generate it with `npm run db:generate`, then run db:migrate.
2. In openLeadDesign (app/visualizer/actions.ts), change the insert to `.onConflictDoNothing()`. Then select the lead's kind='lead' row again and return its id, so the tab that loses the race opens the design the winner created. Call revalidatePath only when this call's own insert went in.
3. Before the index is created, repair-demo-data.ts needs a new rule that merges any duplicate kind='lead' rows. Keep the oldest row, move its project_rooms, render jobs and share links over by design_id, and delete the extras; otherwise the migration fails on a database that already has duplicates. Run it, then `npm run db:baseline`.
There is no UI change.
